signals.title: OpenCode binary fails to run natively on Termux / Android aarch64 (wrong interpreter + non‑PIE executable)
signals.text: ### Description **Environment** - Device: Android smartphone/tablet, HUAWEI PaperMate 11.5 - OS: Android (5.0+), HarmionyOS 4.2.0 - Terminal: Termux - Arch: `aarch64` (`uname -m` → `aarch64`) - Install method: official install script (`curl ... | sh`, binary ends up in `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`) **Summary** After installing OpenCode on Termux using the official script, the Linux/aarch64 `opencode` binary does not start as a native Android executable. 1) The binary requests a dynamic linker at `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`, which does not exist on Android/Termux. 2) After manually changing the interpreter to the correct Android linker, the binary fails with `Android 5.0 and later only support position-independent executables (-fPIE)`, which means it was not compiled as PIE and cannot be run on modern Android at all. **Steps to reproduce** 1. Install Termux from F‑Droid / Play Store. 2. Update packages and install diagnostic tools: ```bash pkg update -y pkg install -y file binutils patchelf ``` 3. Install OpenCode using the official method, for example: ```bash curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install.sh | sh ``` 4. Try to run the binary: ```bash /data/data/com.termux/files/home/.opencode/bin/opencode ``` 5. Observe the shell error: ```bash bash: /data/data/com.termux/files/home/.opencode/bin/opencode: cannot execute: required file not found ``` **Diagnostics** 1. Check the file type: ```bash file /data/data/com.termux/files/home/.opencode/bin/opencode ``` The output shows a 64‑bit ELF for `aarch64`, with the program interpreter set to `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1` (standard on many Linux distros, but not on Android/Termux). 2. On Termux/Android, `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1` does not exist. To find the correct interpreter, I inspected a working Termux binary (`bash`): ```bash readelf -l "$(which bash)" | grep "Requesting program interpreter" ``` This reports `/system/bin/linker64` as the requested program interpreter. 3. I tried to “fix” the `opencode` binary by changing its interpreter: ```bash patchelf --set-interpreter /system/bin/linker64 \ /data/data/com.termux/files/home/.opencode/bin/opencode ``` This successfully changes the interpreter to the Android linker used by Termux. 4. Running `opencode` again: ```bash /data/data/com.termux/files/home/.opencode/bin/opencode ``` Now I get a different error: ```text "/data/data/com.termux/files/home/.opencode/bin/opencode": error: Android 5.0 and later only support position-independent executables (-fPIE). ``` This is the typical Android error when the ELF binary is not built as PIE. Since Android 5.0, only position‑independent executables (built with `-fPIE` / `-pie`) are allowed to run. **What I expected** I expected the official Linux/aarch64 OpenCode binary to either: - run natively under Termux on Android (with a correct interpreter and PIE build), or - clearly be documented as *not* supported for native Termux/Android, with guidance to use a different build or a proot‑based Linux environment instead. **What actually happens** - With the unmodified binary: `bash: cannot execute: required file not found` due to the non‑existent `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`. - After setting the interpreter to `/system/bin/linker64`: the binary exits with `Android 5.0 and later only support position-independent executables (-fPIE)` and cannot be started at all. - This cannot be fixed on the user side by patching the existing ELF; it requires recompiling OpenCode with the correct flags and target. **Analysis / root cause** - The binary shipped by the installer appears to be a regular Linux ELF for `aarch64` with glibc, requesting `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1` as interpreter. - Termux runs on Android, using `/system/bin/linker64` and a different ABI, and Android ≥ 5.0 rejects non‑PIE executables. - Even after manually fixing the interpreter path, the OpenCode binary still cannot run, because it does not satisfy Android’s requirement for position‑independent executables. **Why this deserves a dedicated fix** - There are already reports about OpenCode issues on Termux (usually when running inside a proot‑distro like Ubuntu/Debian, with freezes, TUI issues, crashes on the second run, etc.), but those are runtime problems inside a Linux userland. - In this case, the problem is more fundamental: the official Linux/aarch64 binary is simply incompatible with the native Android ABI (wrong interpreter and non‑PIE), so it is impossible to run it directly in Termux without a full Linux environment in proot. **Suggested fix** 1. Provide an official Android/Termux build for `aarch64` that: - is built as PIE (`-fPIE` / `-pie`), - uses the correct interpreter for Android (for example `/system/bin/linker64`, depending on the target ABI), - is tested in a real Termux environment, not only on standard Linux. 2. Alternatively (until such a build exists), update the documentation and installer to: - explicitly state that the current Linux/aarch64 binary is not intended to run natively on Termux/Android, - recommend using OpenCode via a proot‑distro (Ubuntu/Debian) or a remote Linux server when working from Android. **Additional info** - I can attach exact outputs of `file`, `readelf -l`, and `patchelf --print-interpreter` if needed. - I’m happy to test any experimental Android/Termux builds (aarch64) and provide feedback. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: 建议增加滚动条和指令预览
signals.text: 🎯 **问题描述** 当使用 OpenCode 处理复杂任务时，Terminal User Interface (TUI) 会显示大量的交互信息。在 Windows PowerShell 环境下，缺少滚动条和快速导航功能，导致： 1. **信息过长时无法快速定位**：历史对话记录堆积，难以找到特定位置 2. **指令预览缺失**：无法快速浏览和重用之前的命令 3. **导航效率低**：只能通过 PageUp/PageDown 逐页翻阅 4. **用户体验差**：长时间使用时容易迷失在大量信息中 🛠️ **建议方案** --- 注：方案由opencode自动生成。 **方案 A: 滚动条 + 指令历史面板** ┌─ OpenCode v1.1.34 ── GPT-5 Nano ─────────────────┐ │ │ │ 对话区域 │ │ > 用户: 解释这段代码 │ │ 🤖 AI: 这是一个函数... │ │ │ │ 滚动条 ██████████░░░░░░░░░░ 60% │ │ │ │ 指令历史侧边栏 │ │ !ls -la │ │ /models │ │ help │ │ /export │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ #### **方案 B: 命令模式 + 快速跳转** - 新增快捷键 `Ctrl+R` 打开命令历史搜索 - 支持 `Ctrl+G <行号>` 快速跳转到指定位置 - `Ctrl+H` 切换显示/隐藏历史对话 #### **方案 C: 分屏模式** - `Ctrl+S` 切换分屏布局 - 左侧：当前对话 - 右侧：指令历史和快速操作面板 ### 🎮 **具体实现建议** #### **快捷键设计:** - `Ctrl+R`: 打开命令历史搜索 - `Ctrl+G`: 行号跳转 - `Ctrl+H`: 历史对话切换 - `Ctrl+J/K`: 历史记录上下导航 - `F3`: 搜索下一个 - `Shift+F3`: 搜索上一个 #### **UI改进:** 1. **右侧滚动条**: 实时显示当前位置 2. **迷你地图**: 显示对话结构概览 3. **指令高亮**: 命令和响应用不同颜色区分 4. **状态栏**: 显示当前行数/总行数 #### **PowerShell特定优化:** - 兼容 Windows Console Host - 适配 PowerShell 5.1+ 字符渲染 - 支持 Windows Terminal 的现代化特性 ### 🔄 **替代方案考虑** 1. **渐进式增强**: 先实现滚动条，再添加指令预览 2. **配置驱动**: 通过 config.json 让用户自定义快捷键 3. **插件化**: 将导航功能做成可选插件 ### 💡 **用户场景** #### **场景1: 代码审查** 用户在审查长代码对话时，需要快速回到某个特定代码段的讨论位置。 #### **场景2: 调试会话** 在长时间的调试过程中，需要回顾之前的错误信息和解决方案。 #### **场景3: 学习回顾** 学习新概念时，想要快速翻到关键解释部分重新理解。 ### 🔧 **技术实现思路** ```javascript // 伪代码示例 class TUIEnhancer { constructor() { this.scrollbar = new Scrollbar() this.commandHistory = new CommandHistory() this.searchEngine = new SearchEngine() } enableScrolling() { // 实现平滑滚动 } showCommandPreview() { // 显示指令历史侧边栏 } quickJump(lineNumber) { // 快速跳转到指定行 } } 📊 优先级评估 - 影响用户: 所有 Windows PowerShell 用户 - 使用频率: 每次使用都会受益 - 实现复杂度: 中等 - 向后兼容: 完全兼容现有功能 🌟 相关Issue - 搜索现有Issue，避免重复 - 参考: 如果有类似的UI改进请求 📝 环境信息 - OS: Windows PowerShell 5.1.22621.4391 - OpenCode版本: 1.1.34 - 模型: opencode/gpt-5-nano - 终端: Windows Console Host 🎯 预期效果 1. 导航效率提升 50%+ 2. 减少信息查找时间 3. 提升长时间使用的舒适度 4. 增强专业开发者体验

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Auto-continue when model hits output token limit (finish_reason: "length")
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request When using models with large context windows (e.g., Claude Opus 4.6 with 1 million input context), the input context is rarely exhausted. However, the per-response output token cap (`OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX`, default 32K) frequently causes the model to stop mid-task with `finish_reason: "length"`. The user must then manually type "continue" to resume — which breaks the autonomous agent workflow. **Current behavior:** The loop in `prompt.ts` exits when `finish_reason` is anything other than `"tool-calls"` or `"unknown"`: ```typescript if ( lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls", "unknown"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id ) { break } ``` When finish_reason is "length", the loop breaks and waits for user input. Requested behavior: When finish_reason is "length", it would be nice for OpenCode to automatically inject a synthetic "continue" user message and re-enter the loop — the same pattern already used for subtask summaries. The model's output was truncated, not intentionally finished, so the loop should continue. Suggested implementation 1. Add "length" to the continuation conditions in prompt.ts, or handle it separately 2. When finish_reason === "length" is detected, inject a synthetic user message (e.g., "Continue from where you left off.") and continue the loop instead of breaking 3. The infrastructure for synthetic user messages already exists (used for subtask command summaries) 4. Consider adding a config option (compaction.auto_continue or similar) to make this opt-in/out - The MessageV2.OutputLengthError type is already defined in message-v2.ts but appears unused - The plugin system cannot solve this, as there is no hook between the finish reason being set and the loop exit decision
signals.author: stephenstubbs

signals.title: [FEATURE]:Support inline "ghost text" code completion (like Cursor/Copilot)
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Currently, OpenCode works excellently as a chat/agent interface in the terminal or sidebar. However, it lacks inline automatic code completion (often called "ghost text"). When I am typing code in my editor, I have to stop, switch context to ask OpenCode for help, and then copy-paste the result. This breaks my flow compared to AI-native editors like Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or Codeium, where suggestions appear automatically as grayed-out text while typing. I would love to see a feature where OpenCode can provide real-time inline completions: 1. As I type code, OpenCode analyzes the current context (cursor position, surrounding code). 2. It suggests the next few lines or the rest of the current line as gray "ghost text" directly in the editor. 3. I can press Tab to accept the suggestion or continue typing to ignore it.

signals.title: [FEATURE] Pre/post API call hooks in Provider interface for secret redaction and exfiltration prevention
signals.text: ## Problem When using OpenCode, all code, file contents, command outputs, and user prompts are sent to external LLM API servers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, etc.). This includes secrets, project names, company names, and NDA-protected material. Organizations need the ability to **prevent sensitive data from leaving the machine** — whether to the LLM provider or to attackers via prompt injection — and un-redact AI responses before they reach local tools. ### Current plugin limitations The existing plugin system provides `tool.execute.before` which intercepts tool calls. But this operates at the **tool level**, not the **API level**. There is no way to: - Redact file contents read by tools before they're sent in the API request - Redact user prompts before they reach the LLM provider - Un-redact model responses before tool calls execute - Cover all providers uniformly (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, etc.) ## Proposed Solution Add two hook points in the `Provider` interface, firing before/after the actual API call. ### Where in the code The interception point already exists in `internal/llm/provider/provider.go`: ```go func (p *baseProvider[C]) SendMessages(ctx context.Context, messages []message.Message, tools []tools.BaseTool) (*ProviderResponse, error) { messages = p.cleanMessages(messages) // ← NEW: fire PreApiCall hooks here, allow modifying messages return p.client.send(ctx, messages, tools) // ← NEW: fire PostApiCall hooks here, allow modifying response } func (p *baseProvider[C]) StreamResponse(ctx context.Context, messages []message.Message, tools []tools.BaseTool) <-chan ProviderEvent { messages = p.cleanMessages(messages) // ← NEW: fire PreApiCall hooks here, allow modifying messages return p.client.stream(ctx, messages, tools) // ← NEW: fire PostApiCall hooks on each event, allow modifying content } ``` ### Implementation approach: Go decorator ```go type RedactingProvider struct { inner Provider redactor Redactor // interface with Redact(text) and Unredact(text) } func (r *RedactingProvider) SendMessages(ctx context.Context, messages []message.Message, tools []tools.BaseTool) (*ProviderResponse, error) { redactedMessages := r.redactMessages(messages) response, err := r.inner.SendMessages(ctx, redactedMessages, tools) if err != nil { return nil, err } r.unredactResponse(response) return response, nil } ``` This: - Works with **all providers** (wraps the `Provider` interface) - Requires **minimal code changes** (wrap at creation time) - Is **testable** (mock the `Redactor` interface) - Is **opt-in** (only activates when configured) ### Alternative: Plugin hooks If a Go-level change is not preferred, expose as plugin events: ```typescript api.on("api.request.before", (event) => { return { messages: redactMessages(event.messages) }; }); api.on("api.response.after", (event) => { return { response: unredactResponse(event.response) }; }); ``` ## End-to-end flow ``` 1. User: "Check config.py for the AcmeCorp API key" 2. Agent reads file → gets content with real secret 3. Agent builds messages array with tool_result containing the secret 4. ✨ PreApiCall fires → redacts secret → placeholder token 5. Redacted messages sent to LLM provider — secret never leaves machine 6. LLM responds using placeholder token 7. ✨ PostApiCall fires → un-redacts token → real value 8. Agent processes response with real values 9. Tool calls execute with real content ``` ## Defense against prompt injection exfiltration Beyond protecting data sent to the LLM provider, API-level hooks defend against **prompt injection attacks** that trick the model into exfiltrating secrets via tool calls. Real-world attack vectors (see [gricha/dangerous-skills](https://github.com/gricha/dangerous-skills)): | Attack | Pwn Rate | Vector | |--------|----------|--------| | Trojan helper script | 100% | Payload buried in legitimate bash code | | Memory poisoning | 96% | Persistent backdoor in global config, survives skill removal | | Hook exploitation | 89% | Skill-defined hooks fire shell commands — model never knows | | Test file RCE | 60% | `conftest.py` auto-imported by pytest | | Symlink exfiltration | 54% | "Example" file is symlink to `~/.ssh/id_rsa` | | Supply chain | 36% | npm `postinstall` hook | | Image injection | 30% | Hidden instructions in PNG metadata | With PreApiCall, a redaction tool scans the **entire outgoing request** and blocks secrets before they reach any server. With PostApiCall, suspicious tool calls in the response can be stripped before execution. ## Why this matters - **Enterprise adoption**: Organizations cannot send proprietary code to external APIs without redaction - **GDPR/PII compliance**: Employee names, emails, internal data must be scrubbed - **NDA protection**: Project names, client names, business logic - **Provider-agnostic**: One redaction layer covers all LLM providers - **Zero gaps**: Unlike tool-level hooks, API-level hooks cover everything - **Defense-in-depth**: Catches exfiltration that tool-level hooks miss ## Scope Minimal change — add 2 hook points in `provider.go` or expose via plugin API. The actual redaction logic lives in external tools/plugins. OpenCode just needs to provide the interception point.
signals.author: paroque28

signals.title: bug: mouse escape sequences garbled after TUI exit
signals.text: ## Description After exiting the opencode TUI (via quit, Ctrl+C, or process stop), mouse escape sequences appear as garbled text in the terminal: ``` 35;89;19M35;84;20M35;76;22M35;71;23M35;67;23M35;67;24M35;67;25M35... ``` This is a separate issue from in-session mouse garbling (#3199 / PR #19520). The in-session bug is about fragmented SGR sequences leaking through StdinParser timeouts during active use. This bug occurs **after** the TUI has exited. ## Root Cause This is an upstream bug in `@opentui/core`'s `cleanupBeforeDestroy()` method. During renderer destruction, `stdin.setRawMode(false)` is called (re-enabling terminal ECHO) **before** mouse tracking is disabled. Any mouse events arriving during this window get echoed as raw escape sequence bytes. The correct ordering already exists in `@opentui/core`'s `suspend()` method, which calls `disableMouse()` before `setRawMode(false)`. **Upstream issue:** https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/issues/904 **Upstream fix PR:** https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/pull/905 ## Reproduction 1. Run `opencode` 2. Move the mouse while the TUI is active 3. Exit the TUI (quit or Ctrl+C) 4. Move the mouse in the shell immediately after exit 5. Garbled escape sequences appear ## Workaround A `patchedDependencies` patch for `@opentui/core` can fix this by adding `disableMouse()` + stdin drain before `setRawMode(false)` in `cleanupBeforeDestroy()`. A PR with this patch is forthcoming. ## Environment - macOS / Linux - Affects `@opentui/core@0.1.90` and `@opentui/core@0.1.95`
signals.author: agutmanstein-scale

signals.title: Memory Megathread
signals.text: We have scattered reports of memory issues so we are going to tackle them all in a central place. PLEASE DO NOT RUN YOUR LLM AND SUGGEST SOLUTIONS IT IS ALWAYS WRONG What we need help with is collecting heap snapshots. There are two ways to do that. Manual snapshot flow - run opencode (terminal not desktop) - use it until memory has grown (we don't need crazy numbers, once it hits 1-2gb it should help) - press ctrl+p and select heap snapshot - ui will freeze while it is generated - upload generated files [here](https://www.dropbox.com/request/njJ07VcjIb0wPQ50ARe2) - leave a comment describing your issue a bit Automatic snapshot flow - run opencode with `OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT=1`, for example `OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT=1 opencode` - use it until memory grows past around 2gb - opencode checks memory once a minute and automatically writes a heap snapshot when rss is above 2gb - snapshots are written to the log directory as `.heapsnapshot` files - upload generated files [here](https://www.dropbox.com/request/njJ07VcjIb0wPQ50ARe2) - leave a comment describing your issue a bit and mention that you used the automatic flow If you follow this we can almost always trace the issue and fix it
signals.author: thdxr

signals.title: opencode serve stops polling listener epoll fd; all connections hang until restart
signals.text: ### Description `opencode serve` can get into a state where the process is still alive and listening on `127.0.0.1:4096`, but it no longer responds to any HTTP request, including `/global/health`. Restarting the `opencode serve` process immediately fixes it. This does not look like a slow route, project bootstrap, MCP, LSP, or plugin initialization issue because `/global/health` also hangs and receives 0 bytes. The socket/runtime state suggests the listener remains open and registered in epoll, but the thread that normally polls the listener epoll fd stops doing so. ### OpenCode version ```text 1.3.17 ``` ### Command ```bash opencode serve --hostname=127.0.0.1 --port=4096 --log-level=DEBUG ``` ### Steps to reproduce I do not have a deterministic reproduction yet. I observed this on a long-running `opencode serve` process inside a Linux sandbox/container while using the server from a local client. When wedged, this request connects but times out with 0 bytes: ```bash curl -sv --http1.1 --no-keepalive --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:4096/global/health ``` Output: ```text * Trying 127.0.0.1:4096... * Connected to 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) port 4096 > GET /global/health HTTP/1.1 > Host: 127.0.0.1:4096 > User-Agent: curl/8.5.0 > Accept: */* > * Operation timed out after 5002 milliseconds with 0 bytes received * Closing connection ``` ### Expected behavior `/global/health` should return quickly: ```json {"healthy":true,"version":"1.3.17"} ``` ### Actual behavior The TCP connection is established, but no HTTP response bytes are returned. The process remains alive and listening, but requests pile up until clients time out. Killing and restarting `opencode serve` restores normal behavior. ### Process state In one occurrence, the listener process was PID `900`: ```bash PID=$(ss -ltnp 'sport = :4096' | grep -o 'pid=[0-9]*' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2) echo "$PID" ps -p "$PID" -o pid,ppid,stat,etime,pcpu,pmem,wchan:32,args ``` Output: ```text 900 PID PPID STAT ELAPSED %CPU %MEM WCHAN COMMAND 900 7 Sl 40:48 0.1 0.0 futex_wait_queue_me opencode serve --hostname=127.0.0.1 --port=4096 --log-level=DEBUG ``` After a timed-out `/global/health` request: ```bash ss -tanpi '( sport = :4096 or dport = :4096 )' ``` Output excerpt: ```text LISTEN 13 512 127.0.0.1:4096 0.0.0.0:* users:(("opencode",pid=900,fd=16)) cubic cwnd:10 unacked:13 CLOSE-WAIT 91 0 127.0.0.1:4096 127.0.0.1:42694 bytes_received:91 ... ESTAB 218 0 127.0.0.1:4096 127.0.0.1:59964 bytes_received:218 ... ``` This suggests opencode is still listening, but not draining the accept backlog or reading request bytes. ### strace I attached `strace` while issuing a `/global/health` curl. The trace showed no `accept4`, `read`, `recvfrom`, or `write` activity for the request. Threads were blocked in `futex(...)`, with one thread blocked in `epoll_pwait2(...)`. Excerpt from a wedged process: ```text 698 19:16:29.615002 futex(0x3112fa48, FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET_PRIVATE|FUTEX_CLOCK_REALTIME, 0, NULL, FUTEX_BITSET_MATCH_ANY <unfinished ...> 627 19:16:29.615050 1, NULL <unfinished ...> 609 19:16:29.615068 futex(0x618660c, FUTEX_WAIT_PRIVATE, 1, NULL <unfinished ...> 608 19:16:29.615073 futex(0x618660c, FUTEX_WAIT_PRIVATE, 1, NULL <unfinished ...> 607 listener socket was still registered under epoll fd `5`. In a working sandbox, `strace` during `curl /global/health` shows a thread polling that listener epoll fd: ```text epoll_pwait2(5, ...) ``` In the wedged sandbox, `strace` no longer shows any thread polling epoll fd `5`. This suggests the listener socket remains registered, but the event-loop thread responsible for the listener epoll fd is no longer polling it, or the runtime has otherwise stopped dispatching listener readiness. ### Environment ```text OS: Linux, inside a sandbox/container OpenCode: 1.3.17 Server command: opencode serve --hostname=127.0.0.1 --port=4096 --log-level=DEBUG ``` `gdb` was not available on the machine, so I could not collect native backtraces. I have observed this in more than one repository/sandbox. Restarting the opencode process fixes the issue immediately. ### Additional context Because `/global/health` hangs and there is no request/response activity in `strace`, this appears to be below opencode route handling. It seems more likely to involve the Bun runtime, Node HTTP compatibility, or the `@hono/node-server` adapter than project/plugin/MCP/LSP code. signals.title: [FEATURE]: ~90% of compaction cost is avoidable cache miss
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ### Why compaction matters opencode runs long multi-turn agent sessions. As conversation history grows, we periodically compact it — asking the LLM to summarize old messages and replacing them with a concise summary. This is essential for staying within the context window. ### The paradox Compaction is supposed to save tokens. But to summarize the history, we have to **re-send** that same history to the LLM. The compaction request itself becomes one of the largest requests in the entire session — often 40K–50K tokens of input. That would be acceptable if the provider's prompt cache helped. But it doesn't. ### Why the cache misses opencode's normal chat requests share a common prefix — system prompt, tool definitions — that hits the provider's prompt cache across turns. This is already working well. The compaction request, however, builds a completely different structure: - **No system prompt** (compaction agent has none) - **No tools** (empty tool set) - **Different message history** (prior compaction messages filtered out) - **Different serialization** (media stripped, tool output truncated) Because the request shares zero prefix overlap with normal chat requests, **every token is charged at full input price**. The cache that was built up over dozens of turns is completely wasted. ### The cost in numbers Compacting ~45K tokens of history with Claude Sonnet 4 ($3.00/MTok input, $0.30/MTok cached): | | Tokens | Full price | If cached | |---|---|---|---| | System prompt | ~2K | $0.006 | $0.0006 | | Tools | ~3K | $0.009 | $0.0009 | | Dropped messages | ~40K | $0.120 | $0.012 | | Summary instruction | ~200 | $0.0006 | $0.0006 (not cached) | | **Total** | **~45.2K** | **$0.136** | **$0.014 (~90% saved)** | The difference is **~10x**. Over a long session with multiple compactions, this adds up — especially ironic for an operation whose entire purpose is cost reduction. ### The fix is straightforward The compaction request should share the same prefix as normal chat requests. Instead of building a separate request structure, keep the system prompt, tool definitions, and message serialization identical — only append a short "please summarize" instruction at the end. ``` Normal chat: [system] + [tools] + [old messages] + [kept messages] + [user input] Compaction: [system] + [tools] + [old messages] + [summary prompt] ↑ cache hit up to here ``` The prefix `[system] + [tools] + [old messages]` was already sent in previous turns. The provider serves it from cache at 10% of the normal price. Only the ~200-token summary instruction is new. This is the same approach described in the [bash-agent wiki on Cache-Aligned Summarization](https://github.com/lloydzhou/bash-agent/wiki/Cache%E2%80%90Aligned-Summarization), where it cuts compaction cost by ~90% in practice.

This is slower and less discoverable than a message-level action. ## Proposed behavior - Add a message action button: "Fork to new session" on user messages. - On click, call `session.fork` with `sessionID` and `messageID`. - Navigate to the returned forked session. - Restore prompt content from the selected source message in the new session. - Use localized error handling (no hard-coded strings). ## Scope - `packages/ui`: expose/render message-level fork action next to existing message actions. - `packages/app`: wire action to API, prompt scoping, navigation, and error toast. - Keep implementation small and focused; do not change server fork semantics in this issue. ## Acceptance criteria - Fork action appears on user messages in app timeline. - Fork creates a new session from the selected message boundary. - New session opens immediately and is highlighted/selected in sidebar. - Prompt state is scoped to the new session, not the previous one. - Typecheck passes for affected packages. ## Verification plan - Run `bun run typecheck` from `packages/app`. - Manual test: 1. Open a session with at least one user+assistant turn. 2. Click "Fork to new session" on a user message. 3. Confirm route changes to the new session. 4. Confirm sidebar highlights the new session. 5. Confirm draft/prompt content corresponds to the selected source message. ## Notes - This issue is intentionally app-focused and aligned with the contribution rule to keep changes small. - If maintainers want sibling-aware fork title increments (`fork #2`, `fork #3`), that should be tracked as a separate backend issue.

signals.title: Review panel cannot be resized smaller than ~55% of window width due to session panel max-width cap
signals.text: ### Description The session/chat panel has a hardcoded maximum width of 45% of the window (`window.innerWidth * 0.45`) in the ResizeHandle in `packages/app/src/pages/session.tsx`: ```tsx <ResizeHandle direction="horizontal" size={layout.session.width()} min={450} max={typeof window === "undefined" ? 1000 : window.innerWidth * 0.45} ... /> ``` Because the review panel takes whatever space the session panel doesn't use, this effectively forces the review panel to always occupy at least ~55% of the window width. There is no way to make the review panel smaller than this, regardless of window size. On a 1920px wide monitor the session panel maxes out at ~864px, leaving the review panel with at least ~1056px it cannot give back. On smaller screens the problem is worse, at 1280px the session panel caps at ~576px, pinning the review panel at a minimum of ~704px (~55%). The fix appears straightforward: raise `max` to a higher fraction (e.g. `window.innerWidth * 0.70`) so the session panel can take up more of the screen, allowing the review panel to be resized to a narrower, more practical width. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.15.13 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open OpenCode Desktop with an active workspace 2. Open the Review panel 3. Attempt to drag the divider handle rightward to make the session/chat panel wider and the review panel narrower 4. signals.title: Project-level local plugin causes OpenCode v1.16.0 startup to hang
signals.text: ### Description ### Summary OpenCode `v1.16.0` appears to hang during startup when a project contains any local plugin under `.opencode/plugins/`. This does not seem to be caused by the plugin implementation itself: even a minimal empty plugin reproduces the issue. Downgrading to `v1.15.12` makes the same project start normally. ### Environment - OpenCode: `1.16.0` - OS: Ubuntu under WSL - Install path: `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` - Bun: `1.3.14` - Project uses project-level local plugin directory: `.opencode/plugins/` ### Minimal Reproduction Create a new project: ```bash mkdir opencode-plugin-repro cd opencode-plugin-repro mkdir -p .opencode/plugins ``` Add a minimal local plugin: ```bash cat > .opencode/plugins/minimal.js <<'EOF' export const MinimalPlugin = async () => ({}) EOF ``` Run: ```bash opencode debug config ``` ### Expected Behavior OpenCode should start normally and load the local plugin quickly. ### Actual Behavior on v1.16.0 `opencode debug config` hangs or exceeds 30s timeout. In logs, startup reaches internal plugin loading and then stops before loading the project local plugin: ```text service=plugin ... loading internal plugin service=plugin ... loading internal plugin ... ``` It does not proceed to: ```text service=plugin path=file://.../.opencode/plugins/minimal.js loading plugin ``` ### Control Test: Remove Local Plugin If `.opencode/plugins/minimal.js` is removed, the same project starts quickly: ```bash rm .opencode/plugins/minimal.js timeout 30s opencode debug config ``` This completes in under 1s. ### Control Test: Downgrade to v1.15.12 Downgrading OpenCode fixes the issue: ```bash opencode upgrade 1.15.12 --method curl opencode --version # 1.15.12 ``` With the same `.opencode/plugins/minimal.js` present: ```bash timeout 30s opencode debug config ``` Result: succeeds. After first-run cache work, subsequent runs complete in around 1s. Logs show the local plugin loads: ```text service=plugin path=file:///.../.opencode/plugins/minimal.js loading plugin ``` ### Additional Notes This also reproduces with a real project plugin, but the minimal empty plugin above is sufficient. Clearing proxy-related environment variables did not change the behavior. This looks like a regression in v1.16.0 around project-level local plugin discovery/loading, or the Bun/dependency handling path triggered by local plugins. ### Plugins described in the issue ### OpenCode version 0.16.0 ### Steps to reproduce See issue body ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Linux Ubuntu ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: glob tool respects .gitignore
signals.text: ### Summary The `glob` tool runs `rg --files --glob=<pattern>` without `--no-ignore`, so anything in `.gitignore` is silently filtered out — even when the agent passes an exact path it already knows exists. This makes sense for `grep` (gitignored matches would flood context with `node_modules`/`dist` noise). It doesn't make sense for `glob`, which only returns paths. The cost of including a gitignored hit is one line; the cost of hiding it is the agent asserting a file doesn't exist when it does. ### Reproduction Just using this repo as example, on `dev` after `bun install`, ask your agent to run: ``` $ ls packages/opencode/node_modules/effect/package.json # exists glob("packages/opencode/node_modules/effect/package.json") # I → No files found glob("**/node_modules/effect/package.json") → No files found ``` Same for `dist/`, `tmp/`, `logs/`, `.env*`, `*.tsbuildinfo`. Inconsistent with `--hidden`, which the same call passes — hidden files are returned, gitignored files are not. Common cases this breaks: - "Find the built bundle" → `dist/**/*.js` returns nothing - "Where does `effect` define X?" → `**/node_modules/effect/**` returns nothing - "Find generated SDK / codegen output" → invisible ### Code `packages/core/src/ripgrep.ts:157-170`: ```ts glob: (input) => run<string>({ cwd: input.cwd, args: [ "--no-config", "--files", ...(input.hidden ? ["--hidden"] : []), ...(input.follow ? ["--follow"] : []), `--glob=${input.pattern}`, "--glob=!**/.git/**", ".", ], ... }) ``` ### Suggestion Add `--no-ignore-vcs` to the `glob` argv (keep `--glob=!**/.git/**`), leave `grep` as-is. Optionally expose `respectGitignore` on the tool for opt-back-in. Happy to PR.

signals.title: bug: UI stuck on 'thinking' indefinitely after stream error, no error displayed or state recovery
signals.text: ## Issue When a stream error occurs (e.g., `AI_APICallError`, socket closed unexpectedly), the desktop UI gets stuck showing "thinking..." indefinitely. No error message is displayed, no state recovery happens, and the session becomes unusable. The user must restart the app to recover. ## Root Cause Analysis After analyzing multiple server logs from debug dumps: 1. **Stream errors are frequent but silently swallowed** - `AI_APICallError: <none>` — empty error object, no details from the upstream API - `AI_APICallError: The socket connection was closed unexpectedly` — upstream proxy terminates the SSE stream mid-response - These errors are logged on the server side but **never propagated to the UI** 2. **UI state machine never transitions out of 'thinking'** - After a stream error, the server logs show the session is dead (no further `stream` events) - But the desktop UI continues displaying "thinking..." with no cancel button or error indicator - The frontend apparently waits for a stream event that will never come 3. **No automatic retry or timeout** - No retry mechanism after stream failure - No client-side timeout to abort stuck states - User must manually cancel or restart the app 4. **Server log stops processing** - In one dump, the last log entry at `2026-06-15T01:46:02Z` was a `cancel` event - After that, zero log entries despite the UI showing "thinking" - This confirms the **server stopped processing but the UI never received this state change** ## Server Log Evidence ``` # Frequent silent stream errors (no error detail) level=ERROR message="stream error" providerID=YerPlan modelID=qwen3.6-plus error.error="AI_APICallError: <none>" # Socket-level failures level=ERROR message="stream error" error.error="AI_APICallError: Cannot connect to API: The socket connection was closed unexpectedly" # After stream errors, server stops responding but UI stays 'thinking' level=INFO message=cancel session.id=ses_13898e204ffemfGewCcp9BrPCN # ← zero further log entries after this point (01:46 UTC) ``` ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Connect opencode desktop to an API provider via an openai-compatible proxy (e.g., `https://api.xxx.com/v1`) 2. Use a worktree session on a local project directory 3. Send a message that triggers a long-running response 4. Wait for the upstream proxy to drop the connection (intermittent, but happens frequently with unstable proxies) 5. Observe: UI stuck on "thinking...", no error shown, session unresponsive ## Expected Behavior 1. Display an error message when the stream fails (e.g., "Connection lost. Retry?") 2. Provide a "Retry" or "Cancel" button 3. Implement a client-side timeout to prevent indefinite stuck states 4. Auto-recover when the server stops responding ## Environment - **opencode**: 1.17.7 (Desktop app) - **OS**: macOS darwin arm64 (M-series) - **Electron**: 42.3.3 / Chrome 148 - **Provider**: openai-compatible proxy (not direct Anthropic/OpenAI) - **Model**: qwen3.6-plus (via proxy) - **Node**: 24.15.0 ## Related Issues - #17655: UI stuck on 'Thinking...' when tool output is pending - #19512: Build mode with Thinking enabled — UI freezes during thinking stream - #24342: Main & Sub-agents Randomly Freeze Indefinitely: Frontend Permanently Shows "thinking" - #23481: Similar — agents stuck with frontend permanently showing "thinking", no errors

signals.title: Daily date in cached system prefix breaks prompt cache across midnight
signals.text: ## Description `SystemPrompt.environment()` emits `Today's date: ${new Date().toDateString()}` at packages/opencode/src/session/system.ts:70. `env` is the first element of the `system` array built in session/prompt.ts (`const system = [...env, ...instructions, ...]`), so the date ends up in the first `role: "system"` message. `applyCaching()` in provider/transform.ts:323 takes the first two system messages (`.slice(0, 2)`) and attaches `cacheControl: { type: "ephemeral" }`. The date is therefore inside the cache-controlled prefix. `toDateString()` rolls over at local midnight. A session that stays within the cache TTL but spans midnight sends a different system prefix on the next request — cache miss, and the whole system block is re-billed as a write instead of a read. It's the only daily-changing token in that block (model id, cwd, platform, git status are all session-stable), so caching is defeated exactly for the long-running sessions that benefit most. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Use a caching-capable model (e.g. Anthropic-family). 2. Keep a session active across local midnight, within the cache TTL. 3. The next request reports a cache write for the system prefix rather than a read. ## Suggested fix Keep the date out of the cached prefix — e.g. move it from `environment()` into the trailing user message (after the cache breakpoint). The model still receives the date, but the cached system bytes become date-invariant. ## Operating System Platform-independent

signals.title: Shell redirect targets bypass the external_directory permission
signals.text: When the shell tool scans a command for out-of-project paths, it gates them through the `external_directory` permission (default `ask`) — the same boundary the native `write`/`edit`/`read` tools enforce. But the scan skips redirection nodes (`packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts`: `… || item.type === "redirection") continue`), and there is no redirect-target handling. As a result a shell **redirect** target is never checked against `external_directory`: - `cp foo /tmp/out` → `external_directory` is **asked** ✅ - `cat foo > /tmp/out`, `env > /tmp/out`, `echo k >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` → `external_directory` is **never consulted**; only the `bash` permission fires, and the redirect silently writes outside the project. So a one-token shell redirect bypasses the project boundary that every other write path in opencode respects. **Reproduce** (on current `dev`): with `external_directory` set to `ask`/`deny`, `cp src /external/x` prompts but `env > /external/x` does not, and the write to `/external/x` goes through. **Impact**: an out-of-project write/exfiltration via redirection is not gated by `external_directory`, inconsistent with `cp`/`mv`/native tools. A fix is proposed in the linked PR (feed `file_redirect` destinations through the existing `argPath → containsPath → scan.dirs` pipeline; skip fd-dups / here-docs / std-stream pseudo-devices).

signals.title: fix(tui): prevent whitespace-only prompt from being submitted
signals.text: ## Summary The TUI prompt can be submitted when it contains only whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines), which sends an effectively empty message to the session. ## Root Cause In `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx`, the submit guard checks: ```ts if (!store.prompt.input) return false ``` This only blocks a completely empty string. A string of whitespace characters (`" "`, `"\t"`, etc.) is truthy and passes the check, resulting in a blank user message being sent. ## Fix Change the guard to trim whitespace before checking: ```ts if (!store.prompt.input.trim()) return false ``` The trimmed value is already computed two lines below for command detection, so this is a minimal, safe change. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open the TUI. 2. Type one or more spaces in the prompt. 3. Press Enter. 4. Observe that a blank user message bubble appears and the session receives an empty prompt. ## Expected Behavior Pressing Enter on a whitespace-only prompt should do nothing (same behavior as an empty prompt).

signals.title: fix(runtime): unhandled promise rejection on modelTask startup
signals.text: ### Description In `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run/runtime.ts:430`, the `modelTask` promise is chained with `.then()` but **no `.catch()`** handler is attached. Every other fire-and-forget promise in the same vicinity has a `.catch()`: ```ts // line 402-405 -- has .catch void footer.idle().then(loadCatalog).catch(() => {}) // line 427 -- has .catch void Promise.resolve(input.afterPaint(ctx)).catch(() => {}) // line 430 -- MISSING .catch() void modelTask.then((info) => { state.providers = info.providers state.variants = variantsFor(state.providers, state.model) state.limits = info.limits // ... footer events ... }) ``` If `modelTask` rejects (network failure, corrupted model catalog, provider registry error), the rejection goes unhandled -- this is an **unhandled promise rejection** that can crash the process. This runs on every session startup, so it's on a critical code path. State variables (`state.providers`, `state.variants`, `state.limits`) would remain unpopulated, causing downstream consumers to crash or behave incorrectly. **Fix**: Add `.catch(() => {})` to match the sibling patterns: ```diff - void modelTask.then((info) => { + void modelTask.then((info) => { state.providers = info.providers state.variants = variantsFor(state.providers, state.model) state.limits = info.limits // ... - }) + }).catch(() => {}) ``` ### Plugins n/a ### OpenCode version dev ### Steps to reproduce Cause `modelTask` to reject (e.g. network interruption during model catalog load) and observe the unhandled promise rejection crash. ### Screenshot and/or share link n/a ### Operating System n/a ### Terminal n/a

signals.title: fix(mdns): log mDNS errors instead of silencing them
signals.text: ### Description In `packages/opencode/src/server/mdns.ts`, all mDNS error paths use empty handlers, making any mDNS failure completely invisible: ```ts // line 22 -- service-level errors silenced service.on("error", () => {}) // line 25-33 -- publish errors silenced try { ... } catch { if (bonjour) { try { bonjour.destroy() } catch {} // line 29 } } // line 38-42 -- unpublish errors silenced try { bonjour.unpublishAll(); bonjour.destroy() } catch {} ``` When running `opencode server`, if mDNS/Bonjour fails (port conflict, network interface issue, library error), the server silently fails to advertise itself on the local network. Users trying to discover it via network discovery tools see nothing and have **zero diagnostic feedback** about why. **Fix**: Log the error details in each handler instead of swallowing them, for example: ```diff - service.on("error", () => {}) + service.on("error", (err) => console.warn("mDNS:", err)) ``` ### Plugins n/a ### OpenCode version dev ### Steps to reproduce Start `opencode server` in an environment where mDNS is unavailable or fails. The server starts without error but is not discoverable via network discovery. ### Screenshot and/or share link n/a ### Operating System n/a ### Terminal n/a

signals.title: fix(mcp): log process.kill failures during MCP client cleanup instead of silencing
signals.text: ### Description In `packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts:525`, when cleaning up MCP client child processes, `process.kill(dpid, "SIGTERM")` is wrapped in an empty `catch {}` block: ```ts for (const dpid of pids) { try { process.kill(dpid, "SIGTERM") } catch {} // error silently swallowed } ``` If `process.kill` fails (e.g., process already dead, permission denied, process ID reused), the error is completely invisible. The MCP cleanup continues but the child process may remain alive as a zombie, accumulating over time and leaking OS resources. **Fix**: Log the error instead of swallowing it: ```diff try { process.kill(dpid, "SIGTERM") - } catch {} + } catch (err) { + console.warn("MCP kill failed:", err) + } ``` ### Plugins n/a ### OpenCode version dev ### Steps to reproduce Kill or otherwise invalidate an MCP child process ID, then trigger MCP client cleanup. The error is silently ignored and the process may remain alive. ### Screenshot and/or share link n/a ### Operating System n/a ### Terminal n/a

signals.title: TUI: Enter key swallowed in Connect Provider API-key dialog after paste (v1.17.7)
signals.text: ## Bug In the TUI Connect Provider flow, pressing `Enter` after pasting an API key into the `DialogPrompt` field does nothing. The UI appears stuck and the only escape is to restart OpenCode. The credential **does** get persisted to `auth.json`, so on next launch the provider is connected — but the in-session flow is broken. ## Repro 1. Launch `opencode` (v1.17.7) TUI 2. `/models` 3. `Ctrl+a` (open provider list) 4. Select **OpenRouter** (or any provider using the `api` auth method) 5. Paste API key into the **"API key"** prompt 6. Press `Enter` ## Expected `Enter` submits the key, dialog closes, provider is connected. ## Actual `Enter` is swallowed. UI stays on the prompt. No error, no feedback. Restarting OpenCode shows the credential was saved. ## Environment - opencode: 1.17.7 - platform: darwin (macOS) - Installed via: npm/bun global ## Logs `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` shows no error around the attempt — only repeated instance dispose/recreate cycles when the TUI is restarted. ## Suspected cause `packages/tui/src/ui/dialog-prompt.tsx` uses a multiline `TextareaRenderable` and relies on the keymap layer (`dialog.prompt.submit` bound to `return`, priority 1) to intercept Enter before the textarea consumes it. This routing appears unreliable, particularly right after a paste. The default keybind in `packages/tui/src/config/keybind.ts`: ```ts "dialog.prompt.submit": keybind("return", "Submit dialog prompt"), ``` Related test file `packages/tui/test/cli/tui/dialog-prompt.test.tsx` covers Enter-vs-newline conflicts but does **not** cover the paste-then-submit path. ## Workaround Any of: ```sh opencode auth login --provider openrouter ``` or manually edit `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`: ```json "openrouter": { "type": "api", "key": "sk-or-v1-..." } ``` ## Suggested fix - Use a single-line input renderable for API-key style prompts (no newline semantics needed), OR - Explicitly intercept raw `return` at the `DialogPrompt` level before the textarea handles it - Add a regression test: paste text into `DialogPrompt` → press `return` → `onConfirm` called exactly once with the pasted value

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Add Personas to support role-specific OpenCode environments
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Problem OpenCode currently supports agents, commands, permissions, configuration, rules, MCPs, and plugins, but these concepts are all loaded into the same global or project-level working environment. This becomes noisy when a user works in different roles inside the same repository or across multiple repositories. For example, the same user may sometimes work as: ```text frontend developer backend developer code reviewer scrum master product manager ``` Today, this often leads to a large shared setup like: ```text .opencode/ agents/ frontend-dev.md backend-dev.md code-reviewer.md scrum-master.md product-manager.md commands/ frontend-feature.md backend-task.md review-code.md refine-story.md sprint-risk.md ``` The issue is not that agents or commands are missing. The issue is that unrelated working modes are mixed together in the same namespace. A reviewer should normally have a read-only setup. A frontend developer may need UI-specific commands, design-system instructions, Storybook/Playwright MCPs, and edit permissions. A product manager may need refinement and acceptance-criteria workflows, but no code-editing tools. Right now, users can approximate this with agents and commands, but there is no first-class way to switch the entire OpenCode environment according to the role they are currently performing. --- ## Proposed Solution Add a new first-class concept called **Personas**. A persona would be a named, role-specific OpenCode operating environment. ```text Persona = a named configuration overlay for a specific working mode ``` Example personas: ```text frontend backend reviewer scrum-master product-manager ``` Each persona could define or scope: ```text commands agents instructions permissions model defaults MCP settings tool behavior plugins, if supported by the current architecture ``` Instead of all commands and agents living in one shared namespace, persona-specific setup could live under: ```text .opencode/ personas/ frontend/ persona.jsonc AGENTS.md agents/ commands/ backend/ persona.jsonc AGENTS.md agents/ commands/ reviewer/ persona.jsonc AGENTS.md agents/ commands/ product/ persona.jsonc AGENTS.md agents/ commands/ ``` The selected persona would act as a config overlay on top of the normal OpenCode configuration. Conceptual load order: ```text 1. OpenCode defaults 2. Global config 3. Project config 4. Existing .opencode config 5. Selected persona config 6. Runtime or CLI overrides ``` If no persona is selected, OpenCode should keep its current behavior. --- ## Behavior ### CLI Users should be able to start OpenCode with a persona: ```bash opencode --persona frontend opencode --persona reviewer ``` For non-interactive mode: ```bash opencode run --persona reviewer "review the current diff" ``` ### TUI Users should be able to inspect and switch personas from inside the TUI: ```text /persona list /persona current /persona switch frontend /persona inspect frontend ``` The active persona should be visible somewhere in the TUI status area, for example: ```text Persona: frontend Agent: dev Model: claude-sonnet ``` ### Persona-scoped commands Commands should be scoped to the active persona. For example: ```text /review ``` Could mean a frontend review workflow inside the `frontend` persona, but a stricter read-only code review workflow inside the `reviewer` persona. This avoids command pollution like: ```text /frontend-review /backend-review /security-review /product-review ``` OpenCode should define clear conflict behavior when a persona command has the same name as a global command. Possible behavior: ```text persona command > project command > global command ``` Or OpenCode could warn when a command is shadowed. ### Persona-scoped agents A persona should also be able to load persona-specific agents. Example: ```text .opencode/personas/frontend/agents/dev.md .opencode/personas/frontend/agents/a11y-reviewer.md .opencode/personas/frontend/agents/design-system-reviewer.md ``` And: ```text .opencode/personas/reviewer/agents/reviewer.md ``` This would allow each persona to expose only the agents relevant to that working mode. ### Permission changes Persona switching may change permissions. Example: ```text reviewer → frontend ``` This may enable file editing. OpenCode should warn when switching to a persona that grants broader permissions: ```text Switching from reviewer to frontend will enable file editing. Continue? ``` --- ## Example Persona Config ```jsonc { "name": "frontend", "label": "Frontend Developer", "description": "React, TypeScript, UI quality, design system, accessibility, and frontend verification.", "defaultAgent": "dev", "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5", "instructions": [ "AGENTS.md", "docs/frontend-standards.md", "docs/design-system.md", "docs/accessibility.md" ], "permission": { "read": "allow", "glob": "allow", "grep": "allow", "edit": "ask", "bash": "ask", "lsp": "allow", "websearch": "ask", "webfetch": "ask" }, "mcp": { "context7": { "enabled": true }, "storybook": { "enabled": true }, "playwright": { "enabled": false } } } ``` Example reviewer persona: ```jsonc { "name": "reviewer", "label": "Code Reviewer", "description": "Read-only code review mode focused on correctness, regressions, maintainability, security, and test coverage.", "defaultAgent": "reviewer", "permission": { "read": "allow", "glob": "allow", "grep": "allow", "edit": "deny", "bash": "ask", "lsp": "allow", "websearch": "ask", "webfetch": "ask" } } ``` --- ## Why This Matters * Keeps OpenCode setups clean when users perform multiple roles. * Reduces command and agent namespace pollution. * Makes role-specific permissions safer and more explicit. * Allows read-only reviewer setups without affecting developer workflows. * Allows frontend/backend/product/delivery workflows to have different instructions, commands, agents, MCPs, and validation behavior. * Improves team usage because each role can have a predictable OpenCode environment. * Preserves current behavior when no persona is selected. This would make OpenCode more scalable for users who are not always acting as the same kind of developer. [1]: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/32672 "[FEATURE]: Add /usage slash command to display subscription usage in TUI · Issue #32672 · anomalyco/opencode · GitHub"

signals.title: FFF grep tool returns no matches when `path` is a directory
signals.text: ## Summary The `grep` tool (FFF-backed) returns **zero matches** whenever its `path` argument is a **directory**, even for files it finds in an unfiltered repo-wide search. The directory filter over-constrains to empty. ## Environment - opencode `1.16.2` (FFF v0.8.1 per `fff_health`), Linux x86_64. - Repo: ~2973 git-tracked files, all tracked (none gitignored). ## Reproduction (decisive) Same pattern, only the `path` differs. The match string `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` exists in `docs/adf/operations.md` and `docs/taxonomy/routing_scenarios/adf/review_tier.md`. | pattern | `path` arg | result | |---|---|---| | `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | *(none — repo-wide)* | **FOUND** both files | | `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | `docs` | **No matches** | | `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | `docs/taxonomy` | **No matches** | | `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | `docs/adf` | **No matches** | | `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | `docs/taxonomy/routing_scenarios/adf/review_tier.md` (exact file) | **FOUND** | And a string that lives **only** under one directory: - `grep "Route through pi-rust until opencode"` (no path) → found in all 4 `docs/taxonomy/routing_scenarios/adf/*.md`. - `grep "Route through pi-rust until opencode" path=docs/taxonomy/routing_scenarios/adf` → **No matches**. ## What works / what does not - `grep` with **no** `path` (repo-wide): works. - `grep` with an **exact file** `path`: works (direct read). - `grep` with a **directory** `path`: returns nothing. ← bug - `find` / `glob` (file-name search): works (locates the files fine; they are in the FFF index — `fff_health` reports 2783 indexed files). ## Likely cause The directory `path` filter is over-strict — it appears to discard all candidates instead of constraining to those under the directory. It is **not** staleness (`fff_rescan` does not fix it), **not** a `.md`/`docs` exclusion (some `.md` files are matched repo-wide), **not** frecency/cold-files (the files ARE found repo-wide), and **not** depth-specific (shallow dirs like `docs` also fail). ## Workaround Use shell `grep -rn <dir>` for directory-scoped search, or drop the `path` arg and search repo-wide. ## Expected Directory `path` should constrain results to files under that directory (recursive), matching ripgrep/git-grep semantics. Happy to provide more diagnostics. Thanks!

signals.title: [BUG] Auto-compaction crashes with SessionPrompt.loop stack trace when context is full
signals.text: ## Description When the context window reaches its limit during a long session, the expected auto-compaction does not trigger. Instead, the session crashes with a stack trace originating from `SessionPrompt.loop` → `SessionRunState.ensureRunning`. This is distinct from #22883 (OOM kill) — this is a runtime crash in the compaction trigger path, not a memory issue. ## Stack Trace ``` ess (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-zbg3d2c1.js:895:3280) at SessionPrompt.run (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-zbg3d2c1.js:1031:1645) at SessionPrompt.run (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-zbg3d2c1.js:1030:904) at SessionRunState.ensureRunning (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-zbg3d2c1.js:1031:1616) at SessionRunState.ensureRunning (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-zbg3d2c1.js:2:8040) at SessionPrompt.loop (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-zbg3d2c1.js:1030:628) at SessionPrompt.loop (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-zbg3d2c1.js:1031:1552) at SessionPrompt.prompt (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-nv7cdy3k.js:3:13187) at SessionPrompt.prompt (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-zbg3d2c1.js:1030:247) ``` ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Start an OpenCode session with a model via OpenAI-compatible provider (9Router local gateway) 2. Continue the session until the context window approaches its limit 3. Send a message that would exceed the context limit 4. Observe: crash instead of auto-compaction ## Expected Behavior Auto-compaction should trigger automatically when the context window is full, summarizing older messages and continuing the session seamlessly. ## Actual Behavior The session crashes with the above stack trace. Manual `/compact` works fine before context is full — the issue is specifically with the automatic compaction trigger path. ## Environment | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | **OpenCode** | 1.17.7 | | **Node** | v24.14.1 | | **Platform** | Windows (win32) | | **Provider** | OpenAI-compatible via 9Router (local gateway) | ## Additional Context - Manual `/compact` works correctly when invoked before context is full - The crash occurs specifically in `SessionRunState.ensureRunning` → `SessionPrompt.loop` when auto-compaction should be invoked - The provider is a local OpenAI-compatible gateway (9Router) — the issue appears to be client-side in OpenCode's session management, not provider-side

signals.title: {env:VAR} in permission keys expands to native Windows backslashes, producing invalid JSON on Windows
signals.text: ### Description When an environment variable is set with a native Windows path (backslashes), using` {env:VAR} `as a permission key causes opencode to fail with a JSON parse error on startup. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.14.33 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Set an environment variable with a native Windows path: ` set MYDIR=C:\Users\me\AppData\Roaming\MyApp\config` 2. Add it as a permission key in opencode.json: "permission": { "external_directory": { "{env:MYDIR}/**": "allow" } } 3. Run opencode . **Expected behavior** opencode normalizes the expanded path to forward slashes before using it as a JSON key, or accepts backslashes in permission key paths on Windows. **Actual behavior** opencode expands `{env:MYDIR} `literally and treats the backslashes as JSON escape sequences, producing a parse error: ``` --- Errors --- InvalidEscapeCharacter at line N, column 7 Line N: "C:\Users\me\AppData\Roaming\MyApp\config/**": "allow" ^ --- End --- ``` **Workaround** Set the environment variable with forward slashes before launching opencode: `set MYDIR=C:/Users/me/AppData/Roaming/MyApp/config` This is not always possible when the variable is set by a third-party application that uses native Windows path separators. **Suggested fix** Normalize `{env:...} `expanded values to forward slashes before inserting them as permission key paths. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: opencode 1.17.7 panics with ThreadPoolBuildError (EAGAIN) when initializing worker thread pool
signals.text: Titre de l'issue : opencode 1.17.7 panics with ThreadPoolBuildError (EAGAIN) when initializing worker thread pool --- ## Description opencode crashes with a Rust panic (`SIGABRT`) when it fails to initialize its worker thread pool. The underlying OS error is `EAGAIN` (`WouldBlock`, "Resource temporarily unavailable"). This appears to be a robustness issue in opencode's thread-pool startup code rather than a hard resource limit on the system. ## Environment | Item | Value | |------|-------| | opencode version | `1.17.7` | | OS | Arch Linux (rolling) | | Kernel | `6.18.35-1-lts` | | Shell | `zsh 5.9.1` | | Terminal multiplexer | `tmux 3.6b` | | Executable | `/home/richard/.opencode/bin/opencode` | | Working project | `/home/richard/Nexus/Tech/Projects/Bash/forge-disk-customize` | ## Steps to reproduce A fully deterministic reproduction is not yet available. The crash occurred during an interactive opencode session in tmux while working on a small Bash project. The sequence was approximately: 1. Open a tmux session. 2. Start opencode in `/home/richard/Nexus/Tech/Projects/Bash/forge-disk-customize`. 3. Run several tasks that spawn sub-agents / shell commands. 4. opencode panics while trying to initialize a worker thread pool. ## Observed frequency Three consecutive crashes within roughly 30 minutes, all `SIGABRT`, in the same tmux scope: ```text PID 61761 opencode SIGABRT 16:07 PID 67642 opencode SIGABRT 16:09 PID 79018 opencode SIGABRT 16:37 ``` ## Logs / error output ```text thread 'main' (1039099) panicked at src/main.rs:315:10: Failed to initialize worker thread pool: ThreadPoolBuildError { kind: IOError(Os { code: 11, kind: WouldBlock, message: "Resource temporarily unavailable" }) } note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace zsh: fork failed: ressource temporairement non disponible zsh: fork failed: ressource temporairement non disponible zsh: fork failed: ressource temporairement non disponible _zsh_autosuggest_bind_widgets:15: fork failed: ressource temporairement non disponible ``` The error repeats across multiple panicked threads and is accompanied by cascading `zsh: fork failed` messages. ## Coredump details ```text PID: 79018 (opencode) UID: 1000 (richard) Signal: 6 (ABRT) Timestamp: Wed 2026-06-17 16:37:03 CEST Command Line: opencode Executable: /home/richard/.opencode/bin/opencode Control Group: /user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/tmux-spawn-a2c8654e-9279-401b-a004-2954c480a8c1.scope Storage: /var/lib/systemd/coredump/core.opencode.1000.e60bad988b79471fa8c9a82b90d82df6.79018.1781707023000000.zst (present, 102.2M) ``` Stack trace of the crashing thread: ```text #0 0x00007fb3cb8256e6 abort (libc.so.6 + 0x256e6) #1 0x00000000039ca5d0 n/a (opencode + 0x37ca5d0) #2 0x00000000046a5425 n/a (opencode + 0x44a5425) #3 0x0000000004ffadda n/a (opencode + 0x4dfadda) #4 0x00000000051820fc n/a (opencode + 0x4f820fc) #5 0x00000000049894c6 n/a (opencode + 0x47894c6) #6 0x00000000050fcbb4 n/a (opencode + 0x4efcbb4) ... ``` ## Resource state at crash time The following measurements were taken **after** the crashes, once the system had partially recovered. They help exclude simple `ulimit` / cgroup exhaustion as the root cause. | Resource | Value | |----------|-------| | `ulimit -u` (max user processes) | 255 322 | | cgroup `user.slice/user-1000.slice/pids.max` | `max` | | cgroup `user.slice/user-1000.slice/pids.current` | 242 | | Total system threads (`ps -eLf`) | ~635 | | Available RAM | ~58 GiB | | Memory pressure (`memory.pressure`) | `avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00` | A single zombie process was left behind: `[zsh] <defunct>`, indicating a parent process did not reap its child. ## Project context The project being edited at the time of the crash is a 135-line Bash script skeleton with no `main()`, no infinite loops, no background jobs (`&`), and no heavy forking logic. It is not the cause of the crash. The active opencode instance at the time was performing sub-agent work. ## Expected behavior When the OS returns `EAGAIN` while creating a worker thread, opencode should handle the situation gracefully, for example: - Retry with a short backoff, - Reduce the requested thread-pool size, - Display a clear user-facing error message, - Or at least fail cleanly without a panic and `SIGABRT`. ## Actual behavior opencode panics in `src/main.rs:315`, aborts with `SIGABRT`, terminates the session, and leaves a `zsh` zombie process. ## Attachments 1. Terminal screenshot: `~/Capture d'écran_20260617_163908.png` 2. Compressed coredump: `/var/lib/systemd/coredump/core.opencode.1000.e60bad988b79471fa8c9a82b90d82df6.79018.1781707023000000.zst` ## Additional context - The current opencode instance (restarted after the crash) is running normally with ~33 threads. - The issue appears transient, but the panic makes recovery impossible without restarting opencode and losing context. - A `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` run has not yet been captured because the crash is not deterministic. --- *Report generated on 2026-06-17 for opencode 1.17.7.*

signals.title: fix: auto-title overwrites plugin session rename on first turn
signals.text: ### Description Plugin tools that rename a session via `client.session.update()` have no effect on the first turn of a new session. The title reverts to an auto-generated one. Calling the same tool on the second turn works fine. The cause is a race in `SessionPrompt.ensureTitle` (`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`). On step 1 of the loop, auto-title is forked into the background: ```typescript if (step === 1) yield* title({ session, ... }).pipe(Effect.ignore, Effect.forkIn(scope)) ``` The forked task checks `isDefaultTitle(input.session.title)` against the `session` object captured at the top of the loop iteration (line 1139), before any tools have run. On a new session this is always `true`, so auto-title proceeds to generate and set its own title via `sessions.setTitle()`. Meanwhile the main LLM stream runs, the model calls the plugin's rename tool, and the plugin sets the title through the HTTP API. The auto-title's LLM call finishes later and overwrites the plugin's title. On the second turn, `sessions.get()` returns the session with the auto-generated title from turn 1. `isDefaultTitle()` returns `false`, auto-title bails out immediately, and the plugin's rename sticks. The fix would be to re-read the session title from the DB before overwriting, or to skip auto-title when the title was explicitly set by a tool during the same turn. ### Plugins Custom plugin registering a `session_rename` tool (calls `client.session.update`) ### OpenCode version 1.17.7 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a plugin that registers a tool calling `client.session.update({ path: { id: context.sessionID }, body: { title: args.title } })` 2. Configure the agent to call this tool on every turn (e.g. via system prompt or AGENTS.md) 3. Start a new session and send a message 4. Observe the session title is the auto-generated one, not the plugin's title 5. Send a second message in the same session 6. Observe the plugin's title now sticks ### Operating System Fedora 44 (Linux 7.0.12) ### Terminal Ghostty

signals.title: fix(lsp): pyright spawn sets only pythonPath, never venvPath/venv — venv imports unresolved without pyrightconfig.json
signals.text: ### Description OpenCode's pyright LSP spawn sets only `pythonPath` in the initialization options, never `venvPath`/`venv`. This means pyright can't resolve third-party packages installed in a project's `.venv/` unless the user manually creates a `pyrightconfig.json`. Without that workaround, every venv import is flagged `reportMissingImports`, flooding the agent with noise until it ignores diagnostics entirely. The pyright spawn code in [`packages/opencode/src/lsp/server.ts`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/lsp/server.ts) only sets `initialization["pythonPath"]` after detecting the venv interpreter: ```ts const initialization: Record<string, string> = {} // ... detects VIRTUAL_ENV / .venv / venv ... initialization["pythonPath"] = potentialPythonPath ``` Pyright's preferred venv mechanism is `venvPath` + `venv` (path concatenation, no interpreter execution needed). Setting only `pythonPath` requires pyright to execute the interpreter to discover `sys.path`, which is fragile and silently falls back to system Python when that fails. Related: #6131 (closed as not planned, but the `workspace/configuration` part it reported is actually fixed on current `dev` — the remaining unfixed part is this `server.ts` issue), #25408, #2050. The fix is small — add `venvPath` and `venv` to `initialization` alongside `pythonPath` in the pyright spawn function (~5 lines). ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version v1.17.7 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a Python project with a `.venv/` at the root containing third-party packages (e.g. `pandas`, `numpy`). 2. Enable `"lsp": true` in opencode config. Do **not** add a `pyrightconfig.json`. 3. Open a `.py` file in the project that imports a venv-only package. 4. Run `opencode run` with a trivial prompt that triggers an edit to that file. 5. Observe `reportMissingImports` diagnostics on every venv import. Verification that `pyrightconfig.json` with `{"venvPath": ".", "venv": ".venv"}` resolves it: with config → 0 errors; without config → 2 `reportMissingImports` errors on `pandas`/`numpy` (system Python doesn't have them, venv does). The config-file workaround bypasses the LSP channel entirely by reading from disk. ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A — reproducible via the steps above and source link. ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04 ### Terminal GNOME Terminal

signals.title: bug: InterruptError — All fibers interrupted when InstanceStore.dispose races with Agent.list
signals.text: ## Describe the bug When an HTTP request triggers `Agent.list` (which reads agent configuration from the filesystem via `ScopedCache.get`), and at the same time another request triggers `InstanceStore.dispose`, the `ScopedCache` invalidation interrupts all in-flight lookup fibers, producing `InterruptError: All fibers interrupted without error`. This error propagates up to the HTTP response and reaches the Telegram Bot as a `session.promptAsync` failure. ## Stack trace ``` InterruptError: All fibers interrupted without error at FileSystem.up (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-pcf2w4yn.js:2:18581) at FileSystem.up (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-ewqah108.js:16:23248) at Agent.state (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-ae5jadfy.js:2:4743) at Agent.state (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-10rcnd8y.js:171:805) at Agent.list (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-nv7cdy3k.js:2:207057) at Agent.list (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-10rcnd8y.js:171:5293) at InstanceHttpApi.agent (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-nv7cdy3k.js:2:79248) at InstanceHttpApi.agent (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-nv7cdy3k.js:2:207000) at Server.listen (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-nv7cdy3k.js:3:46713) at Server.listen (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-nv7cdy3k.js:3:46836) ``` ## Root cause ### 1. Race condition in `InstanceState.make` + `disposeMiddleware` `packages/opencode/src/effect/instance-state.ts` line 38 registers a disposer that invalidates the `ScopedCache` when the instance is disposed. If a concurrent HTTP request is in the middle of `Agent.list` → `ScopedCache.get` → `lookup` → `Agent.state` (reading files via `FileSystem.up`), the invalidation closes the Effect scope and interrupts all child fibers. ### 2. Unhandled `InterruptError` in `Agent.list` `packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts` lines 357-358: ```typescript list: Effect.fn("Agent.list")(function* () { return yield* InstanceState.useEffect(state, (s) => s.list()) }) ``` `InterruptError` propagates unhandled through `InstanceHttpApi.agent` to the HTTP response. ## Affected files - `packages/opencode/src/effect/instance-state.ts` (lines 30-39) — ScopedCache with disposer that interrupts in-flight lookups - `packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts` (lines 357-358) — Agent.list without InterruptError handling - `packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/lifecycle.ts` (lines 43-53) — disposeMiddleware triggers teardown while requests are in-flight ## Suggested fix 1. In `Agent.list` (agent.ts:357), catch `InterruptError` and retry or return a degraded response 2. Consider using `Effect.uninterruptible` for the ScopedCache lookup to prevent disposal from interrupting in-flight requests

signals.title: [URGENT] Zen paid balance still hits FreeUsageLimitError / daily free usage limit.
signals.text: ### Description After adding a paid Zen balance of "$20", OpenCode Zen still returns: Free usage exceeded, add credits https://opencode.ai/zen This happens barely under 1 hour of usage, even though the account has billing/credits enabled. My understanding is that the daily free usage limit should apply only to accounts without billing/credits, not paid-balance accounts. Expected behavior Once Zen billing/credits are added, the request should be charged normally or fail with a proper paid-account/balance/model/provider error, not "FreeUsageLimitError". Actual behavior Zen still appears to apply the free/daily/IP usage limit and blocks usage with "Free usage exceeded", despite available paid balance. Why this looks like a bug The limiter path appears related to: packages/console/app/src/routes/zen/util/ipRateLimiter.ts Older/current related code paths throw "FreeUsageLimitError" from the Zen IP rate limiter. This suggests the free usage limiter may still be checked before billing/account state, or the request is being classified as free/anonymous even when using a paid Zen API key. Possible cause The paid API key/account/billing state may not be bypassing the IP/free-tier limiter, or the request may be missing/losing the authenticated Zen user/session context and falling back to IP-based free usage tracking. Steps to reproduce 1. Add "$20" credits/balance to OpenCode Zen. 2. Use a Zen API key in OpenCode / API gateway. 3. Use Zen models for normal coding-agent requests. 4. Continue for under ~1 hour. 5. Observe "Free usage exceeded, add credits https://opencode.ai/zen". Additional context This seems similar to previous reports where users had credits/balance but still received "Free usage exceeded". Please clarify whether paid Zen users are still subject to the same free daily/IP limiter, or whether this is an auth/billing-state bug. ### Plugins NA ### OpenCode version NA ### Steps to reproduce 1.
