signals.title: Unbounded growth of the `event` table: opencode.db reaches 13GB+, mostly `message.updated.1` snapshots (no retention/compaction)
signals.text: ## Summary The local SQLite store (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) grows **unbounded** on long-lived instances because the event-sourcing `event` table is never pruned, capped, or compacted. On two of our long-running instances it reached **~13 GB each**, filling a 22 GB volume to 97–99% and eventually producing `sqlite3.OperationalError: database or disk is full` on ordinary queries — the instance becomes effectively unusable. The actual conversation data is tiny by comparison; **>90% of the DB is the event log**, and within it a single event type (`message.updated.1`) dominates. ## Measured breakdown (real instance, 13.7 GB DB) ``` page_size=4096 page_count=3342166 total=13.69 GB freelist_count=18 dead=0.00 GB (0.0%) <- live data, VACUUM does not help ``` Per-table (`sum(length(data))`): | table | rows | size | avg/row | |---------|---------|-----------|---------| | **event** | 141,951 | **12.20 GB** | 83.9 KB | | message | 6,955 | 1.15 GB | 161 KB | | part | 27,775 | 0.07 GB | 2.4 KB | | others | — | ~0 | — | Within `event`, by `type`: | event type | rows | size | avg | |-------------------------------|--------|------------|---------| | **`message.updated.1`** | 26,463 | **11.94 GB** | **440 KB** | | `session.next.tool.success.1` | 7,843 | 0.12 GB | 14.8 KB | | `message.part.updated.1` | 52,644 | 0.10 GB | 1.8 KB | | everything else | ~55k | < 0.3 GB | — | So ~87% of the entire database is `message.updated.1` events. With ~6,955 messages there are ~3.8 `message.updated` events per message, each persisting what looks like a full message snapshot (avg 440 KB), and **all historical snapshots are retained forever**. The same pattern was observed independently on a second instance (also ~13 GB, same `event`-table dominance), so this is reproducible, not a one-off. ## Root cause (confirmed in source, `dev` branch) `packages/core/src/event/sql.ts` — the `event` table has no TTL, no row cap, no size limit, and no compaction column; it just stores every event's full `data` JSON: ```ts export const EventTable = sqliteTable("event", { id: text().$type<EventV2.ID>().primaryKey(), aggregate_id: text().notNull().references(() => EventSequenceTable.aggregate_id, { onDelete: "cascade" }), seq: integer().notNull(), type: text().notNull(), data: text({ mode: "json" }).$type<Record<string, unknown>>().notNull(), }, ...) ``` `packages/core/src/event.ts` — the **only** delete against `event` is a full-aggregate cascade, used when an entire session/aggregate is removed: ```ts function remove(aggregateID: string) { return db.transaction(() => Effect.gen(function* () { yield* db.delete(EventSequenceTable).where(eq(EventSequenceTable.aggregate_id, aggregateID)).run() yield* db.delete(EventTable).where(eq(EventTable.aggregate_id, aggregateID)).run() })).pipe(Effect.orDie) } ``` There is **no partial pruning** — nothing collapses superseded `message.updated.*` snapshots, keeps only the latest per message, caps per-aggregate history, or stores deltas. `packages/opencode/src/sync/README.md` confirms this is an intentional append-only log "for session replayability." That's a reasonable design goal, but with full-snapshot `message.updated` events and no retention it means every session's event history accumulates for the lifetime of the session, with no upper bound. `SessionCompaction.prune` does **not** address this — it trims context tokens sent to the model, not persisted `event` rows. ## Impact - Disk exhaustion on long-lived instances (containers/sandboxes/servers with persistent home dirs). - Once the volume is full, even read queries that need temp space fail with `database or disk is full`. - `VACUUM` cannot reclaim it (freelist ≈ 0%; it is all live data). The only current remediation is deleting whole sessions (cascade) or manually `DELETE FROM event ...`. ## Suggested fixes (any one would help) 1. **Compact superseded snapshots**: for snapshot-style events like `message.updated.*`, retain only the latest event per `(aggregate_id, message_id)` (or per message `seq`), deleting older ones — newer fully supersedes older. 2. **Store deltas instead of full snapshots** for `message.updated` (the README already notes `session.updated` was moved to fields-only; `message.updated` appears to still carry a full snapshot). 3. **Per-aggregate retention cap / periodic compaction** of the event log for inactive/completed sessions. ## Environment - Observed on builds in the 1.15.x–1.17.x range; root cause confirmed present on `dev` (current `latest`, 1.17.9) via the source above. - SQLite store at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`. Happy to provide the full per-session breakdown or a repro script if useful.

signals.title: Wispr Flow dictation is not inserted into OpenCode input inside VS Code integrated terminal on Windows
signals.text: ### Description When I run OpenCode inside the VS Code integrated terminal on Windows, dictating with Wispr Flow does not insert the transcribed text into the OpenCode prompt. What makes this notable is that the same dictation workflow works in the same machine under other conditions: - Wispr Flow works when dictating directly into the VS Code integrated terminal while OpenCode is **not** running. - Wispr Flow works when running OpenCode from Windows Terminal. So the failure seems to be specific to the combination of: - Windows - VS Code integrated terminal - OpenCode prompt active - Wispr Flow dictation This suggests an input/paste handling incompatibility in OpenCode's TUI/input layer when hosted inside the VS Code integrated terminal. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.17.11 ### Steps to reproduce ## Steps to reproduce 1. On Windows, install and enable Wispr Flow. 2. Open Visual Studio Code. 3. Open the integrated terminal in VS Code. 4. Start OpenCode in that terminal. 5. Focus the OpenCode input/prompt. 6. Dictate a sentence with Wispr Flow. 7. Observe that the transcription does not get inserted into the OpenCode prompt. ## Additional comparison checks - If I dictate directly into the VS Code integrated terminal **without** OpenCode open, Wispr Flow works. - If I run OpenCode in **Windows Terminal** and dictate there, Wispr Flow also works. ## Expected behavior The dictated/transcribed text should be inserted into the active OpenCode prompt, the same way text input works in other terminal contexts. ## Actual behavior The dictated text is not inserted into the OpenCode prompt when OpenCode is running inside the VS Code integrated terminal. ## Notes - This does **not** appear to be a general Wispr Flow issue on Windows. - This does **not** appear to be a general VS Code integrated terminal issue either. - The problem appears to be specific to OpenCode running inside the VS Code integrated terminal. - A useful angle to investigate may be how OpenCode handles paste/input/raw terminal events in this environment. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal vscode integrated terminal

signals.title: [Feature] Lazy-load MCP tool definitions to reduce token overhead
signals.text: ## Problem When multiple MCP servers are connected, ALL tool definitions from ALL servers are injected into the system prompt of EVERY conversation. With 9 MCP servers connected (project-tools, supabase, agent-browser, chrome-devtools, playwright, memory, context7, sequential-thinking, fetch), this results in ~40,000-70,000 tokens of tool definitions loaded upfront — even if the user only needs 2-3 tools. Users paying per-token to LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) bear this cost on every single message. ## Current behavior - 9 MCP servers = ~250+ tool definitions - Each tool definition = 50-200 tokens - Total overhead: ~40-70k tokens per conversation - User pays for ALL tools in EVERY message, even unused ones ## Proposed solutions 1. **Lazy tool loading** — Only inject tool definitions when context suggests they are needed (e.g., if user mentions "deploy", load Supabase tools) 2. **Tool profiles** — Let users configure preset profiles (e.g., "dev", "deploy", "debug") with only relevant MCP servers 3. **Tiered loading** — Load essential tools (project-tools, bash, read, write) by default, load others on-demand via a `/tools` command ## Impact - Reduces token cost by 30-50k tokens per conversation - No behavior change for users who want all tools available - Better UX for cost-conscious users ## Environment - OpenCode version: latest - OS: Windows - MCP servers: 9 connected

signals.title: [Bug] Native built-in file tools (Read/Write/Edit/glob/grep) return "Bun is not defined" under Desktop
signals.text: ## Summary Under OpenCode Desktop, the **built-in native file tools** (`Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `glob`, `grep`) fail immediately with the error string `Bun is not defined`. This is distinct from #25880, which tracks *third-party plugins* failing to load under the Node sidecar ΓÇö here the affected components are opencode's own first-party tools, not user-installed plugins.## Environment - OS: Windows 11 - OpenCode CLI: 1.15.10 (installed via npm global; runs under Bun and works fine) - OpenCode Desktop: running (Electron app process active)- Bun: 1.3.4 (installed and on PATH) - Node.js: v24.12.0 ## Reproduction 1. Launch an OpenCode Desktop session. 2. From any agent, invoke a native file tool, e.g.: - `glob` with any pattern - `Read` on any file - `Edit` on any file 3. The tool returns the error: `Bun is not defined`No file content is read or written; the call fails before any filesystem work.## Observed across tools Direct evidence of failure in sessions on this machine:- `glob` ΓåÆ `Bun is not defined`- `Read` ΓåÆ `Bun is not defined`- `Edit` ΓåÆ `Bun is not defined``Write` and `grep` were initially assumed affected; the canonical-database evidence below confirms all of Write, Edit, and grep (across hundreds of sessions).## Concrete evidence (canonical session database) Captured from OpenCode's authoritative session store — the SQLite database at `<user>/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, table `part` (each tool call is one `part` row whose `data` column is JSON). Aggregated across the full table: | Metric | Value | |---|---| | Tool-parts returning `Bun is not defined` | **2,611** | | Distinct sessions affected | **494** | | Date range | 2026-05-31 → 2026-07-06 (5+ weeks) | | Reproducer environment | OpenCode Desktop, local builds (`session.version = "local"`) | **All five native file tools are confirmed affected** (upgraded from the "assumed" wording in the original report): | Tool | Error occurrences | |---|---| | `read` | 1,622 | | `glob` | 465 | | `write` | 241 | | `edit` | 152 | | `grep` | 131 | ### `part` row shape ```json { "type":"tool","tool":"<name>","callID":"toolu_…", "state":{ "status":"error","input":{…},"error":"Bun is not defined", "time":{ "start":…,"end":… } } } ``` ### Representative anonymized records `read` — fails in ~4 ms; no filesystem access occurs ```json { "tool":"read","state":{ "status":"error", "input":{ "filePath":"C:\\Users\\<user>\\projects\\<repo>" }, "error":"Bun is not defined","time":{ "start":1780266435647,"end":1780266435651 } } } ``` `write` — fails in ~2 ms (content elided) ```json { "tool":"write","state":{ "status":"error", "input":{ "filePath":"C:\\Users\\<user>\\projects\\<repo>\\doc.md","content":"…" }, "error":"Bun is not defined","time":{ "duration_ms":2 } } } ``` `edit` — fails in ~3 ms ```json { "tool":"edit","state":{ "status":"error", "input":{ "filePath":"C:\\Users\\<user>\\.config\\opencode\\opencode.jsonc", "oldString":"\"small_model\": \"openai/gpt-5.4-mini\",", "newString":"\"small_model\": \"zai-coding-plan/glm-5.1\"," }, "error":"Bun is not defined","time":{ "duration_ms":3 } } } ``` `glob` ```json { "tool":"glob","state":{ "status":"error", "input":{ "pattern":".opencode/**/*","path":"C:\\Users\\<user>\\projects\\<repo>" }, "error":"Bun is not defined" } } ``` `grep` ```json { "tool":"grep","state":{ "status":"error", "input":{ "pattern":"session.*name|title.*generat","include":"*.go" }, "error":"Bun is not defined","time":{ "duration_ms":454 } } } ``` ### Observations - Failures are **synchronous and fast** (2–4 ms for `read`/`write`/`edit`): the error is returned before any filesystem work, consistent with a missing global (`globalThis.Bun`) at tool-init time rather than an I/O or permission failure. - **Deterministic per session**: every native-file-tool call fails until the agent switches to PowerShell (`Get-Content`/`Set-Content`/`Select-String`/`Get-ChildItem`), after which file access works normally — pointing at the tool implementation/runtime, not the filesystem. - **494 sessions over 5+ weeks** indicates a persistent, reproducer-stable condition under Desktop, not an intermittent fault. ## CLI vs Desktop- **CLI** (`opencode` in PowerShell, Bun runtime): native file tools work.- **Desktop** (Electron, Node.js sidecar): native file tools fail with `Bun is not defined`. This CLI/Desktop split mirrors the pattern in #25880, which suggests the same underlying root cause: the Desktop sidecar runs Node.js where `globalThis.Bun` is undefined, and the native tool implementations reference Bun-specific APIs (e.g. `Bun.file`, `Bun.write`). ## How this differs from #25880 - #25880 is titled and scoped to **third-party plugin load failures** (oh-my-openagent, opencode-pty, etc.) ΓÇö components the user opt-in installs.- This issue is about **opencode's own built-in tools** failing, which is core functionality rather than an opt-in plugin surface.- Filing separately so the native-tools symptom is triageable on its own; the root cause is very likely shared with #25880. ## Issue search (prior art) - Before filing, I searched this repo's issues for `"Bun is not defined"`, `file tool Read Edit Bun`, `glob grep Bun Windows Desktop`, and `native tool undefined Windows` (all states). The only directly related issue found was **#25880** (third-party plugin load failures under the Desktop Node sidecar). I did not find any existing issue covering **native built-in file tools** failing with this error, which is why I'm filing this separately rather than commenting on #25880. Happy to consolidate if maintainers prefer. ## Current workaround Switch the entire session to PowerShell via the `bash` tool (do not retry the native tools per-call ΓÇö each retry is wasted). Mapping:- `Read` ΓåÆ `Get-Content -Raw`- `Write` ΓåÆ `Set-Content -Encoding utf8`- `Edit` ΓåÆ `Select-String` to locate + literal `[string]::Replace()` (not regex `-replace`)- `glob` ΓåÆ `Get-ChildItem -Recurse`- `grep` ΓåÆ `Select-String`This keeps sessions functional but loses the native tools' structured output and forces every file operation through shell quoting, which is higher-variance and hazard-prone (literal structural-character edits, indentation bleed, etc.). ## Likely root cause (hypothesis, please confirm) The Desktop sidecar switched from Bun to Node.js/Electron's bundled Node around v1.14.35 (per #25880). If the native file tool implementations were written against Bun globals (`Bun.file` / `Bun.write` / etc.), they will throw `Bun is not defined` under Node even though Bun is installed on the host ΓÇö because the tool code runs inside the sidecar process, not the host shell.## Suggested fixes (any one)1. Restore the Desktop sidecar to the Bun runtime, or2. Provide a config option to select sidecar runtime (Bun / Node.js), or3. Ship a Bun API polyfill in the Desktop Node sidecar (covers `Bun.file`/`Bun.write`-style usage in native tools), or4. Rewrite native file tools to be runtime-agnostic (no `Bun.*` references).## Related issues- #25880 ΓÇö Desktop v1.14.39: Bun-target plugins fail to load (Node.js sidecar lacks Bun APIs)

signals.title: V2: define restart semantics for foreground and background shells
signals.text: ## Summary Define what happens to long-running foreground and background shell processes when the managed server restarts. Both shell process ownership and background job tracking are currently process-local. A restart interrupts that ownership, but foreground and background shells interact differently with Session restart continuity and need explicit, safe semantics. ## Current behavior `Shell.Service` owns running subprocess handles, output streams, timeout fibers, and waiters in one Location-scoped in-memory map. The process handle is scope-bound, and layer teardown clears the map and unblocks pending waiters. `Job.Service` also tracks foreground/background state and completion through process-local maps, scopes, and `Deferred`s. For a foreground shell: - the tool call remains part of active Session execution; - graceful managed shutdown suspends the active Session; - teardown interrupts the shell/tool ownership chain; - startup resumes the Session and reconciles the old running tool as interrupted rather than replaying it. For a background shell: - the shell tool has already returned a model-visible `running` result; - the Session may become idle while the subprocess continues; - managed shutdown only snapshots active Session executions, so this Session may not receive a restart-continuation marker; - teardown loses the shell and job registries, and the next server cannot observe the old PID, settle the shell, or deliver its completion through the Session inbox. Output files may remain on disk, but they are not sufficient to establish process liveness, ownership, exit status, or completion. ## Why automatic replay is unsafe Shell commands have host-user filesystem, process, and network authority. A command interrupted after partial execution may already have produced side effects. Restarting the command from the beginning can duplicate writes, deployments, messages, payments, or other external actions. Unexpected machine restart also guarantees that the original process is gone, while a managed-server-only restart could theoretically leave a detached process alive. The design should not infer either case from a stale PID without explicit ownership and identity guarantees. ## Questions to decide - On graceful managed-server restart, should OpenCode cancel running shells, wait for them, transfer/reattach ownership, or support more than one policy? - Should foreground and background shells have different shutdown behavior? - If a shell is interrupted, how is that terminal fact durably recorded and delivered to the Session? - Should an idle Session with a background shell be included in restart continuation or receive a durable completion/interruption inbox entry independently? - Can a surviving process be identified safely across server restart, including PID reuse and descendant process groups? - What output remains readable after ownership is lost? - What guarantees are possible on POSIX and Windows? - Which semantics apply to graceful service restart, server crash, and machine restart? - Should command replay ever be automatic, or only an explicit user/model decision after interruption is visible? ## Required invariants - Restart never silently reports an interrupted shell as still running. - Restart never automatically repeats ambiguous shell side effects. - Every shell that OpenCode stops during graceful shutdown receives a durable terminal/interrupted outcome. - A background shell cannot disappear without a model-visible or user-visible terminal outcome. - Completion or interruption is admitted durably before Session execution is scheduled. - Stale PIDs cannot be adopted after PID reuse. - Process-tree cleanup and orphan behavior are explicit per platform. - Retained output accurately distinguishes complete, partial, truncated, and unavailable output. ## Coverage Cover at least: - graceful restart during a foreground shell; - graceful restart while an idle Session owns a background shell; - shell exit racing with shutdown; - restart after partial output; - unexpected server death and machine restart; - process-tree cleanup on POSIX and Windows; - no duplicate command execution during Session continuation; - durable interruption/completion delivery through the Session inbox. ## Related - #34366 tracks the broader V2 shell backgrounding API and UX semantics. - #35646 implements graceful managed-service continuation for active Sessions. - #35642 tracked stale interrupted tool state after machine restart and requested fresh focused issues against the current lifecycle. - #35924 moved background completion delivery through the durable Session inbox. - `specs/v2/session-restart-continuation.md` explicitly excludes exactly-once provider or tool execution.

signals.title: Desktop stuck in "thinking" mode - sidecar stream never completes (v1.17.18, Windows)
signals.text: ### Description Body: ## Environment - **OS:** Windows 10/11 - **OpenCode Desktop:** v1.17.18 (Electron, packaged) - **Node.js:** (bundled with Electron) ## Description When sending any message in OpenCode Desktop, the app enters a permanent "thinking" state and never returns a response. This happens with **all models** — built-in free models (`deepseek-v4-flash-free`, `hy3-free`, `mimo-v2.5-free`) and custom providers (Agnes, Sensenova). ## Reproduction Steps 1. Launch OpenCode Desktop 2. Select any model (free or custom) 3. Send a message (e.g., "你好") 4. App shows "thinking" indicator indefinitely ## Log Analysis ### Sidecar starts and becomes ready sidecar connection started { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:XXXXX' } spawning sidecar { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:XXXXX' } server ready { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:XXXXX' } ### Stream starts but never completes From `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`: message=stream providerID=opencode modelID=hy3-free session.id=ses_XXX small=false agent=build mode=primary message="llm runtime selected" llm.runtime=ai-sdk llm.provider=opencode llm.model=hy3-free After this, **no further log entries** — the stream hangs silently. ### Sidecar exits after ~6 minutes From Electron logs: warn (utility) sidecar exited { code: 0 } ### Persistent npm warning WARN background dependency install failed dir="C:\Users\<user>\.config\opencode" error="Cause(Fail(NpmInstallFailedError (cause: @opencode-ai/plugin: No matching version found for @opencode-ai/plugin@local.)))" ### Git lock file conflict WARN failed to add snapshot files exitCode=128 stderr="fatal: Unable to create '.../snapshot/global/.../index.lock': File exists. Another git process seems to be running in this repository, or the lock file may be stale" ## What I've Tried 1. **Restarted OpenCode** — same issue 2. **Cleared all cache/session data** (`AppData\Roaming\ai.opencode.desktop`, `~/.local/share/opencode`, `~/.cache/opencode`) — same issue 3. **Reinstalled OpenCode completely** — same issue 4. **Verified API works directly** — tested `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions` via PowerShell, returns valid responses 5. **Checked proxy** — v2rayN/xray running on 127.0.0.1:10808, but no proxy env vars are set (`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` all empty) ## Hypothesis The sidecar's Node.js process may be: 1. Hanging on the `@opencode-ai/plugin@local` npm dependency install (blocking the event loop?) 2. Stuck waiting for a response that never arrives due to network/proxy configuration 3. The `useEnvProxy()` → `http.setGlobalProxyFromEnv()` call may be interfering with outgoing requests even when no proxy env vars are set ## Additional Info - The `@opencode-ai/plugin@local` error appears every time the sidecar initializes - Sidecar process (PID) is alive and listening on its port, but the stream never completes - No firewall/antivirus blocking detected ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: opencode attach ignores NO_PROXY — loopback requests sent through HTTP(S)_PROXY
signals.text: ### Description When `HTTP_PROXY` or `HTTPS_PROXY` is set, `opencode attach http://127.0.0.1:<port>` routes its requests (e.g. `GET /config/providers`) through the proxy **even when `NO_PROXY` includes `127.0.0.1`/`localhost`**. This breaks attaching to a local server when a corporate/system proxy is configured. The attach path connects via `createOpencodeClient`, which falls back to the runtime's global `fetch` (`packages/sdk/js/src/v2/client.ts:51-56`) with no proxy handling. Bun's native fetch honors `HTTP(S)_PROXY` but not `NO_PROXY`. The repo already ships a correct `NO_PROXY`-aware resolver (`packages/opencode/src/util/proxy-env.ts`, `getProxyForUrl`/`shouldProxy`), but it's only wired into the OpenAI WebSocket path (`packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/ws.ts:88`) — whose own comment notes "Bun does not apply HTTP(S)_PROXY to WebSockets unless the proxy is supplied explicitly." The HTTP/attach path has no equivalent, and unlike the desktop app (`packages/desktop/src/main/sidecar.ts` `ensureLoopbackNoProxy()`) it does no loopback bypass. ### Steps to reproduce 1. `export HTTPS_PROXY=http://your-proxy:8080` (and/or `HTTP_PROXY`) 2. `export NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost` 3. Start an opencode server, then `opencode attach http://127.0.0.1:<port>` 4. The request to `127.0.0.1` still goes through the proxy instead of connecting directly. ### OpenCode version 1.18.0 (Bun 1.3.14) ### Operating System Linux (WSL2)

signals.title: [FEATURE]: OAuth login for Moonshot / Kimi models (K2 / K3)
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request **Summary** opencode already supports OAuth-based login for some providers (e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI) so users can authenticate with their existing account instead of pasting an API key by hand. I would like the same OAuth login flow for **Moonshot AI / Kimi models** (Kimi K2 / K3). **Which OAuth flow** Authorization Code flow with PKCE, mirroring the existing Anthropic OAuth implementation in opencode (open browser → user authorizes → redirect/callback → exchange code for token). No client secret stored on the user machine; access token refreshed via refresh token. **Expected UX** 1. Run `opencode auth login`. 2. Select `Moonshot / Kimi` from the provider list (next to Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.). 3. Browser opens the Moonshot authorization page; user logs in and approves. 4. opencode receives the callback, stores the token, and refreshes it automatically when it expires — same behavior as the other OAuth providers today. 5. Kimi K2 / K3 models become usable without ever generating or copy-pasting an API key. **Why** - Consistent login experience across providers. - Easier onboarding: no manual API-key creation/copy. - Safer credential handling: refreshable token instead of a long-lived key in plain config. **Open question** Does Moonshot / Kimi currently expose a public OAuth endpoint opencode could integrate with? If not, this may depend on the provider adding OAuth support first. **Not a duplicate** The related issues flagged automatically (#12156, #22408, #37343) are all **closed**. This request is specifically about adding an **OAuth login flow** for Moonshot / Kimi (as exists for Anthropic/OpenAI), not just adding the model or a plain API-key integration.

signals.title: v2 cli: headless commands load OpenTUI and leak native temp files
signals.text: ## Summary OpenCode V2 loads its embedded OpenTUI native library for commands that do not render a TUI, including `--version`, `--help`, `service status`, and `api`. Each process leaves a uniquely named 13.1 MiB `libopentui.so` in the temporary directory, allowing repeated API or diagnostic calls to exhaust `/tmp`. Current V1 loads OpenTUI lazily and does not produce these files for equivalent noninteractive and headless commands. ## Environment - opencode version: installed `0.0.0-next-15760`; also reproduced with `0.0.0-next-15803` and current `0.0.0-next-15806` - OS: Arch Linux, kernel `7.1.2-arch3-1`, x86_64 - Terminal: tmux, `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor` - Shell: `/bin/zsh` - Install/channel: npm package `@opencode-ai/cli`, `next` channel - Active plugins: `goal-mode.ts`, `superpowers.ts`, and `tmux-status.ts`; the minimal `--version` reproduction does not initialize a session or require plugin activity ## Reproduction 1. Create an isolated temporary directory: ```sh probe="$(mktemp -d)" ``` 2. Run a command that cannot render a TUI: ```sh TMPDIR="$probe" BUN_TMPDIR="$probe" opencode2 --version ``` 3. Inspect the directory: ```sh find "$probe" -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '%s %f\n' ``` 4. Repeat the command and inspect the directory again. With `0.0.0-next-15806`, one invocation produces: ```text opencode2 v0.0.0-next-15806 13745312 .9adb78bde7f6fdc7-00000000.so ``` `readelf -d` identifies the extracted file as: ```text SONAME=libopentui.so ``` Each invocation creates another randomly named copy. The installed `next-15760` build also reproduces this with `--help`, `service status`, and `opencode2 api ...`. ## Expected Behavior Commands that do not render terminal UI should not import or initialize OpenTUI. Version, help, service-management, and API commands should not extract the renderer library. This is independent of whether Bun eventually deduplicates or cleans embedded `bun:ffi` libraries: OpenCode should avoid loading its renderer when the selected command cannot use it. ## Actual Behavior Every tested V2 process extracts and retains a separate 13,745,312-byte `libopentui.so`, including `--version`. In one real workload, repeated `opencode2 api` diagnostics accumulated: - 459 complete OpenTUI libraries - 188 zero-byte failed extraction attempts after quota exhaustion - 5.82 GiB of leaked native libraries - Exhaustion of the per-user quota on an 8 GiB `/tmp` tmpfs The file-creation timeline correlated with CLI process starts. During one minute, 77 `opencode2 api` processes started and 77 native libraries appeared. After quota exhaustion, starting the TUI failed with: ```text Failed to initialize OpenTUI render library: Failed to open library "/$bunfs/root/libopentui-h3hyjpa5.so": /$bunfs/root/libopentui-h3hyjpa5.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory ``` Deleting the leaked libraries restored TUI startup. ## Additional Context The current stable V1 release, `opencode 1.18.3`, was tested as a control. These V1 commands leave no extracted native library: ```sh opencode --version opencode run --help opencode serve --help opencode debug paths opencode serve ``` Starting the actual V1 interactive TUI does extract one 13,622,688-byte `libopentui.so`, including after a clean Ctrl-C exit. This confirms that V1 still inherits Bun's extraction leak when OpenTUI is genuinely needed, but it does not amplify it through every headless CLI invocation. The underlying Bun `bun:ffi` extraction issue is already tracked: - https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/30962 - https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/29585 - Proposed Bun fix: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/29587 Related OpenCode reports: - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/28089 - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/21427 This report is specifically about V2 eagerly loading OpenTUI in commands that do not need terminal rendering. Avoiding that import would remove the high-frequency API and diagnostic amplification independently of the pending Bun fix.

signals.title: Global tools globs don't exclude MCP tools from provider requests
signals.text: ### Description The docs say MCP tools can be disabled through the global `tools` key with server-prefix globs (`"mymcpservername_*": false`). On 1.18.3 this has no effect on MCP tools: they are still included in the tools array sent to the provider. I hit this because the Postman remote MCP server (`https://mcp.postman.com/minimal`) exposes a tool `searchPostmanElements` whose input schema uses refs like `#/properties/filters/properties/$and/items/properties/createdBy` instead of `#/$defs/...`. Moonshot rejects the request with: ``` [Moonshot AI] Invalid request: tools.function.parameters is not a valid moonshot flavored json schema, details: <At path 'properties.filters.properties.$and.items.properties.createdBy.$ref': references must start with #/$defs/> ``` Neither `"postman*": false` nor `"*searchPostmanElements": false` in the global `tools` key changes anything; the same 400 comes back. `opencode debug config` shows the tools entry resolved. Disabling the whole server via `mcp.postman.enabled: false` does work, so the only workaround is losing the entire server. ### OpenCode version 1.18.3 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a remote MCP server with a tool schema Moonshot rejects, e.g. Postman minimal (`https://mcp.postman.com/minimal`, needs OAuth) and a Moonshot model: ```json { "model": "openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k3", "tools": { "postman*": false }, "mcp": { "postman": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.postman.com/minimal", "enabled": true } } } ``` 2. `opencode run "hi"` 3. 400 from Moonshot referencing the postman tool's schema path, despite the glob disabling it. Expected: tools matching a disabled glob are excluded from provider requests. ### Operating System macOS 26 (Darwin 25.5.0) ### Terminal n/a (`opencode run`)

signals.title: Silent failure: opencode provider returns 500 errors but client drops response without showing error
signals.text: ## Description When using `opencode/big-pickle` (the built-in opencode provider), intermittent `AI_APICallError: Internal server error` (500) responses cause the agent to silently stop responding. The user sees the spinner ("thinking...") for a while, then the flow cuts with no output, no error message, and no indication anything went wrong. From the logs, I can see the client retries internally (multiple `stream error` entries followed by new `stream` attempts), but after exhausting retries it **silently drops** the response instead of surfacing the error to the user. ## Log evidence Here's a sample from `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`: ``` timestamp=... level=INFO run=eba88ab6 message=stream providerID=opencode modelID=big-pickle session.id=ses_XXX small=false agent=build mode=primary timestamp=... level=INFO run=eba88ab6 message="llm runtime selected" llm.runtime=ai-sdk llm.provider=opencode llm.model=big-pickle timestamp=... level=ERROR run=eba88ab6 message="stream error" providerID=opencode modelID=big-pickle session.id=ses_XXX small=false agent=build mode=primary error.error="AI_APICallError: Internal server error" timestamp=... level=INFO run=eba88ab6 message=stream providerID=opencode modelID=big-pickle ... (retry) timestamp=... level=ERROR run=eba88ab6 message="stream error" ... error.error="AI_APICallError: Internal server error" (again) ``` This pattern repeats 3-6+ times per user message. Sometimes it eventually succeeds, sometimes it silently fails. ## Key observations 1. **The 500 errors are from the opencode provider backend** — not a client-side issue 2. **The `small=true` path (title agent) shows a visible retry error** (`AI_RetryError: Failed after 3 attempts`) 3. **The `small=false` path (build/main agent) fails silently** — no error shown to the user 4. **No `chunkTimeout` is configured for the `opencode` provider** — only `openrouter` has one in my config 5. Related to #37580 (chunkTimeout has no default) but this is a distinct issue: the server actively returns 500s, not a silent stall ## Environment - opencode version: 1.18.4 - OS: Linux (NixOS) - Model: `opencode/big-pickle` - Provider: opencode (built-in) - No custom provider options for the `opencode` provider ## Expected behavior When the provider returns a 500 error and retries are exhausted, opencode should: 1. Show the error to the user (not silently drop it) 2. Or at minimum log a clear "giving up after N retries" message ## Workaround Adding `provider.opencode.options.chunkTimeout` may help with silent stalls, but doesn't address the 500 error handling.

signals.title: bug: /status shows truncated name for local file:// plugins on Windows
signals.text: ### Description On Windows, the /status dialog shows local file:// config plugins with a truncated name. A plugin at C:\Users\me\.config\opencode\plugins\superpowers.js is displayed as "C:\Users\me" instead of "superpowers". The name is derived in DialogStatus by splitting the fileURLToPath() result on "/", which does not split Windows backslash paths. The whole path becomes the "filename", and filename.split(".")[0] then truncates it at the first dot in the path. ### Plugins oh-my-openagent@latest ### OpenCode version 1.18.11 ### Steps to reproduce 1. On Windows, place any local plugin at %USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\plugins\<name>.js 2. Run opencode and open the /status dialog 3. The plugin appears as "C:\Users\<username>" (truncated at the first dot of the path) instead of the plugin file name ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows Terminal

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Add configurable TUI keybind for auto-approve permissions
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request The TUI supports toggling auto-approve permissions through the `permission.mode` command added in #33279, but that command cannot currently be assigned a key in `tui.json`. #7928 requested broader permission-mode cycling without implementing a keybind. Open PR #12633 is related, but proposes separate persisted state, a default `Shift+Tab` binding, edit-only behavior, and permission-default changes. Add `app_toggle_auto_approve_permissions` with a default of `none`, map it to the existing `permission.mode` command, and register that command with the global TUI bindings. This adds configuration without changing permission behavior, persistence, or default shortcuts. Keeping the default unbound preserves current behavior while allowing users to opt in. Process: human-directed and reviewed, with agentic assistance from openai/gpt-5.6-sol/high.

signals.title: unstable internet leaves opencode in stuck state
signals.text: ### Description I have unstable internet, which drops packets every few hours. This causes opencode to get stuck in a state where it doesn't error out. It just seems to stall. Permanently saying "Esc to interrupt" and nothing happening. Ive tried to make a watchdog script, but that stalls when opencode stalls. Some info from gemini: When a network connection drops mid-stream (specifically a silent TCP drop or packet loss without an explicit FIN or RST packet from the server), OpenCode hangs indefinitely in the streaming/busy state. The TUI remains stuck displaying "ESC to interrupt", no incoming tokens are rendered, and no request timeout is triggered. Furthermore, the process hangs or blocks the Node/Bun event loop during this state, preventing internal JavaScript plugin hooks or external IPC/events from recovering or receiving command signals. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.18.11 ### Steps to reproduce Start an interactive session in opencode. Submit a prompt that generates a multi-second response. Mid-stream, simulate a silent network drop (e.g., disable Wi-Fi, pull Ethernet cable). Observe OpenCode's behavior. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System linux ### Terminal kde teminal

signals.title: `deepseek-v4-flash-free` (zen free tier): stream drops the final text delta before `tool_calls`; non-streaming is complete
signals.text: ### Description `deepseek-v4-flash-free` via `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions` (free tier) drops the **final text delta before `tool_calls`** from streamed responses: the sentence before the tool call ends mid-word, no error, `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. The same request with `stream: false` returns the complete text. Non-deterministic — identical requests sometimes complete. ### Plugins None — raw HTTP, no client SDK involved. ### OpenCode version N/A (API-level; also reproduced via Vercel AI SDK `streamText`, pi's SDK `streamSimple`, and headless `opencode run`) ### Steps to reproduce `repro.sh` — curl + python3, no other deps: ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Usage: ./repro.sh [runs] set -u KEY="${OPENCODE_API_KEY:-public}" # free tier accepts "public" N="${1:-8}" PHRASE="The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog" req() { # $1 = stream(true/false) curl -sS --max-time 90 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"deepseek-v4-flash-free\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Say exactly '$PHRASE' then call the tool get_time with an empty object.\"}],\"stream\":$1,\"tools\":[{\"type\":\"function\",\"function\":{\"name\":\"get_time\",\"parameters\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{}}}}]}" \ "https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions" } stream_text() { python3 -c ' import sys, json text = "" for line in sys.stdin: line = line.strip() if not line.startswith("data:"): continue p = line[5:].strip() if p == "[DONE]": continue try: o = json.loads(p) except Exception: continue for c in o.get("choices", []): d = c.get("delta") or {} if isinstance(d.get("content"), str): text += d["content"] print(text)' } trunc=0 for i in $(seq 1 "$N"); do body=$(req true) id=$(printf '%s' "$body" | grep -o '"id":"[^"]*"' | head -1 | cut -d'"' -f4) text=$(printf '%s' "$body" | stream_text) if [[ "$text" == *"lazy dog"* ]]; then s="complete" elif [[ "$text" == *"fox"* ]]; then s="TRUNCATED"; trunc=$((trunc+1)) else s="no-text"; fi printf 'run %2d id=%-22s %-9s ...%s\n' "$i" "${id:0:22}" "$s" "${text: -32}" sleep 0.3 done echo echo "streaming: $trunc/$N truncated (expected tail: '$PHRASE')" echo "--- non-streaming control (stream:false) ---" req false | python3 -c 'import sys,json; o=json.load(sys.stdin); print("content:", o["choices"][0]["message"]["content"])' ``` ### Screenshot and/or share link Output of one run: ``` run 1 id=router-c651e84ac345a25 TRUNCATED ...e quick brown fox jumps over the run 2 id=router-4b3abcc145d862d TRUNCATED ...e quick brown fox jumps over the run 3 id=router-59f37695f6c301f TRUNCATED ... run 4 id=router-906ca39fd5009d0 TRUNCATED ...e quick brown fox jumps over the run 5 id=router-4f990f930cbd9cd TRUNCATED ...e quick brown fox jumps over the run 6 id=b7ea5f8c-1b71-4d5a-9d3 complete ...rown fox jumps over the lazy dog run 7 id=router-87d80b13af7041b TRUNCATED ...e quick brown fox jumps over the run 8 id=router-b0831d8d0f852b9 TRUNCATED ...e quick brown fox jumps over the streaming: 7/8 truncated (expected tail: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog') --- non-streaming control (stream:false) --- content: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog ``` Second run: `streaming: 6/6 truncated`, non-streaming control complete. ### Operating System Linux (container); client-independent ### Terminal N/A ### Additional evidence - Raw SSE of a truncated run (verbatim capture, no parser): `content='The'` → `content=' quick brown fox jumps over the'` (last content delta) → `tool_calls` → `finish_reason: tool_calls` → `[DONE]`. The tail `' lazy dog'` never appears as a content delta. The full sentence IS present in the same stream's `reasoning_content` deltas and in the `stream: false` response — the model generated it; the SSE dropped it. - Truncation correlates with the response chunk `id` prefix. Across ~100 streamed runs with tools: every truncated response had a `router-*` id; `uuid`-prefixed responses were always complete. In the systematic matrix: 28/33 `router-*` runs truncated (~85%), 0/14 `uuid` runs. - Request parameters don't change it: reproduced with/without `temperature`, `x-opencode-session`, `stream_options`, `max_tokens`, and different tool-schema shapes. - Not a parsing artifact: with the Vercel AI SDK and pi's SDK, the SDK's emitted text matched the captured raw bytes byte-for-byte (both truncated). Related: #40888 (streaming + tools truncated on the Go tier), #40176 (deepseek-v4-flash on Go drops the tool call after text — same text↔tool transition defect, opposite side).

signals.title: Desktop: renaming a project folder breaks the project binding (phantom project, rename ignored, sessions silently fall back to global)
signals.text: ### Description On OpenCode Desktop (v1.18.14, macOS arm64), renaming a project **folder in Finder** (outside OpenCode) permanently breaks the project↔directory binding. The app keeps a phantom project whose `worktree`/`project_directory` point to non-existent paths, the project display name cannot be changed, and new sessions silently fall back to the `global` project (or fail to start when clicking the phantom). ### To Reproduce 1. Create a project in OpenCode Desktop (folder `A`). Rename the project in-app to e.g. "DarkRain" → Save. 2. Rename folder `A` → `B` in Finder, then rename the project in-app → **name does not change**. 3. Rename folder `B` → `C` in Finder. Delete the project in-app, then create a new project selecting folder `C` → **the name auto-reverts to the original project name**, and a phantom entry pointing at a dead path still shows in the sidebar. 4. Click that phantom project and start a conversation → **no output, no session is created**. ### Expected behavior - Renaming the project folder in Finder should either re-associate the same project (follow the rename) or the app should detect the stale record and clean it up / relink it. - In-app project rename should always persist. - Recreating a project on a new path must not reuse the stale DB record. ### Environment - OpenCode Desktop 1.18.14 - macOS arm64 - SQLite storage at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` ### Root cause (from bundled code) - `Project.fromDirectory` does an **exact-match** lookup of the directory (via `projectV2.resolve` + `project_directory`). After a Finder rename the new path has no row, so it silently resolves to the `global` project (`worktree = "/"`, per `node-CU9-BMuP.js` `fromDirectory`). - `ProjectCopy.refresh` only deletes stored directory rows whose paths no longer exist; it never adopts a renamed folder as the same project, so the old `project.worktree` / `project_directory.directory` stay stale. - The edit-project dialog (`edit-project.js`) special-cases the `global` project: for it the save path only calls `sync.project.meta(...)` (silent, no DB `project` row), which is why renames appear to do nothing. Observed DB state after the sequence above: ``` project: cfdc78b7… name=DarkRain worktree=/old/A (deleted) project_directory: cfdc78b7… /old/B (deleted) session for folder C: project_id=global ``` The snapshot (`.local/share/opencode/snapshot/<projectID>`) also keeps a git worktree config pointing at the deleted path. ### Related issues - #38478 (project display name changes ignored in NewLayout) - #35851 (deleting and re-adding a project with a different path reuses stale worktree) - #40336 / #39471 (sessions fail / empty response when saved directory no longer exists) - #35240 (stale `project.worktree` after folder rename) --- ## 中文版描述 ### 问题描述 OpenCode Desktop (v1.18.14, macOS arm64) 中，在 Finder 里直接重命名项目文件夹（OpenCode 之外的操作）会永久破坏"项目 ↔ 目录"的绑定：应用里留下一个幽灵项目，其 `worktree`/`project_directory` 指向已不存在的路径；项目显示名无法修改；新会话会静默回退到 `global` 项目（点击幽灵项目发起会话则直接无响应）。 ### 复现步骤 1. 在 OpenCode Desktop 新建项目（文件夹 `A`），在应用内把项目改名为如 "DarkRain" → 保存。 2. 在 Finder 里把文件夹 `A` 改名为 `B`，然后在应用内改名项目 → **名称不变化**。 3. 在 Finder 里把文件夹 `B` 改名为 `C`。在应用内删除该项目，再新建项目并选择文件夹 `C` → **名称自动变回最初的项目名**，侧边栏仍显示一个指向死路径的幽灵条目。 4. 点击该幽灵项目发起对话 → **无任何输出，不创建会话**。 ### 预期行为 - 在 Finder 中重命名项目文件夹后，应用应能重新关联同一项目（跟随改名），或检测到失效记录并清理/重新关联。 - 应用内修改项目名称应始终生效。 - 在新路径重建项目时，不得复用旧的数据库残留记录。 ### 环境 - OpenCode Desktop 1.18.14 - macOS arm64 - 数据存储：`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`（SQLite） ### 根因分析（来自打包代码） - `Project.fromDirectory` 对目录做**精确匹配**（通过 `projectV2.resolve` + `project_directory`）。Finder 改名后新路径无对应记录，便静默降级到 `global` 项目（`worktree = "/"`，见 `node-CU9-BMuP.js` 的 `fromDirectory`）。 - `ProjectCopy.refresh` 只会删除路径已不存在的目录记录，**从不**把改名后的新目录重新关联为同一项目，导致 `project.worktree` / `project_directory.directory` 一直残留旧路径。 - 编辑项目对话框（`edit-project.js`）对 `global` 项目做了特判：保存时只调用 `sync.project.meta(...)`（静默，不写 `project` 表），这就是改名看起来"没生效"的原因。 上述操作序列后观察到的数据库状态： ``` project: cfdc78b7… name=DarkRain worktree=/old/A (已删除) project_directory: cfdc78b7… /old/B (已删除) 文件夹 C 的会话: project_id=global ``` 快照目录（`.local/share/opencode/snapshot/<projectID>`）中的 git worktree 配置同样指向已删除的路径。

signals.title: [BUG]: Manually selected model resets to config default on primary-agent switch (Tab) — regression of #4344
signals.text: ### Description On v1.18.15, a model selected via `/models` does not persist across primary-agent switches (Tab build↔plan). Re-entering an agent I had manually switched re-applies the configured default and discards my pick. This is the symptom fixed in #4344 / PR #4514, recurring on 1.18.15. In daily use I switch models per-task via `/models`, so pinning one model in config isn't a viable workaround — I depend on the runtime pick persisting. **Expected:** A manual `/models` pick persists per-agent across activations (ideally for the session) until I change it. Re-entering an agent should restore that agent's last-selected model, not the config default. **Actual:** Re-entering a primary agent re-applies the config default and discards the override. Separately, compaction has also been reported to reset the model/agent (#4546). **Logs** — within one agent the pick holds across many turns; it's lost specifically on primary-agent switch / re-entry. (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`, session `ses_020510ee…`; all entries `small=false`.) | time (UTC) | agent | model | event | |---|---|---|---| | 04:43:32 | plan | zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2 | session created; plan runs my pick — held for ~20 min across many turns (through 05:04) | | 05:05:35 | build | kimi-for-coding/k3-256k | Tab → build; runs the config default, not my pick | | 05:15:55 | build | zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2 | re-selected glm-5.2 in build | | 05:21:54 | plan | kimi-for-coding/k3-256k | Tab back → plan; the 04:43 pick is gone (reverted to config default) | | 05:28:02 | plan | zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2 | re-selected glm-5.2 in plan, again | Verbatim, same session, same agent — model flipped with no selection in between (only a Tab detour into build and back): ``` 2026-08-08T04:43:32.082Z level=INFO message=stream providerID=zai-coding-plan modelID=glm-5.2 session.id=ses_020510ee0ffeHV1Bvoci8LgJYb small=false agent=plan 2026-08-08T05:21:54.199Z level=INFO message=stream providerID=kimi-for-coding modelID=k3-256k session.id=ses_020510ee0ffeHV1Bvoci8LgJYb small=false agent=plan ``` **Related:** #4344 (same symptom, fixed via #4514 — regressed), #39319 (pick reverts after every turn — overlapping root cause), #4546 (compaction resets model/agent), open PRs #39322, #40604. ### Plugins N/A ### OpenCode version 1.18.15 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Config: `"model": "kimi-for-coding/k3-256k"` (global default). No explicit model on build/plan. 2. `/models` → select `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2` in the plan agent. 3. Work a few turns in plan → runs on glm-5.2 ✓ (pick holds within the agent). 4. Tab → build → runs `kimi-for-coding/k3-256k` (config default). 5. Re-select glm-5.2 in build → works. 6. Tab back → plan → now on `kimi-for-coding/k3-256k`. The step-2 pick is gone. ### Screenshot and/or share link ### Operating System macOS (Apple Silicon) ### Terminal kitty

signals.title: Session silently stops on empty LLM response (finish: unknown, 0 tokens)
signals.text: ## Description When the model provider returns an **empty completion** (0 tokens, no text/reasoning/tool output, finish reason maps to `unknown`), opencode treats it as a normal completed turn: - the session loop exits silently (`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts` breaks on any finish that isn't `tool-calls`) - no error is surfaced to the user, no retry happens - the conversation appears to "suddenly stop" mid-task Observed with the opencode-go gateway (deepseek-v4-flash) returning an empty response: the session went idle with the last assistant message recorded as `finish: unknown` with 0 tokens. ## Repro - Provider returns an SSE stream with no content/tool deltas and an unknown finish reason. - After processing, the loop exits and the session goes idle with no error. ## Expected An empty response should be retried (or surfaced as an error), not silently treated as a completed turn. Related: #40531 (upstream PR with the same fix, currently conflicting with dev).

signals.title: V2 AI package: audit and close critical protocol correctness gaps
signals.text: ## Summary Track correctness and parity gaps in the V2 native `@opencode-ai/ai` package by wire protocol. This is **not** a feature wishlist. It excludes citations, provider-hosted tools, and unsupported optional capabilities. Scope is critical flow integrity: normalization, ordering, streamed-state settlement, persistence/replay, request intent, terminal outcomes, transport classification, and accounting. ## Anthropic Messages (`/v1/messages`) ### P0 — tool/result integrity - [ ] **Coalesce parallel tool results into the immediately following user turn.** V2 currently lowers `assistant[tool_use A, tool_use B]` into `user[result A]`, `user[result B]`. Reproduced end-to-end through `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` on `/zen/go/v1/messages`; result B arrives one message too late. Official DeepSeek error: ``Each `tool_use` block must have a corresponding `tool_result` block in the next message.`` Coalescing both results makes the same run succeed. - [ ] **Settle or fail pending streamed tool calls at `message_stop`.** Native only emits a call on `content_block_stop`; terminal `message_stop` can report success while pending tool state is silently dropped. ### P0 — output and continuation integrity - [ ] **Preserve Anthropic compaction blocks and deltas.** Native accepts unknown block types structurally but silently drops compaction content from output and persisted history. - [ ] **Map compaction stop reasons and retain continuation state** rather than converting them to `unknown`. ### P1 — request normalization - [ ] **Normalize thinking budgets and answer-token semantics.** Enforce minimum budget and `budget < max_tokens`; account for thinking tokens when canonical `maxTokens` represents answer budget. - [ ] **Remove incompatible thinking/sampling combinations.** Do not forward invalid combinations of enabled thinking, `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k`. - [ ] **Add `anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-2026-04-07`** whenever native lowering emits a mid-conversation system-role message. - [ ] **Do not silently downgrade supported system updates into wrapped user text.** Capability and negotiation should be explicit. - [ ] **Never replay unsigned visible `thinking` blocks.** Replay valid signed/redacted Anthropic state or fail/lower locally. - [ ] **Trim/normalize final assistant prefill whitespace** where Anthropic requires it. - [ ] **Reject, serialize, or explicitly warn for every accepted provider option.** Open-ended options currently type-check while lowering reads only `thinking` and `effort`; parallel-tool controls and request metadata can silently vanish. ### P1 — stream and accounting integrity - [ ] **Validate lifecycle ordering:** require `message_start`, reject duplicate/out-of-order starts, reject events after terminal completion, and settle open fragments at EOF. - [ ] **Aggregate raw usage once at terminal completion**, including split start/delta counters and compaction/advisor/fallback iterations. Existing tracker: #40713. - [ ] **Retain response identity and stop diagnostics:** actual served model, response ID, initial content snapshot, stop/refusal details, and complete provider metadata. ## Bedrock Converse ### P0 — tool/result integrity - [ ] **Coalesce parallel tool results into one immediately following Bedrock user turn.** Same deterministic failure class as Anthropic Messages; existing report: #41445. - [ ] **Normalize adjacent user/tool messages generally** so synthetic, compaction, and ordinary user content cannot violate Converse role/turn requirements. ### P1 — replay safety - [ ] **Keep Bedrock/Anthropic thought and tool metadata bound to compatible route origin.** Do not replay incompatible Anthropic signatures or foreign protocol state after model/provider switches. Related: #34996 and #35827. ## OpenAI Chat Completions (`/v1/chat/completions`) ### P0 — output integrity - [ ] **Preserve streamed `delta.refusal`.** Native accepts the field structurally but ignores it, allowing a refusal to become an empty successful response and disappear from persisted history. ### P0 — tool integrity - [ ] **Classify and retain truncated tool arguments correctly.** Distinguish provider truncation, transport interruption, and adapter premature finalization; never execute malformed input; add bounded safe recovery. Existing report: #36766. ### P1 — stream integrity - [ ] **Require valid terminal lifecycle state** rather than treating partial content/tool buffers as clean completion. ## OpenAI Responses (`/v1/responses`) ### P0 — tool integrity - [ ] **Finalize or fail pending function calls when `response.completed` arrives without `response.output_item.done`.** Current behavior can leave a tool permanently pending. Existing deterministic report: #37159. - [ ] **Retain terminal provider diagnostics for truncated argument buffers**, including whether the stream ended normally, finish state, and bounded byte counts. Related: #36766. ### P0 — output integrity - [ ] **Preserve `response.refusal.delta` and `response.refusal.done`.** Native ignores them, yields an empty successful response, and cannot replay the refusal. - [ ] **Do not mark reasoning-only output with no text/refusal/tool call as successful.** Existing production report: #37372. ### P1 — reasoning lifecycle - [ ] **Normalize overlapping reasoning fragments** instead of crashing the execution as `unknown`. Existing report: #36892. - [ ] **Finalize or explicitly interrupt every open reasoning/text fragment before response completion.** ## Gemini `generateContent` ### P0 — function-call integrity - [ ] **Support official incremental function arguments (`partialArgs` / `willContinue`).** Native currently requires complete `name + args` in each frame, so valid Gemini streams fail schema decoding before accumulation. - [ ] **Normalize omitted zero-argument call input to `{}`.** A valid `functionCall: { name: "ping" }` currently fails decoding. ### P0 — safety outcome integrity - [ ] **Preserve prompt-level safety blocks (`promptFeedback.blockReason`) as a typed terminal outcome.** Candidate-less blocked prompts currently lose the safety reason and become generic incomplete-stream failures. ### P1 — replay safety - [ ] **Bind Gemini thought signatures and native metadata to compatible route origin.** Do not replay foreign or stale thought state after protocol/model switches. Related: #34996 and #35827. ## Shared V2 runner/history layer ### P0 — successful execution contract - [ ] **A successful execution must contain usable text, a refusal, or completed tool work.** Token usage or a provider `stop` alone is insufficient. Existing report: #37372. - [ ] **Every announced local tool call must settle exactly once before its owning step terminates.** ### P1 — persistence and replay - [ ] **Bind opaque provider metadata to resolved protocol origin**, not only the configured provider/model reference. Existing trackers: #34996 and #35827. - [ ] **Distinguish normally ended fragments from cleanup-interrupted text, reasoning, and tool input.** Existing tracker: #36874. - [ ] **Do not persist interrupted raw tool input as an executable call.** ### P1 — request intent - [ ] **Keep variants effective after native package overrides.** Confirmed end-to-end: `#low`, `#high`, and `#max` for `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` through native Anthropic produced identical request bodies with no effort/thinking field. - [ ] **Every accepted request option must be serialized, explicitly ignored with a warning, or rejected locally.** ### P1 — transport and error classification - [ ] **Classify response-body resets as transport failures, not invalid model output**, and retain a sanitized low-level cause. Existing report: #39326. - [ ] **Before output starts, preserve bounded transport retry behavior.** After output/tool side effects begin, expose an explicit interrupted-step recovery path rather than silently retrying. - [ ] **Keep child-session stream failures visible to the parent** so dropped subagent work can be restarted. ## Protocol conformance matrix Add fixtures and differential tests for every native protocol covering: 1. Single, sequential, and parallel tool calls. 2. Adjacent user/tool/synthetic/system messages. 3. Missing, duplicate, reordered, and truncated stream boundaries. 4. Pending tools/fragments at every terminal event. 5. Text, refusal, safety block, content filter, empty response, and normal stop outcomes. 6. Same-origin replay and incompatible provider/model/protocol switching. 7. Request options and model variants at the actual wire body/header boundary. 8. Split streaming usage, cache counters, executor iterations, and fallback accounting. 9. Transport reset before output, during reasoning/text, during tool input, and after tool execution. ## Suggested implementation order 1. Anthropic Messages and Bedrock parallel-result normalization. 2. Pending tool settlement across Anthropic, Responses, Chat, and Gemini. 3. Refusal, safety, and empty-success outcome invariants. 4. Replay provenance and interrupted-fragment semantics. 5. Request option/variant normalization. 6. Transport classification and usage aggregation.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Allow version ranges when connecting to the background service
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Right now, `Service.discover()` and `Service.ensure()` can require an exact OpenCode version, but they cannot accept a compatible range. This is awkward for apps that use OpenCode as an external service. They may work with several compatible releases, but currently have to either require one exact version or skip version checking completely. Could these APIs support a `versionRange` option using normal npm semver syntax? ```ts await Service.ensure({ versionRange: ">=2.0.0 <3.0.0", }) ``` The existing `version` option could stay as-is for exact matching, with `version` and `versionRange` being mutually exclusive. It would also be useful for prerelease versions to work with these ranges. I already have an implementation and tests ready locally, but I have not opened a PR because the contributing guide asks people to discuss new functionality in an issue first. If this sounds like a useful addition, I'd be happy to open the PR.

signals.title: TUI: text disappears during LLM streaming, main thread stuck in timerfd busy-loop (TreeSitter worker stack overflow)
signals.text: ### Description ## TL;DR During LLM streaming, the syntax highlighting worker crashes with a WASM stack overflow in tree-sitter's `captures()`. Because the streaming code path doesn't update the text buffer independently of the highlight result, a worker crash leaves the displayed code frozen at an arbitrary position. The crash is content-deterministic — the same deeply-nested code triggers the same AST shape, which triggers the same stack overflow — so resume does not help if the same code block is re-rendered. ## Related issues This is the first report to identify the root cause (TreeSitter worker WASM stack overflow). Previous reports described the same or overlapping symptoms but did not identify the cause: - #15388 — TUI garbled/corrupted after long output (closed as not planned, same symptom: restart restores rendering) - #3905 — Message history randomly flickers/disappears (closed, tagged `opentui`) - #3935 — Unstable TUI, disappearing content area (closed, same symptom cluster) - #23914 — TUI text becomes garbled (no developer response) - #17793 — TUI display corruption regression on v1.2.27 (regression of #16351 fix) - #32335 — `opencode run` processes don't exit after completing work (same "event loop stuck" symptom) - #7301 — Logs sent via `client.app.log()` not visible with `--print-logs` (related logging visibility issue) ## Reproduction Send this prompt to the LLM in the opencode TUI: ``` Please write a complete TypeScript web server project. I need: 1. A main server file with nested middleware (at least 5 levels of composition) 2. A database layer with nested query builders 3. A routing configuration with nested route groups 4. Type definitions with deeply nested generics 5. Utility functions with complex type inference Output each file as a separate ```ts code block. Make each file at least 100 lines. Use deeply nested object literals, chained method calls, and complex type unions. ``` The crash is triggered by deeply nested code structures in the LLM's response. It depends on the specific code the LLM generates, so not every run will trigger it. In our testing, it triggered on the first attempt with this prompt — but since the crash depends on the exact AST shape of the generated code, reproducibility will vary. Once triggered, the same session content will crash deterministically on every subsequent render. ## What happens ### Original observation (during normal use) During LLM streaming, **some text on the screen suddenly disappears**. The TUI is still responsive — the user can still type and interact — but certain characters are gone. Exiting the session and resuming **appeared** to restore the rendering — but as discovered during reproduction, this was only because the problematic code block was not immediately re-rendered. When the same content is displayed again, the crash recurs deterministically. This happened three times in a single day of normal use, including once in a brand-new session (not a resume), ruling out it being a random fluke or tied to a specific session's history. **Ruled out via strace**: No user interrupt keys (fd 22 = real stdin shows 0 inputs), no SIGHUP, no SIGWINCH, no terminal resize. The issue is purely in the rendering layer — the underlying data is intact. `strace` recording revealed the cause: the worker thread was generating **thousands of SIGSEGV** — `SEGV_ACCERR` with addresses steadily decreasing, the classic signature of a stack overflow hitting the guard page: | | First time | Second time | Third time | |---|---|---|---| | Session type | Original | Resumed | **Brand new** | | SIGSEGV count | 5,961 | 4,932 | 16,378 | | Duration | ~3.5 min | ~3.2 min | ~5.3 min | | Error type | `SEGV_ACCERR` | `SEGV_ACCERR` | `SEGV_ACCERR` | | Address pattern | Decreasing | Decreasing | Decreasing | **These are not one crash.** Each SIGSEGV represents a separate worker crash-and-recreate cycle (see Root Cause §4). The worker crashes, gets recreated, receives the same content, and crashes again — thousands of times over several minutes. After the worker crashes, the main thread gets stuck in a timerfd busy-loop (reading fd 7 and fd 8 every second), spinning endlessly even after opencode.log shows all session loops have ended (`exiting loop`). ### Finding during reproduction When reproducing with the prompt above, an additional symptom became clear: the code is not just "disappearing" — it is **frozen mid-stream at an arbitrary position**, with everything after that point missing. And **resume does not fix it**: the code stays truncated at the exact same position, because the same code content triggers the same crash. Notably, `TreeSitter`, `highlighting failed`, `falling back` appear **0 times** in all log files. This is because `@opentui/core`'s `ConsoleCapture` intercepts all `console.warn` / `console.error` calls, storing them only in memory, never writing to any log file (see Root Cause §5). ## Environment - opencode: v1.18.15 - `@opentui/core`: 0.4.5 - `web-tree-sitter`: 0.25.10 - OS: Linux 6.8.0-48-generic (x86_64) - This issue is not new to v1.18.15 — the same symptom has been observed in older versions, but `ConsoleCapture` hides all warnings, so there was never enough evidence to report it. ## Root cause A cascading failure with five key links. Source references are from `@opentui/core@0.4.5` (locate by function name, not line number). ### 1. Text rendering is coupled to highlighting during streaming (why text freezes) The `CodeRenderable.content` setter in streaming mode only updates `_content` (in-memory) and does **not** update `textBuffer` (the screen). The `textBuffer` is only updated when `startHighlight()` succeeds. If highlighting hangs, the screen freezes. ```typescript // CodeRenderable.content setter (packages/core/src/renderables/Code.ts) set content(value: string) { if (this._content !== value) { this._content = value this._highlightsDirty = true if (this._streaming && this._filetype && !this._drawUnstyledText) { this.requestRender() return // ← returns WITHOUT updating textBuffer } this.textBuffer.setText(value) // ← only reached in non-streaming mode } } ``` `textBuffer` is only updated inside `startHighlight()`, after `await this._treeSitterClient.highlightOnce(content, filetype)` resolves. If that Promise hangs, the catch block (which falls back to plain text) **never executes**: ```typescript // CodeRenderable.startHighlight() (Code.ts) private async startHighlight(): Promise<void> { const result = await this._treeSitterClient.highlightOnce(content, filetype) // ↑ if this hangs, everything below never runs this.textBuffer.setStyledText(styledText) // ← only way textBuffer gets updated // ... } catch (error) { this.textBuffer.setText(content) // ← fallback, only runs if Promise rejects } ``` ### 2. No debounce on streaming highlights (trigger condition) Every token triggers the full highlight pipeline — `content` setter → `renderSelf()` → `startHighlight()` → `highlightOnce()` → `postMessage` to worker. `TreeSitterClient` has a `DebounceController` but `highlightOnce()` bypasses it entirely. At 30fps render rate, this means up to 30 full highlight requests per second, each sending the complete accumulated content. ### 3. WASM `captures()` has no safeguards (the crash) In the worker, `ParserWorker.handleOneShotHighlight()` (`packages/core/src/lib/tree-sitter/parser.worker.ts`) calls `query.captures(tree.rootNode)`, which is tree-sitter's C code compiled to WASM using **recursion** to traverse the AST. Deep nesting → WASM stack overflow → hard abort (emscripten `abort()`). There is only `try/finally`, no `catch` — and WASM stack overflow is a hard abort that JS try/catch cannot reliably intercept. ### 4. Worker crash loop — no `on("exit")` handler, no circuit breaker (why it repeats thousands of times) The `NodeWorkerShim` constructor (`packages/core/src/platform/worker.ts`) only attaches `on("message")` and `on("error")`: ```typescript // NodeWorkerShim constructor (platform/worker.ts) this.worker = new node.Worker(createWorkerBootstrapSource(resolvedSpecifier), { eval: true, type: "module", name: options.name, // no resourceLimits, no stackSizeMb }) this.worker.on("message", this.handleMessage) this.worker.on("error", this.handleError) // no on("exit")! no on("close")! ``` A search of the published `@opentui/core@0.4.5` package source confirms no `worker.on("exit")` exists anywhere. During a WASM abort, the worker thread dies outright, and the JS `error` event **may not be dispatched**. If `onerror` doesn't fire, `handleWorkerFailure` never runs, `rejectPendingRequests` never runs, and the `highlightOnce()` Promise **never settles** — neither resolves nor rejects. This is why the fallback catch block is unreachable. Additionally, `handleWorkerFailure` (`packages/core/src/lib/tree-sitter/client.ts`) only sets `this.initialized = false` — it does **not** destroy the client and has no circuit breaker. The next `highlightOnce()` call lazily re-creates a new worker via `initialize()`, which crashes again on the same content. **This is the crash loop.** The thousands of SIGSEGVs in the strace data (5,961 / 4,932 / 16,378) are not one crash generating many signals — they are thousands of separate crash-recreate-crash cycles, each one spawning a new worker that immediately dies on the same content. This loop continues for minutes until the streaming ends or the session is exited. ### 5. ConsoleCapture hides all warnings (why it was never reported) `TerminalConsoleCache.overrideConsoleMethods()` (`packages/core/src/console.ts`) replaces all `console.warn` / `console.error` with in-memory storage only (max 1000 entries). The warnings that `startHighlight()`'s catch block would produce are invisible in all log files. This is why the issue has existed across multiple versions but was never reported — there was simply no evidence available to users. ### Crash flow ``` LLM streams token → content setter (updates _content only, NOT textBuffer) → startHighlight() → highlightOnce() → worker.postMessage(ONESHOT_HIGHLIGHT) → worker: parser.parse() → captures(rootNode) → WASM stack overflow → worker dies If onerror fires (not guaranteed with WASM abort): → handleWorkerFailure → rejectPendingRequests → Promise rejects → catch block runs → textBuffer.setText(content) → plain text fallback ✓ → but client not destroyed, no circuit breaker → next token recreates worker → crash again (crash loop) If onerror does NOT fire (observed in production): → Promise never settles → startHighlight() hangs forever → textBuffer frozen → code truncated mid-stream → worker never terminated → timerfd busy-loop Resume → same content → same crash → code still truncated (content-deterministic) ``` ## Suggested fixes Ordered by impact: 1. **Always update `textBuffer` in the `content` setter** — even in streaming mode, call `this.textBuffer.setText(value)` before `return`. This ensures text is always visible even if highlighting fails or hangs. The styled highlight can upgrade the display later when it succeeds. (This means text may briefly appear unstyled before highlighting completes — a minor visual tradeoff compared to text being completely invisible.) 2. **Add a timeout to `highlightOnce()`** — reject the Promise after N seconds so the catch block can run even when both `onerror` and `on("exit")` fail to fire. 3. **Add `on("exit")` handler to `NodeWorkerShim`** — call `handleWorkerFailure` on worker exit, so cleanup (including `rejectPendingRequests`) happens even when WASM abort prevents `onerror` from firing. 4. **Add a circuit breaker to `handleWorkerFailure`** — after N consecutive failures on the same content, stop re-creating the worker and permanently fall back to plain text for that code block. This is essential because the crash is content-deterministic: without this, the crash loop repeats indefinitely. 5. **Add debounce to `highlightOnce()`** — use the existing `DebounceController` (already used by `resetBuffer()`). Reduces crash frequency during streaming but does not prevent the crash (the crash-inducing content will eventually be sent). 6. **Add depth limit or timeout to `captures()`** — or limit content size / nesting depth sent to the worker. Prevents the crash itself. 7. **Set `stackSizeMb` in Worker options** — `resourceLimits: { stackSizeMb: 8 }`. Only delays the crash (deeper nesting needed to trigger), doesn't fix the root cause. 8. **Write WARN/ERROR to log files** — in `TerminalConsoleCache.appendToConsole`, at least write WARN/ERROR level messages to an external log file so issues are diagnosable without strace. <details> <summary>How we collected this evidence</summary> `ConsoleCapture` intercepts all `console.warn` / `console.error`, so opencode's own logs contained zero traces. To work around this, we used a shell wrapper to record two types of low-level logs simultaneously: 1. **`script` (PTY recording)** — records all bytes opencode outputs to the terminal (stdout + stderr), including the full TUI rendering sequence. Lets us verify what was actually displayed and which text was missing. 2. **`strace -f -e trace=read` (syscall recording)** — records all `read` syscalls from the process and all child threads. Lets us observe SIGSEGV, signals, and which fds were read at what time (especially fd 22 = real stdin, to confirm the user pressed no interrupt keys). By cross-referencing the two, we pinpointed the worker stack overflow and the main thread busy-loop despite opencode's own logs having zero traces. </details> ### Plugins N/A ### OpenCode version v1.18.15 ### Steps to reproduce As above ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A ### Operating System Linux 6.8.0-48-generic (x86_64) ### Terminal N/A

signals.title: Auto-updater breaks global npm install: stub binary + missing shims, hung npm processes left behind
signals.text: ## Bug Report: Auto-updater can permanently break the global install (stub binary + missing shims), and hung `npm install` processes keep running **Environment:** Windows 11 (10.0.26200), node v24.15.0, npm 11.12.1, opencode installed via `npm install -g opencode-ai` ### Summary On every startup, opencode spawns a **background** `npm install -g opencode-ai@<latest>` (the parent process of the npm process is the opencode.exe process itself). When the npm registry is unreachable/flaky (e.g. `ECONNRESET`), this install **hangs for 15+ minutes** and, when it finally progresses, it can leave the global installation in a broken state: 1. npm extracts the new tarball, which **overwrites `bin/opencode.exe` (the currently running binary!) with the 479-byte placeholder stub** that says "Error: opencode-ai's postinstall script was not run." 2. npm removes the old bin shims (`opencode`, `opencode.cmd`, `opencode.ps1`) before creating new ones - the failed install leaves only `.opencode-*` temp files behind. 3. The postinstall then fails with `EBUSY: resource busy or locked` because the still-running opencode processes hold the old binary file (Windows locks running executables) - the install rolls back, but the shims are never recreated and the stub stays in place. ### Result - `opencode` is no longer recognized in new terminal sessions (command not found). - Even invoking the exe directly prints the "postinstall was not run" stub error. - Existing opencode sessions keep working (the old binary stays mapped in memory) - so the breakage is invisible until you open a new terminal. ### Observed evidence - `npm install -g opencode-ai@1.18.18` started at 16:49 and 16:56, parented by `cmd.exe /d /s /c` whose parent was the `opencode.exe` process (auto-update), **still alive/hung ~30 min later**. - npm debug log: `ECONNRESET Invalid response body while trying to fetch https://registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai: aborted`. - After the failed install: `bin/opencode.exe` = 479-byte stub (LastWriteTime = the moment of the breakage), shims missing, `.opencode-UwDeVezx` / `.opencode.cmd-*` / `.opencode.ps1-*` temp files left behind. ### Suggested fixes 1. **Don't replace the binary in place while a process is running from it** - install/verify first, then atomically swap; or refuse to update when an opencode process is still running (on Windows this can never work). 2. **Verify postinstall succeeded before removing old bin links**, and restore the previous state on failure. 3. **Run the updater with a network timeout/retry limit** instead of hanging indefinitely in the background. 4. **Provide a supported way to disable auto-update** (e.g. `autoupdate: false`) - today there is no config option to opt out.
