signals.title: fix(core): keep plan mode reminders in sync with session agent
signals.text: ## Problem The plan plugin communicates Plan mode to the model via `<system-reminder>` synthetic messages injected on `session.created` / `session.agent.selected`. Those messages live in the transcript, but the mode itself lives in durable session state (`SessionTable.agent`) — and several operations edit the transcript without touching the agent: - **Compaction** cuts model-visible history at the checkpoint (`SessionHistory.messageRows` loads `seq >= compaction.seq`), dropping the enter reminder while the session stays on `plan`. - **Committed reverts** delete all message rows past the boundary while `SessionTable.agent` stays put and no `session.agent.selected` re-fires. Undoing past the switch *into* plan leaves the model unaware it's in Plan mode (including the undo-to-empty-session case); undoing past the switch *out of* plan leaves a stale enter reminder so the model wrongly refuses to edit. - Synthetics admitted while a revert is staged never wake execution and are deleted by the commit before delivery. In all cases the tool hook still hard-blocks edits, but the model has a wrong or missing idea of what mode it is in. ## Fix Reconcile the transcript against the durable agent on every model request via `ctx.session.hook("context")`: - Find the most recent live enter/leave reminder in the visible messages (whole-message equality, so reminder text quoted inside a compaction checkpoint doesn't count). - If the session is on `plan` with no live enter reminder, or off `plan` with a stale one, insert the correct reminder into the current request — before the trailing user message, matching where agent-switch reminders land — and persist a durable copy via `ctx.session.synthetic` so subsequent requests find it and the reconciler goes back to a no-op. The steady state is unchanged: durable enter/leave synthetics on agent switches do the work, and the reconciler does nothing while transcript and agent agree. Reminders only ever land near the request tail and earlier messages are never rewritten, so the prompt cache prefix stays warm; healing costs one small uncached insertion, once. This matches how Claude Code and Grok handle mode reminders (persisted, append-only, re-derived from mode state at prompt time); their periodic full/sparse re-assertion cadence is intentionally not adopted. ## Tests `test/plugin/plan.test.ts` runs the real plugin effect against a stubbed plugin context: - enter/leave injection on agent switches (pre-existing behavior) - missing enter reminder reconciled into the request (undo-to-empty scenario) and persisted - steady-state no-op with a live enter reminder - stale enter reconciled with a leave reminder - no injection for non-plan sessions without plan history - no injection when a leave reminder already follows the enter - reminder text quoted inside a checkpoint-like message treated as not live Reminder texts in tests are derived by invoking the plugin rather than duplicating the strings.

signals.title: fix(llm): send assistant text as input_text in OpenAI Responses requests (#42613)
signals.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #42613 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? When conversation history contains an assistant text message, the OpenAI Responses (`/responses`) request body used: ```json {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "..."}]} ``` `output_text` is not a valid easy-input content part: per the official OpenAI schema (`openai-python` types), assistant easy-input messages accept only `str | input_text | input_image | input_file`. Real `api.openai.com` tolerates the non-conformant shape, but strict OpenAI-compatible servers validating with the official SDK types (e.g. a self-hosted Qwen server exposing `/v1/responses`) reject it with a 422/400 pydantic `ValidationError`, so switching a session to such a model fails. The fix lowers assistant text content as `input_text` in request bodies: - `packages/llm/src/protocols/openai-responses.ts`: - Remove the now-unused `OpenAIResponsesOutputText` schema. - Lower assistant text content as `input_text` in request bodies (`lowerMessages`). - `OpenAIResponsesInputItem` assistant schema now uses `input_text` parts. - `packages/llm/test/provider/openai-responses.test.ts`: update expected request bodies (`output_text` → `input_text` for assistant input messages). The AI SDK path (`@ai-sdk/openai` `convertToOpenAIResponsesMessages`) emits the same invalid shape and would need a separate fix upstream (`vercel/ai`) to fix released builds. ### How did you verify your code works? ```sh cd packages/llm bun test test/provider/openai-responses.test.ts ``` 54 pass, 0 fail. ### Screenshots / recordings N/A — not a UI change. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signals.title: fix(opencode): evict message diff patches from the event payload
signals.text: ### Issue for this PR Fixes #42748 Related: #40861 solves the same root issue a simpler way (recompute patches from snapshots on demand, no side table). This PR keeps patches in a side table so they survive snapshot pruning, and it handles the client render explicitly — stripping `patch` from the inline array blanks the timeline silently otherwise (the render reads `summary.diffs` off the message; a broken read renders nothing because the row is gated on `diffs.length > 0`). Both are viable; a maintainer should pick the trade-off. ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix ### What does this PR do? `message.updated.1` carries a full message snapshot, and for user messages that snapshot includes `info.summary.diffs` — the per-file diff list with patch text. A snapshot is written on every update, so the bytes written for one message grow as O(updates × final diff size). Measured on a live 51 GB `opencode.db`, over the events that carry diffs: average payload 432 KB, peak 63 MB. One message whose final diff was 9 MB wrote ~2 GB of event rows across 236 updates; `summary.diffs` was 99.996% of the largest single event. The change moves patch text off the event bus, since diffs are derived state: 1. A `message_diff` side table (keyed by message id) holds the full diffs including patch text. 2. `SessionSummary.summarize` writes the full array to the side table, then publishes the message with `patch` stripped from the inline `summary.diffs` — the `{file, additions, deletions, status}` skeleton and the `additions`/`deletions`/`files` totals stay. 3. A thin ephemeral `message.diff.updated { sessionID, messageID }` event tells clients a diff changed. It carries no patch. It is ephemeral because the durable event reader decodes every row without a manifest filter, so a durable event would throw on any reader whose manifest predates it. 4. The client keeps a diff cache, seeds it from any inline diffs still present (legacy messages), and fetches patches from `session.diff` when a file is expanded. 5. `SessionSummary.diff` reads the side table first and falls back to the legacy inline array, so messages written before this change still render and export their patches with no migration. The migration is `CREATE TABLE` only; no backfill. `patch` was already optional in the `FileDiff` schema (a `session-diff-missing-patch` test already covered the patch-less shape), so this is a supported state, not a new one. **Retention (second commit).** Payload eviction bounds the growth rate; retention bounds the stock. `retention.event_idle_days` (opt-in, absent or <= 0 = disabled) enables an hourly sweep that deletes event-log history — events plus the sequence allocator row, through the existing removal primitive — for sessions idle longer than the configured days. Deleting the allocator with the events is what lets a revived session restart at seq 0 with no sequence gap. Projected state (`session`/`message`/`part`/`message_diff`) is never touched, so swept sessions still render fully; only the change-feed history goes. Bounded at 200 sessions per run, wired to the server lifecycle so embedded `Server.Default()` hosts get it too. ### How did you verify your code works? Red-first per change with per-hunk mutation checks. Plus a Playwright regression that expands a patch-less diff and asserts the patch renders through the fetch path — the unit tests structurally cannot mount the render, and that spec caught a real pre-existing bug where the client type guard rejected patch-less entries (which would have silently blanked the timeline once the strip landed). Retention tests cover: disabled-by-default (no config → ancient sessions untouched), threshold behavior with a recent-session canary (catches seconds-vs-milliseconds day math), post-sweep revival republishing at seq 0, and the per-run bound. Mutation checks: neutering the sweep or breaking the day math by 1000× reddens the corresponding tests. Full suites green across `core`, `schema`, `opencode`, `app`, `session-ui`; one pre-existing ripgrep baseline failure on `core` reproduces on `dev`. **Live deployment results.** The eviction commit has been running in production since 2026-08-15 on the box the problem was measured on — a 51 GB shared `opencode.db` with ~11 concurrent opencode processes: - The migration self-applied on the first restart after install (`CREATE TABLE` only, recorded once; concurrent processes see it done). - New diff-carrying `message.updated.1` events average about 1 KB on live traffic, against 432 KB average / 63 MB peak for the same event class before the change — the per-file skeleton and counts are all that remains inline. - History was untouched by deployment: messages written before the change kept their full inline diffs (5,221 rows on this box, byte-checked against a pre-deploy baseline) and render through the read fallback. After separately migrating those arrays into the side table, old sessions serve their patches through the same expansion-fetch path as new ones. - An external tool on the same database detects compaction markers with a boolean `$.summary` predicate. That population (38 rows) was verified unchanged before and after deployment — the strip only ever rewrites `$.summary.diffs` inside an object summary. - An independent deployment of the same fork on this machine ran its own verification with its own baselines: no reader breakage across its TypeScript and Rust readers of the `message` table, zero storage errors, and zero `database is locked` warnings since the rollout — those warnings were recurring under the old payload sizes. One quiet day is not conclusive for the lock claim, but the direction matches the diagnosis. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signals.title: feat(tui): surface worker RPC failures instead of hanging on a blank scr
signals.text: Covered by new tests in test/util/rpc.test.ts. Reviewed-by: GPT-5.6 Sol ### Issue for this PR Closes #34981 Related: #41284, #35494 ### Type of change - [X] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [X] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Previously a throwing RPC handler, a crashed/killed worker, or an unhandled rejection after the TUI entered alt-screen/raw mode all left the process hanging on a blank terminal with nothing printed and no useful exit code. - rpc.ts: listen() replies with an error instead of dropping it; client() rejects all in-flight and future calls when the worker errors, exits unexpectedly, or sends an undeserializable message; a postMessage() throw only rejects that one call. Adds onDisconnect() for callers with nothing in flight, and expectDisconnect() to distinguish our own worker.terminate() from a real crash. - tui.ts: wires worker disconnects into the TUI's fatal-error path and preserves a non-zero exit code instead of always exiting 0. - app.tsx: catches unhandledRejection/uncaughtException once alt-screen mode is active, restores the terminal, and reports the error. ### How did you verify your code works? Ran opencode with a bad database to verify that I get an error message instead of a blank screen 18 tests in rpc.test.ts covering throwing handlers, worker error/close/ messageerror events, postMessage failures, and (not just a synthetic EventTarget) a real Bun Worker that crashes on import. Plus 1 new test in the tui package's app-lifecycle.test.tsx. See the Tests section below for what each one covers. Cross-checked against a previous attempt at this same bug (#34974, closed, never merged) to see if it covered something that this patch didn't. ### Tests Process-level fatal handling (unhandledRejection/uncaughtException) is only partially covered: the app-lifecycle.test.tsx test invokes the triggerFatal() callback directly rather than emitting a real unhandledRejection or uncaughtException event. `packages/opencode/test/util/rpc.test.ts`: - Tests that a throwing RPC handler in `listen()` replies with an `rpc.result` error instead of leaving the request to hang. - Tests that a thrown value whose message can't be read (e.g. a hostile Proxy) still produces a safe fallback error string, rather than throwing again inside the error path itself. - Tests that a result envelope with `error` set causes `client.call()` to reject rather than resolve. - Tests that a successful result envelope still resolves `client.call()` normally, as a baseline against the error-path tests above. - Tests that a synchronous throw from `target.postMessage()` rejects the call immediately instead of leaving it pending forever. - Tests that a worker `error` event rejects any currently in-flight call. - Tests the same crash-rejects-the-in-flight-call behavior against a real Bun `Worker` (not a mocked EventTarget) running a fixture that throws on import, to confirm the mocked tests reflect real behavior. - Tests that a worker `close` event rejects in-flight calls with an "exited unexpectedly" error. - Tests that a worker `messageerror` event (an undeserializable message) rejects in-flight calls. - Tests that a message whose `data` isn't valid JSON rejects in-flight calls instead of throwing uncaught inside `onmessage`. - Tests that a parsed message missing a well-formed `type` field rejects in-flight calls. - Tests that a message with an unrecognized `type` rejects in-flight calls. - Tests that a call made after the worker has already died rejects immediately instead of queueing forever. - Tests that `onDisconnect` fires on a crash even when no call is currently pending to reject. - Tests that `onDisconnect` does not fire when `worker.terminate()` follows a call to `expectDisconnect()`, i.e. our own intentional shutdown isn't reported as a crash. - Tests that an exit with code 0 is still treated as fatal unless `expectDisconnect()` was called first, since a clean-looking exit code doesn't distinguish our own shutdown from an unrelated one. - Tests that a crash occurring while a call is in flight still rejects it, even if `expectDisconnect()` is called moments later — guards against `expectDisconnect()` being called too early and swallowing a real crash. - Tests that a handler registered on `onDisconnect` after the worker has already died is invoked immediately rather than missed. `packages/tui/test/app-lifecycle.test.tsx`: - Tests that a fatal error raised from within a finalizer (a plugin's `dispose()` call during cleanup) is still printed to stderr and sets exit code 1, instead of being lost once teardown has already started. ### Screenshots / recordings Reproduced against a real corrupted `opencode.db` (a bad `"dummy"` value where a session ID was expected). Before this fix, the terminal just sat blank forever with nothing printed. After: ``` ┃ ┃ ┃ Unexpected server error. Check server logs for ┃ ┃ details. ┃ ┃ ┃ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀▄ █▀▀▀ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █ █ █ █ █▀▀▀ █ █ █ █ █ █ █ █▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ █▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ┃ ┃ Ask anything... "What is the tech stack of this project?" ┃ ┃ Build · Big Pickle OpenCode Zen ╹▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀ tab agents ctrl+p commands ● Tip Run /connect to add an AI provider and start coding /tmp/repo-rw/packages/opencode local ``` Matching server log line: ``` level=ERROR message=failed ref=err_1b5e30e4 error="Error: Expected a string starting with \"ses\", got \"dummy\"" cause="... at workspace-routing.ts:222:23 ..." ``` ### Checklist - [X] I have tested my changes locally - [X] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signals.title: fix(install): honor OPENCODE_INSTALL_DIR and XDG_BIN_DIR as documented

The install script, however, hardcoded `INSTALL_DIR=$HOME/.opencode/bin` and never read any of these variables. This PR makes the script implement the documented behavior. ## Changes - `install`: resolve `INSTALL_DIR` in the documented priority order before `mkdir -p` - `$HOME/bin` is used when it exists or can be created (matches the README wording "if it exists or can be created") ## Verification - `bash -n install` passes - Behavior tested with a fake `$HOME` across four cases: - `OPENCODE_INSTALL_DIR` set → installed to it - only `XDG_BIN_DIR` set → installed to it - neither set, `$HOME/bin` absent → created and used - neither set, `$HOME/bin` present → used - Default install path (`$HOME/.opencode/bin`) unchanged when no variables are set

signals.title: fix(session): don't clobber user's model swap on model-less prompts
signals.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #42893 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix ### What does this PR do? A model-less prompt (no `input.model` — e.g. plugin completion-reminders via `promptAsync`) resolves from the agent fallback (`ag.model`) for the turn. The existing design (PR #26765) intentionally uses the agent's model when no explicit model is given — this is correct for the turn's model and is preserved. However, `setAgentModel` then overwrites the session row to the resolved model, permanently destroying a model the user explicitly stored via a prior swap. The TUI is unaffected (always sends `draft.model` explicitly), but `opencode serve` / mobile clients lose the swap on the next plugin reminder. **The fix:** guard the `setAgentModel` write in `createUserMessage` — skip it when: 1. The prompt carried no explicit model (`input.model == null`), AND 2. The session already has a stored model that differs from the agent's resolved model (`storedModelDiffers`) Fresh sessions (no stored model) still persist the agent's model on the first model-less prompt (`hasNoStoredModel` guard), and explicit-model prompts always persist normally. The model-resolution precedence is unchanged — model-less prompts still use the agent's model for the turn. ### How did you verify your code works? - **New regression test**: `"model-less prompt does not clobber user's stored model swap"` — creates a session, swaps to `kimi-k2.5-free`, sends a model-less prompt with an agent carrying `test/test-model`, asserts the turn uses `test-model` (design preserved) but the session row stays `kimi-k2.5-free` (the fix). Verified RED→GREEN. - **Fresh-session test**: `"model-less first prompt on fresh session persists agent model to row"` — confirms the `hasNoStoredModel` guard fires `setAgentModel` on a fresh session so the row is initialized. - **Existing test preserved**: `"applies agent variant only when using agent model"` (the test that pins the agent-model design from #26765) still passes — model-less prompts still use the agent's model for the turn. - **Full suite**: 46 pass / 14 skip / 0 fail across `test/session/prompt.test.ts`. - **Typecheck**: 30/30 packages clean (turbo typecheck). ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signals.title: fix(tui): sort child sessions by created time, not session ID
signals.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #42905 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? `session.child.first` (Ctrl+X+Down) and the Left/Right child cycle sorted sibling sessions by session ID string. Session IDs are descending-encoded timestamps that wrap around at 2^48, so once the encoding wraps the ID order no longer matches creation order and "first child" lands on an old subagent instead of the newest. The fix sorts `children()` in `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx` by `time.created` descending instead of by session ID. This is the ordering the ID sort was already encoding — "first child" keeps meaning newest-created, but is now stable across the wrap. The footer `(N of M)` counter already sorts by `time.created` ascending, so navigation and the counter stay consistent (Ctrl+X+Down lands on `M of M`). ### How did you verify your code works? - Reproduced the wrap: session IDs are `~current` where `current = timestamp_ms * 0x1000 + counter`, truncated to 48 bits. The last wrap occurred at 2026-08-14 11:19:55 UTC. - Checked against real session data: in an 829-child session spanning the wrap, the smallest-ID child was created minutes before the wrap while the actual newest child ranked ~756th in ID order; the new sort puts the newest-created child first. - `bun typecheck` passes in `packages/tui`. ### Screenshots / recordings Not included — this changes which session navigation lands on, not how the UI looks, so there is nothing visual to capture. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signals.title: fix: adopt new worktree when a project repository is moved
signals.text: ## Problem When a project's repository is moved or renamed on disk (e.g. the folder is moved to a parent directory), opencode keeps using the **old** worktree path: - `Project.fromDirectory` always keeps `existing.worktree` for existing (non-global) projects, even when that path no longer exists. The resolved new checkout is only ever added to `sandboxes`, never adopted as the project's worktree. - `InstanceStore.boot` uses the requested directory verbatim as the instance/session directory. If a client passes a stale path (as the desktop does from its persisted project state), the instance boots with a non-existent directory. The result: "New conversation" fails with `ENOENT` / `FileSystem.realPath` errors until the user manually edits the database. Repros happen whenever the repo root is moved up to its parent (e.g. `G:/.../AlgoTrading/EA Admirals` -> `G:/.../AlgoTrading`), so the old worktree is now a dead child of the new git root. ## Fix Two complementary server-side changes: 1. **`Project.fromDirectory`** (`packages/opencode/src/project/project.ts`): if the project's canonical `worktree` no longer exists on disk and the repository still resolves to a valid checkout, adopt the resolved git worktree (`data.directory`) as the new canonical worktree. Existing sessions rooted at the old worktree are re-pointed to the new directory, so old conversations keep working. 2. **`InstanceStore.boot`** (`packages/opencode/src/project/instance-store.ts`): when the requested directory does not exist but `fromDirectory` resolved it to a non-global git project, boot the instance in the resolved worktree (`result.sandbox`) instead of the stale path. This makes both new sessions and loading old sessions succeed even when a client passes a path that no longer exists. ## Tests - `Project.fromDirectory with worktrees > adopts a moved checkout as the project worktree when the original is gone` — moves a repo and asserts the project adopts the new worktree. - `InstanceStore > boots into the resolved worktree when the requested directory no longer exists` — loads an instance at a non-existent child of a git root and asserts it boots into the resolved worktree. Both new tests pass; the existing `project` and `instance-store` suites pass (47/47). `tsgo --noEmit` and `oxlint` are clean on the touched files.

signals.title: feat: add /reload slash command
signals.text: ## Summary Adds a `/reload` slash command that hot-reloads OpenCode configuration, plugins, MCP servers, and other instance-scoped services without restarting the TUI. If any sessions are active in the current instance, reload is queued until they become idle, then the backend instance is reloaded and the TUI re-syncs before dismissing the reload overlay. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5e9138c-25b9-43db-a53f-ba1de26bf5f9 Closes #6719 <!-- Old screencasts from an earlier implementation may not reflect current behavior: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e14c446-80bc-4a81-b092-94b08ae120e7 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb8140be-d770-4b26-be41-9d9536088fcd --> ## How it works The current implementation is built on the instance HttpApi and EventV2 flow: 1. The global TUI command `/reload` calls `POST /config/reload` for the current workspace. 2. `ConfigReload.request()` records reload state for the current instance/workspace, not globally across every open project. 3. If sessions are active, the reload stays pending until every active session in that instance becomes idle. 4. When execution starts, the server reloads the current instance through `InstanceStore.reload(...)` after the HTTP response is produced. 5. The TUI receives `config.reload.executing`, shows the blocking `Reloading configuration...` overlay, and performs a full bootstrap refresh. 6. The TUI acknowledges the exact bootstrap cycle with `POST /config/bootstrap-complete?cycle=...` only after the full refresh completes. 7. The server emits `config.reload.done`, and the TUI dismisses the overlay and shows a success toast. Reload state is scoped per instance/workspace, bootstrap completions require a matching cycle, and repeated reload requests during an active reload are coalesced so users do not see a false ready state between back-to-back reloads. ## User-visible behavior If no session is active, `/reload` starts immediately and shows the reload overlay. If sessions are running, `/reload` queues the reload and shows a queued toast; the reload starts once all active sessions in that client become idle. During the reload overlay, keyboard input is blocked so stray keystrokes are not leaked into the prompt. The `reload_config` tool still stops the current tool-processing turn with `stopSession: true`, but it no longer injects a synthetic user prompt to continue the conversation after reload. This avoids adding artificial “continue where you left off” text to durable session history or model context. ## Validation - Added focused regression tests for per-instance reload isolation, same-client multi-session queuing, bootstrap-cycle scoping, repeated reload coalescing, and absence of synthetic continuation prompt data. - Regenerated the v2 SDK from the updated HttpApi schema. - Typechecked `packages/opencode` and `packages/tui`. - Stress-tested the real TUI in tmux: `/reload` works from the home screen and from a session screen, no longer resolves to `/snippets:reload`, shows and clears the reload overlay, and remains stable when `/reload` is hammered during an in-flight reload.

signal.title: Desktop becomes unresponsive when Git Changes eagerly loads full-file diffs
signal.text: ### Description Opening a local repository with 29 modified files causes OpenCode Desktop to populate the **Review > Git changes** panel immediately. The app then becomes effectively unresponsive before the panel can be closed or collapsed. The repository is not unusually large by file count (158 tracked files, about 9.9 MB of Git metadata), but several changed source files are large. Git's normalized diff was about 1,700 additions and 126 deletions across 19 files. OpenCode instead displayed apparent full-file rewrites such as: - `MetadataStore.cpp`: +21,720 / -21,708 - `FsHostSemanticsTests.cpp`: +23,311 / -22,987 - `NativeApfsBackend.cs`: +6,662 / -6,635 This repository uses `core.autocrlf=true` and some edited files contain mixed CRLF/LF endings. Git normalizes those changes correctly, but the desktop review UI appears to process the much larger raw/full-context representation. Expected: the Git Changes panel should remain responsive, avoid opening/loading expensive diffs automatically, and lazy-load or cap/virtualize large diffs. Line-ending normalization or full-context patches should not freeze the entire app. Related reports #21068, #21784, #29768, and #21153 are closed, but the problem still reproduces in the current release. The proposed fix in #29928 was closed unmerged; #25581 does not appear to cover this desktop rendering path. ### Plugins No plugin-specific behavior observed. ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 (Desktop, Electron 42.3.3) ### Steps to reproduce 1. On Windows with Git `core.autocrlf=true`, open a repository containing several large source files. 2. Leave roughly 20-30 files modified, including files with mixed CRLF/LF edits. 3. Open the repository/session in OpenCode Desktop. 4. Let the Review / Git Changes side panel appear and populate. 5. Observe full-file-sized addition/deletion counts and severe UI lag; in this case the app became unusable. ### Screenshot and/or share link A screenshot shows the Review panel listing 29 files with multiple apparent 6k-23k-line full-file rewrites. It can be supplied if needed. ### Operating System Windows 11 Enterprise 64-bit, version 10.0.26200 (build 26200) ### Terminal N/A - OpenCode Desktop

signal.title: 48-bit ID overflow (2026-08-14) silently breaks every pre-existing session: prompt is stored, loop exits, model never runs
signal.text: ## Summary `Identifier.create()` truncates the timestamp to 48 bits, and the counter overflowed on **2026-08-14 11:19:55 UTC**. Since then, every newly generated ascending ID (`msg_00cc…`) sorts **before** any ID created prior to that instant (`msg_fec1…`). `SessionPrompt.run` uses lexicographic ID comparison to decide whether the last user message has already been answered: ```js if (O?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(O.finish) && !fe && G.id < O.id) { yield* s.logInfo("exiting loop", { "session.id": t }) break } ``` The result: **sending a message to any session whose last message predates the overflow does nothing** — the message is stored, the loop exits in ~3 ms, no model is ever called, and no error is surfaced to the client. From the UI it looks like the message vanished. ## Root cause `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts`: ```js let now = BigInt(currentTimestamp) * BigInt(0x1000) + BigInt(counter) const timeBytes = Buffer.alloc(6) // 48 bits for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { timeBytes[i] = Number((now >> BigInt(40 - 8 * i)) & BigInt(0xff)) } ``` `Date.now() * 0x1000` currently needs 53 bits; the top 5 are silently dropped. The low 48 bits wrap every `2**36` ms (~2.18 years). The wrap instants are `k * 2**36` ms: | epoch | instant (UTC) | |---|---| | 0x19 | 2024-06-10 02:35:18 | | **0x1a** | **2026-08-14 11:19:55** ← this one | | 0x1b | 2028-10-17 20:04:31 | `Identifier.timestamp(id)` is also affected: for an ID created today it returns ~1997. ## Reproduction (no waiting required) The public API accepts an explicit `messageID`, so the post-wrap condition can be simulated on any version: ```bash S=$(curl -s -X POST "localhost:4096/session?directory=$PWD" -d '{}' | jq -r .id) # 1) normal message -> answered curl -s -X POST "localhost:4096/session/$S/message?directory=$PWD" \ -d '{"model":{...},"parts":[{"type":"text","text":"say ok"}]}' # 2) same session, message ID from "before the wrap" -> silently ignored curl -s -X POST "localhost:4096/session/$S/message?directory=$PWD" \ -d '{"messageID":"msg_00a000000001AAAAAAAAAAAAAA","model":{...},"parts":[{"type":"text","text":"say two"}]}' ``` Log for (2), with no `process` / `stream` in between: ``` loop session.id=ses_… step=0 exiting loop session.id=ses_… ``` Observed in production on v1.18.13/1.18.14 with a session last used on 2026-08-10: after the wrap, every message sent to it was dropped this way. Sessions created after the wrap are unaffected, which is why this only shows up when reopening an older conversation. ## Impact - Every session whose last message predates 2026-08-14 11:19:55 UTC is permanently unable to receive a reply. - Failure is silent: HTTP 200, and the response body is the *previous* assistant message (`ye()` returns the last non-user message), so clients that only look at the payload cannot distinguish it from a real answer. - Session IDs use `descending`, so they wrapped the other way: pre-wrap sessions now sort as if they were the newest. ## Suggested fixes 1. **Stop comparing IDs to establish ordering.** Order by `time.created` (or an explicit sequence) in `SessionPrompt.run` / `Be.latest`. This alone restores every existing session. 2. **Widen the encoded field** to 7 bytes (or encode `timestamp` and `counter` separately) so the value stops being truncated — with a data migration, since existing IDs are already ambiguous. 3. At minimum, **fail loudly**: `create()` could assert that the value fits in the encoded width instead of dropping the high bits, and `SessionPrompt.run` could surface an error when it exits the loop without producing an assistant message for the newest user message. Happy to send a PR for (1) if that's the direction you'd prefer.
signal.author: rafaeljuniorvip

signal.title: Message IDs wrap around, silently dropping new user input in sessions with history
signal.text: ### Description In a session with existing message history, a new user message can be silently ignored — the agent loop exits without processing it. Root cause: Identifier.ascending() IDs are NOT monotonic. packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts encodes `Date.now()*0x1000 + counter` into a 6-byte (48-bit) field: let now = BigInt(currentTimestamp) * BigInt(0x1000) + BigInt(counter) const timeBytes = Buffer.alloc(6) // only 48 bits `Date.now()*0x1000` (~7.2e15 in 2026) exceeds 2^48 (~2.8e14) by ~25x, so the high bits are truncated. A freshly generated "msg_000..." sorts before older IDs. MessageV2.latest() picks the latest message by `info.id > user.id` (string compare), assuming IDs are monotonic (its comment says so). After wraparound it returns a stale message; the run loop then sees `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` and exits, dropping the new input. Suggested fix: compare by `info.time.created` (a real ms timestamp) with id as tiebreaker, matching the existing `(desc time_created, desc id)` pagination ordering. ### Plugins N/A (default config) ### OpenCode version v1.18.15 (also confirmed on dev @ 5d0f866) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start a session and exchange a few messages (build up message history). 2. Wait until the 48-bit timestamp field wraps — current date (2026) is already in the wrap window, since Date.now()*0x1000 overflows 2^48. 3. Send a new user message in the SAME session. 4. Observe: the agent does not respond. The run loop logs "exiting loop" and the new input is never sent to the model. Reproduction is time-dependent (tied to the wraparound point of the 48-bit timestamp), so it is intermittent rather than on every message. A reliable way to reproduce without waiting: unit-test latest() with messages whose time.created increases but whose ids wrap (a fresh "msg_000..." after older "msg_0a8a..."). ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Linux ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: Resuming an old session exits silently (no API call, no error) — even with a valid --model override; stale recorded model also breaks resume
signal.text: ## Description Old sessions can no longer be continued after restarting opencode. Two layers of failure: 1. **Stale model reference**: Sessions last used with a model that the provider has since removed (`zai-coding-plan/glm-5.1`) fail to resume with `ProviderModelNotFoundError` (only visible in logs). 2. **Silent exit even with a valid model override**: Even when passing `--model zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2`, resuming an old session exits the session loop immediately (~20ms, `step=0` → `exiting loop`) with **no API call, no error output, and exit code 0**. The user message is persisted, but no assistant reply is ever produced. Freshly-created sessions resume fine, so this is specific to replaying sessions created by an older version. ## Environment - opencode: 1.17.13 (Linux x64) - Session originally created with: 1.16.2 - Provider: `zai-coding-plan` (glm-5.1 recorded in session; glm-5.1 since removed from provider's model list — glm-4.7 / glm-5-turbo / glm-5.2 remain) ## Reproduction ```console $ opencode run --session <old-session-id> --model zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2 "Reply with exactly: OK" --format json # (no output at all, exit code 0) $ opencode run --session <old-session-id> --model zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2 "Reply with exactly: OK" --print-logs --log-level DEBUG 2>&1 | tail -3 timestamp=2026-08-15T14:13:45.216Z level=INFO run=2b186860 message=loop session.id=ses_161a26406ffe... step=0 timestamp=2026-08-15T14:13:45.233Z level=INFO run=2b186860 message="exiting loop" session.id=ses_161a26406ffe... timestamp=2026-08-15T14:13:45.239Z level=INFO run=2b186860 message="disposing instance" directory=/home/irlovan/AOC/Test ``` Without the model override, the log additionally shows: ``` level=ERROR message="share subscriber failed" type=message.updated cause="Cause([Fail(ProviderModelNotFoundError: Model not found: zai-coding-plan/glm-5.1. Did you mean: glm-4.7, glm-5-turbo, glm-5.2?)])" ``` ### What I verified while debugging - Resuming a **brand-new** session (created and resumed with the same 1.17.13 binary) works fine → not an environment/auth issue. - I patched all 412 stale `"modelID":"glm-5.1"` references in `message.data` to `glm-5.2` and updated `session.model` in the DB — resume **still** exits silently. So the stale model is not the only cause; old-session replay itself is broken. - Session data is structurally intact: no orphan parts, no malformed JSON, all tool parts have valid states, `time_compacting` is NULL. - `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT=1` makes no difference. - `--fork` works and preserves full conversation context. ## Expected behavior - Resume should either work, or surface the error (e.g. "model no longer available — pick another") instead of exiting silently with code 0. - A `--model` override on `run`/`tui` should take precedence over the model recorded in old messages. ## Workaround Fork the session (copies history into a new session that resumes fine): ```console $ opencode --session <old-session-id> --fork ``` ## Related - #33043 / #31141 mention `ProviderModelNotFoundError` for subagents with `model=undefined` — possibly the same class of stale/missing model resolution, but this report is about top-level session resume.

signal.title: bug: InterruptError — All fibers interrupted when InstanceStore.dispose races with Agent.list
signal.text: ## Describe the bug When an HTTP request triggers `Agent.list` (which reads agent configuration from the filesystem via `ScopedCache.get`), and at the same time another request triggers `InstanceStore.dispose`, the `ScopedCache` invalidation interrupts all in-flight lookup fibers, producing `InterruptError: All fibers interrupted without error`. This error propagates up to the HTTP response and reaches the Telegram Bot as a `session.promptAsync` failure. ## Stack trace ``` InterruptError: All fibers interrupted without error at FileSystem.up (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-pcf2w4yn.js:2:18581) at FileSystem.up (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-ewqah108.js:16:23248) at Agent.state (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-ae5jadfy.js:2:4743) at Agent.state (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-10rcnd8y.js:171:805) at Agent.list (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-nv7cdy3k.js:2:207057) at Agent.list (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-10rcnd8y.js:171:5293) at InstanceHttpApi.agent (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-nv7cdy3k.js:2:79248) at InstanceHttpApi.agent (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-nv7cdy3k.js:2:207000) at Server.listen (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-nv7cdy3k.js:3:46713) at Server.listen (definition) (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-nv7cdy3k.js:3:46836) ``` ## Root cause ### 1. Race condition in `InstanceState.make` + `disposeMiddleware` `packages/opencode/src/effect/instance-state.ts` line 38 registers a disposer that invalidates the `ScopedCache` when the instance is disposed. If a concurrent HTTP request is in the middle of `Agent.list` → `ScopedCache.get` → `lookup` → `Agent.state` (reading files via `FileSystem.up`), the invalidation closes the Effect scope and interrupts all child fibers. ### 2. Unhandled `InterruptError` in `Agent.list` `packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts` lines 357-358: ```typescript list: Effect.fn("Agent.list")(function* () { return yield* InstanceState.useEffect(state, (s) => s.list()) }) ``` `InterruptError` propagates unhandled through `InstanceHttpApi.agent` to the HTTP response. ## Affected files - `packages/opencode/src/effect/instance-state.ts` (lines 30-39) — ScopedCache with disposer that interrupts in-flight lookups - `packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts` (lines 357-358) — Agent.list without InterruptError handling - `packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/lifecycle.ts` (lines 43-53) — disposeMiddleware triggers teardown while requests are in-flight ## Suggested fix 1. In `Agent.list` (agent.ts:357), catch `InterruptError` and retry or return a degraded response 2. Consider using `Effect.uninterruptible` for the ScopedCache lookup to prevent disposal from interrupting in-flight requests

signal.title: fix(lsp): pyright spawn sets only pythonPath, never venvPath/venv — venv imports unresolved without pyrightconfig.json
signal.text: ### Description OpenCode's pyright LSP spawn sets only `pythonPath` in the initialization options, never `venvPath`/`venv`. This means pyright can't resolve third-party packages installed in a project's `.venv/` unless the user manually creates a `pyrightconfig.json`. Without that workaround, every venv import is flagged `reportMissingImports`, flooding the agent with noise until it ignores diagnostics entirely. The pyright spawn code in [`packages/opencode/src/lsp/server.ts`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/lsp/server.ts) only sets `initialization["pythonPath"]` after detecting the venv interpreter: ```ts const initialization: Record<string, string> = {} // ... detects VIRTUAL_ENV / .venv / venv ... initialization["pythonPath"] = potentialPythonPath ``` Pyright's preferred venv mechanism is `venvPath` + `venv` (path concatenation, no interpreter execution needed). Setting only `pythonPath` requires pyright to execute the interpreter to discover `sys.path`, which is fragile and silently falls back to system Python when that fails. Related: #6131 (closed as not planned, but the `workspace/configuration` part it reported is actually fixed on current `dev` — the remaining unfixed part is this `server.ts` issue), #25408, #2050. The fix is small — add `venvPath` and `venv` to `initialization` alongside `pythonPath` in the pyright spawn function (~5 lines). ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version v1.17.7 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a Python project with a `.venv/` at the root containing third-party packages (e.g. `pandas`, `numpy`). 2. Enable `"lsp": true` in opencode config. Do **not** add a `pyrightconfig.json`. 3. Open a `.py` file in the project that imports a venv-only package. 4. Run `opencode run` with a trivial prompt that triggers an edit to that file. 5. Observe `reportMissingImports` diagnostics on every venv import. Verification that `pyrightconfig.json` with `{"venvPath": ".", "venv": ".venv"}` resolves it: with config → 0 errors; without config → 2 `reportMissingImports` errors on `pandas`/`numpy` (system Python doesn't have them, venv does). The config-file workaround bypasses the LSP channel entirely by reading from disk. ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A — reproducible via the steps above and source link. ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04 ### Terminal GNOME Terminal

signal.title: fix: auto-title overwrites plugin session rename on first turn
signal.text: ### Description Plugin tools that rename a session via `client.session.update()` have no effect on the first turn of a new session. The title reverts to an auto-generated one. Calling the same tool on the second turn works fine. The cause is a race in `SessionPrompt.ensureTitle` (`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`). On step 1 of the loop, auto-title is forked into the background: ```typescript if (step === 1) yield* title({ session, ... }).pipe(Effect.ignore, Effect.forkIn(scope)) ``` The forked task checks `isDefaultTitle(input.session.title)` against the `session` object captured at the top of the loop iteration (line 1139), before any tools have run. On a new session this is always `true`, so auto-title proceeds to generate and set its own title via `sessions.setTitle()`. Meanwhile the main LLM stream runs, the model calls the plugin's rename tool, and the plugin sets the title through the HTTP API. The auto-title's LLM call finishes later and overwrites the plugin's title. On the second turn, `sessions.get()` returns the session with the auto-generated title from turn 1. `isDefaultTitle()` returns `false`, auto-title bails out immediately, and the plugin's rename sticks. The fix would be to re-read the session title from the DB before overwriting, or to skip auto-title when the title was explicitly set by a tool during the same turn. ### Plugins Custom plugin registering a `session_rename` tool (calls `client.session.update`) ### OpenCode version 1.17.7 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a plugin that registers a tool calling `client.session.update({ path: { id: context.sessionID }, body: { title: args.title } })` 2. Configure the agent to call this tool on every turn (e.g. via system prompt or AGENTS.md) 3. Start a new session and send a message 4. Observe the session title is the auto-generated one, not the plugin's title 5. Send a second message in the same session 6. Observe the plugin's title now sticks ### Operating System Fedora 44 (Linux 7.0.12) ### Terminal Ghostty

signal.title: opencode 1.17.7 panics with ThreadPoolBuildError (EAGAIN) when initializing worker thread pool
signal.text: Titre de l'issue : opencode 1.17.7 panics with ThreadPoolBuildError (EAGAIN) when initializing worker thread pool --- ## Description opencode crashes with a Rust panic (`SIGABRT`) when it fails to initialize its worker thread pool. The underlying OS error is `EAGAIN` (`WouldBlock`, "Resource temporarily unavailable"). This appears to be a robustness issue in opencode's thread-pool startup code rather than a hard resource limit on the system. ## Environment | Item | Value | |------|-------| | opencode version | `1.17.7` | | OS | Arch Linux (rolling) | | Kernel | `6.18.35-1-lts` | | Shell | `zsh 5.9.1` | | Terminal multiplexer | `tmux 3.6b` | | Executable | `/home/richard/.opencode/bin/opencode` | | Working project | `/home/richard/Nexus/Tech/Projects/Bash/forge-disk-customize` | ## Steps to reproduce A fully deterministic reproduction is not yet available. The crash occurred during an interactive opencode session in tmux while working on a small Bash project. The sequence was approximately: 1. Open a tmux session. 2. Start opencode in `/home/richard/Nexus/Tech/Projects/Bash/forge-disk-customize`. 3. Run several tasks that spawn sub-agents / shell commands. 4. opencode panics while trying to initialize a worker thread pool. ## Observed frequency Three consecutive crashes within roughly 30 minutes, all `SIGABRT`, in the same tmux scope: ```text PID 61761 opencode SIGABRT 16:07 PID 67642 opencode SIGABRT 16:09 PID 79018 opencode SIGABRT 16:37 ``` ## Logs / error output ```text thread 'main' (1039099) panicked at src/main.rs:315:10: Failed to initialize worker thread pool: ThreadPoolBuildError { kind: IOError(Os { code: 11, kind: WouldBlock, message: "Resource temporarily unavailable" }) } note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace zsh: fork failed: ressource temporairement non disponible zsh: fork failed: ressource temporairement non disponible zsh: fork failed: ressource temporairement non disponible _zsh_autosuggest_bind_widgets:15: fork failed: ressource temporairement non disponible ``` The error repeats across multiple panicked threads and is accompanied by cascading `zsh: fork failed` messages. ## Coredump details ```text PID: 79018 (opencode) UID: 1000 (richard) Signal: 6 (ABRT) Timestamp: Wed 2026-06-17 16:37:03 CEST Command Line: opencode Executable: /home/richard/.opencode/bin/opencode Control Group: /user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/tmux-spawn-a2c8654e-9279-401b-a004-2954c480a8c1.scope Storage: /var/lib/systemd/coredump/core.opencode.1000.e60bad988b79471fa8c9a82b90d82df6.79018.1781707023000000.zst (present, 102.2M) ``` Stack trace of the crashing thread: ```text #0 0x00007fb3cb8256e6 abort (libc.so.6 + 0x256e6) #1 0x00000000039ca5d0 n/a (opencode + 0x37ca5d0) #2 0x00000000046a5425 n/a (opencode + 0x44a5425) #3 0x0000000004ffadda n/a (opencode + 0x4dfadda) #4 0x00000000051820fc n/a (opencode + 0x4f820fc) #5 0x00000000049894c6 n/a (opencode + 0x47894c6) #6 0x00000000050fcbb4 n/a (opencode + 0x4efcbb4) ... ``` ## Resource state at crash time The following measurements were taken **after** the crashes, once the system had partially recovered. They help exclude simple `ulimit` / cgroup exhaustion as the root cause. | Resource | Value | |----------|-------| | `ulimit -u` (max user processes) | 255 322 | | cgroup `user.slice/user-1000.slice/pids.max` | `max` | | cgroup `user.slice/user-1000.slice/pids.current` | 242 | | Total system threads (`ps -eLf`) | ~635 | | Available RAM | ~58 GiB | | Memory pressure (`memory.pressure`) | `avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00` | A single zombie process was left behind: `[zsh] <defunct>`, indicating a parent process did not reap its child. ## Project context The project being edited at the time of the crash is a 135-line Bash script skeleton with no `main()`, no infinite loops, no background jobs (`&`), and no heavy forking logic. It is not the cause of the crash. The active opencode instance at the time was performing sub-agent work. ## Expected behavior When the OS returns `EAGAIN` while creating a worker thread, opencode should handle the situation gracefully, for example: - Retry with a short backoff, - Reduce the requested thread-pool size, - Display a clear user-facing error message, - Or at least fail cleanly without a panic and `SIGABRT`. ## Actual behavior opencode panics in `src/main.rs:315`, aborts with `SIGABRT`, terminates the session, and leaves a `zsh` zombie process. ## Attachments 1. Terminal screenshot: `~/Capture d'écran_20260617_163908.png` 2. Compressed coredump: `/var/lib/systemd/coredump/core.opencode.1000.e60bad988b79471fa8c9a82b90d82df6.79018.1781707023000000.zst` ## Additional context - The current opencode instance (restarted after the crash) is running normally with ~33 threads. - The issue appears transient, but the panic makes recovery impossible without restarting opencode and losing context. - A `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` run has not yet been captured because the crash is not deterministic. --- *Report generated on 2026-06-17 for opencode 1.17.7.*

signal.title: OpenCode binary fails to run natively on Termux / Android aarch64 (wrong interpreter + non‑PIE executable)
signal.text: ### Description **Environment** - Device: Android smartphone/tablet, HUAWEI PaperMate 11.5 - OS: Android (5.0+), HarmionyOS 4.2.0 - Terminal: Termux - Arch: `aarch64` (`uname -m` → `aarch64`) - Install method: official install script (`curl ... | sh`, binary ends up in `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`) **Summary** After installing OpenCode on Termux using the official script, the Linux/aarch64 `opencode` binary does not start as a native Android executable. 1) The binary requests a dynamic linker at `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`, which does not exist on Android/Termux. 2) After manually changing the interpreter to the correct Android linker, the binary fails with `Android 5.0 and later only support position-independent executables (-fPIE)`, which means it was not compiled as PIE and cannot be run on modern Android at all. **Steps to reproduce** 1. Install Termux from F‑Droid / Play Store. 2. Update packages and install diagnostic tools: ```bash pkg update -y pkg install -y file binutils patchelf ``` 3. Install OpenCode using the official method, for example: ```bash curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install.sh | sh ``` 4. Try to run the binary: ```bash /data/data/com.termux/files/home/.opencode/bin/opencode ``` 5. Observe the shell error: ```bash bash: /data/data/com.termux/files/home/.opencode/bin/opencode: cannot execute: required file not found ``` **Diagnostics** 1. Check the file type: ```bash file /data/data/com.termux/files/home/.opencode/bin/opencode ``` The output shows a 64‑bit ELF for `aarch64`, with the program interpreter set to `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1` (standard on many Linux distros, but not on Android/Termux). 2. On Termux/Android, `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1` does not exist. To find the correct interpreter, I inspected a working Termux binary (`bash`): ```bash readelf -l "$(which bash)" | grep "Requesting program interpreter" ``` This reports `/system/bin/linker64` as the requested program interpreter. 3. I tried to “fix” the `opencode` binary by changing its interpreter: ```bash patchelf --set-interpreter /system/bin/linker64 \ /data/data/com.termux/files/home/.opencode/bin/opencode ``` This successfully changes the interpreter to the Android linker used by Termux. 4. Running `opencode` again: ```bash /data/data/com.termux/files/home/.opencode/bin/opencode ``` Now I get a different error: ```text "/data/data/com.termux/files/home/.opencode/bin/opencode": error: Android 5.0 and later only support position-independent executables (-fPIE). ``` This is the typical Android error when the ELF binary is not built as PIE. Since Android 5.0, only position‑independent executables (built with `-fPIE` / `-pie`) are allowed to run. **What I expected** I expected the official Linux/aarch64 OpenCode binary to either: - run natively under Termux on Android (with a correct interpreter and PIE build), or - clearly be documented as *not* supported for native Termux/Android, with guidance to use a different build or a proot‑based Linux environment instead. **What actually happens** - With the unmodified binary: `bash: cannot execute: required file not found` due to the non‑existent `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`. - After setting the interpreter to `/system/bin/linker64`: the binary exits with `Android 5.0 and later only support position-independent executables (-fPIE)` and cannot be started at all. - This cannot be fixed on the user side by patching the existing ELF; it requires recompiling OpenCode with the correct flags and target. **Analysis / root cause** - The binary shipped by the installer appears to be a regular Linux ELF for `aarch64` with glibc, requesting `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1` as interpreter. - Termux runs on Android, using `/system/bin/linker64` and a different ABI, and Android ≥ 5.0 rejects non‑PIE executables. - Even after manually fixing the interpreter path, the OpenCode binary still cannot run, because it does not satisfy Android’s requirement for position‑independent executables. **Why this deserves a dedicated fix** - There are already reports about OpenCode issues on Termux (usually when running inside a proot‑distro like Ubuntu/Debian, with freezes, TUI issues, crashes on the second run, etc.), but those are runtime problems inside a Linux userland. - In this case, the problem is more fundamental: the official Linux/aarch64 binary is simply incompatible with the native Android ABI (wrong interpreter and non‑PIE), so it is impossible to run it directly in Termux without a full Linux environment in proot. **Suggested fix** 1. Provide an official Android/Termux build for `aarch64` that: - is built as PIE (`-fPIE` / `-pie`), - uses the correct interpreter for Android (for example `/system/bin/linker64`, depending on the target ABI), - is tested in a real Termux environment, not only on standard Linux. 2. Alternatively (until such a build exists), update the documentation and installer to: - explicitly state that the current Linux/aarch64 binary is not intended to run natively on Termux/Android, - recommend using OpenCode via a proot‑distro (Ubuntu/Debian) or a remote Linux server when working from Android. **Additional info** - I can attach exact outputs of `file`, `readelf -l`, and `patchelf --print-interpreter` if needed. - I’m happy to test any experimental Android/Termux builds (aarch64) and provide feedback. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.text: ### Description When an environment variable is set with a native Windows path (backslashes), using` {env:VAR} `as a permission key causes opencode to fail with a JSON parse error on startup. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.14.33 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Add it as a permission key in opencode.json: "permission": { "external_directory": { "{env:MYDIR}/**": "allow" } } 3. signal.title: feat(core): bound tool and admitted event payloads via session blobs
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #36444 https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/36444 Parent: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/36441 ✧ raised · ○ in review · ● approved · ✓ merged [#36441](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/36441) epic: scope streams + bound payloads Merge in order: v2 └ ○ [#37486](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/37486) location interest    └ ○ [#37487](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/37487) session interest + fan-out bench       └ ○ [#37585](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/37585) stream ownership / diagnostics          └ ○ [#37586](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/37586) reconnect herd Siblings under the epic (not git parents of the stack tip): └ ○ [#37559](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/37559) session blobs + payloadHash ← this PR └ ○ [#37570](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/37570) ensure-on-first-failure → feeds [#37586](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/37586) Adjacent: #36524 (image dedupe only — complementary, not a substitute). ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [x] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Durable `session.tool.success` / `progress` and `session.input.admitted` events were carrying multi-megabyte bodies (tool output, inline base64 attachments). That multiplies encode/SSE/decode cost across every subscriber. This PR makes those events bounded projections: - Full tool settlement and admitted attachment bytes live in session-scoped `session_tool_payload` (same lifetime as the session). - Events carry `payloadHash` plus small text previews only. - Encoded durable event `data` budget is **256 KiB** UTF-8; over-budget settlement fails (no silent truncate). - Projectors hydrate `session_message` / `session_pending` from the blob so replay stays complete. - Clients that need the body use existing message/pending fetch APIs; TUI refetches when `payloadHash` is present. - `ToolOutputStore.bound` media rules are unchanged (provider channel only — not the durable event sidecar). ### How did you verify your code works? - `packages/core` `test/tool-payload.test.ts` — multi-MB blob round-trip; thin event under budget; oversize thin fails - `packages/core` `test/session-runner-tool-events.test.ts` — thin success omits base64; over-budget → Failed - `packages/core` `test/session-pending-attachments.test.ts` — large admit thin + hydrate; text-only omits hash - `packages/core` `test/session-tool-progress.test.ts` — projector hydrates thin `tool.success` into `session_message` - `packages/tui` `test/cli/tui/payload-hash.test.tsx` — TUI refetch on `payloadHash` (message + pending); no refetch without hash - typecheck on push ### Acceptance → test - Budget / fail-not-truncate → `tool-payload` + `over-budget thin success fails settlement…` - Multi-MB tool → thin event, full via message → `hydrates thin tool success…` + `tool.success with payloadHash refetches…` - Large attachment → thin admit, full via pending → `admits a large attachment…` + `input.admitted with payloadHash refetches pending` - Uninterested clients see thin frame only → thin event assertions (no mega/base64 on durable `data`) - TUI correct after thin success/admit → `payload-hash.test.tsx` ### Screenshots / recordings _N/A — not a UI layout change._ ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: FFF grep tool returns no matches when `path` is a directory
signal.text: ## Summary The `grep` tool (FFF-backed) returns **zero matches** whenever its `path` argument is a **directory**, even for files it finds in an unfiltered repo-wide search. The directory filter over-constrains to empty. ## Environment - opencode `1.16.2` (FFF v0.8.1 per `fff_health`), Linux x86_64. - Repo: ~2973 git-tracked files, all tracked (none gitignored). ## Reproduction (decisive) Same pattern, only the `path` differs. The match string `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` exists in `docs/adf/operations.md` and `docs/taxonomy/routing_scenarios/adf/review_tier.md`. | pattern | `path` arg | result | |---|---|---| | `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | *(none — repo-wide)* | **FOUND** both files | | `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | `docs` | **No matches** | | `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | `docs/taxonomy` | **No matches** | | `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | `docs/adf` | **No matches** | | `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | `docs/taxonomy/routing_scenarios/adf/review_tier.md` (exact file) | **FOUND** | And a string that lives **only** under one directory: - `grep "Route through pi-rust until opencode"` (no path) → found in all 4 `docs/taxonomy/routing_scenarios/adf/*.md`. - `grep "Route through pi-rust until opencode" path=docs/taxonomy/routing_scenarios/adf` → **No matches**. ## What works / what does not - `grep` with **no** `path` (repo-wide): works. - `grep` with an **exact file** `path`: works (direct read). - `grep` with a **directory** `path`: returns nothing. ← bug - `find` / `glob` (file-name search): works (locates the files fine; they are in the FFF index — `fff_health` reports 2783 indexed files). ## Likely cause The directory `path` filter is over-strict — it appears to discard all candidates instead of constraining to those under the directory. It is **not** staleness (`fff_rescan` does not fix it), **not** a `.md`/`docs` exclusion (some `.md` files are matched repo-wide), **not** frecency/cold-files (the files ARE found repo-wide), and **not** depth-specific (shallow dirs like `docs` also fail). ## Workaround Use shell `grep -rn <dir>` for directory-scoped search, or drop the `path` arg and search repo-wide. ## Expected Directory `path` should constrain results to files under that directory (recursive), matching ripgrep/git-grep semantics. Happy to provide more diagnostics. Thanks!

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Add Personas to support role-specific OpenCode environments
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Problem OpenCode currently supports agents, commands, permissions, configuration, rules, MCPs, and plugins, but these concepts are all loaded into the same global or project-level working environment. This becomes noisy when a user works in different roles inside the same repository or across multiple repositories. For example, the same user may sometimes work as: ```text frontend developer backend developer code reviewer scrum master product manager ``` Today, this often leads to a large shared setup like: ```text .opencode/ agents/ frontend-dev.md backend-dev.md code-reviewer.md scrum-master.md product-manager.md commands/ frontend-feature.md backend-task.md review-code.md refine-story.md sprint-risk.md ``` The issue is not that agents or commands are missing. The issue is that unrelated working modes are mixed together in the same namespace. A reviewer should normally have a read-only setup. A frontend developer may need UI-specific commands, design-system instructions, Storybook/Playwright MCPs, and edit permissions. A product manager may need refinement and acceptance-criteria workflows, but no code-editing tools. Right now, users can approximate this with agents and commands, but there is no first-class way to switch the entire OpenCode environment according to the role they are currently performing. --- ## Proposed Solution Add a new first-class concept called **Personas**. A persona would be a named, role-specific OpenCode operating environment. ```text Persona = a named configuration overlay for a specific working mode ``` Example personas: ```text frontend backend reviewer scrum-master product-manager ``` Each persona could define or scope: ```text commands agents instructions permissions model defaults MCP settings tool behavior plugins, if supported by the current architecture ``` Instead of all commands and agents living in one shared namespace, persona-specific setup could live under: ```text .opencode/ personas/ frontend/ persona.jsonc AGENTS.md agents/ commands/ backend/ persona.jsonc AGENTS.md agents/ commands/ reviewer/ persona.jsonc AGENTS.md agents/ commands/ product/ persona.jsonc AGENTS.md agents/ commands/ ``` The selected persona would act as a config overlay on top of the normal OpenCode configuration. Conceptual load order: ```text 1. OpenCode defaults 2. Global config 3. Project config 4. Existing .opencode config 5. Selected persona config 6. Runtime or CLI overrides ``` If no persona is selected, OpenCode should keep its current behavior. --- ## Behavior ### CLI Users should be able to start OpenCode with a persona: ```bash opencode --persona frontend opencode --persona reviewer ``` For non-interactive mode: ```bash opencode run --persona reviewer "review the current diff" ``` ### TUI Users should be able to inspect and switch personas from inside the TUI: ```text /persona list /persona current /persona switch frontend /persona inspect frontend ``` The active persona should be visible somewhere in the TUI status area, for example: ```text Persona: frontend Agent: dev Model: claude-sonnet ``` ### Persona-scoped commands Commands should be scoped to the active persona. For example: ```text /review ``` Could mean a frontend review workflow inside the `frontend` persona, but a stricter read-only code review workflow inside the `reviewer` persona. This avoids command pollution like: ```text /frontend-review /backend-review /security-review /product-review ``` OpenCode should define clear conflict behavior when a persona command has the same name as a global command. Possible behavior: ```text persona command > project command > global command ``` Or OpenCode could warn when a command is shadowed. ### Persona-scoped agents A persona should also be able to load persona-specific agents. Example: ```text .opencode/personas/frontend/agents/dev.md .opencode/personas/frontend/agents/a11y-reviewer.md .opencode/personas/frontend/agents/design-system-reviewer.md ``` And: ```text .opencode/personas/reviewer/agents/reviewer.md ``` This would allow each persona to expose only the agents relevant to that working mode. ### Permission changes Persona switching may change permissions. Example: ```text reviewer → frontend ``` This may enable file editing. OpenCode should warn when switching to a persona that grants broader permissions: ```text Switching from reviewer to frontend will enable file editing. Continue? ``` --- ## Example Persona Config ```jsonc { "name": "frontend", "label": "Frontend Developer", "description": "React, TypeScript, UI quality, design system, accessibility, and frontend verification.", "defaultAgent": "dev", "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5", "instructions": [ "AGENTS.md", "docs/frontend-standards.md", "docs/design-system.md", "docs/accessibility.md" ], "permission": { "read": "allow", "glob": "allow", "grep": "allow", "edit": "ask", "bash": "ask", "lsp": "allow", "websearch": "ask", "webfetch": "ask" }, "mcp": { "context7": { "enabled": true }, "storybook": { "enabled": true }, "playwright": { "enabled": false } } } ``` Example reviewer persona: ```jsonc { "name": "reviewer", "label": "Code Reviewer", "description": "Read-only code review mode focused on correctness, regressions, maintainability, security, and test coverage.", "defaultAgent": "reviewer", "permission": { "read": "allow", "glob": "allow", "grep": "allow", "edit": "deny", "bash": "ask", "lsp": "allow", "websearch": "ask", "webfetch": "ask" } } ``` --- ## Why This Matters * Keeps OpenCode setups clean when users perform multiple roles. * Reduces command and agent namespace pollution. * Makes role-specific permissions safer and more explicit. * Allows read-only reviewer setups without affecting developer workflows. * Allows frontend/backend/product/delivery workflows to have different instructions, commands, agents, MCPs, and validation behavior. * Improves team usage because each role can have a predictable OpenCode environment. * Preserves current behavior when no persona is selected. This would make OpenCode more scalable for users who are not always acting as the same kind of developer. [1]: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/32672 "[FEATURE]: Add /usage slash command to display subscription usage in TUI · Issue #32672 · anomalyco/opencode · GitHub"

The fix appears straightforward: raise `max` to a higher fraction (e.g. `window.innerWidth * 0.70`) so the session panel can take up more of the screen, allowing the review panel to be resized to a narrower, more practical width. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.15.13 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open OpenCode Desktop with an active workspace 2. Open the Review panel 3. Attempt to drag the divider handle rightward to make the session/chat panel wider and the review panel narrower 4. signal.title: [FEATURE]: Comprehensive Plugin Pipeline - Middleware-Style Data Flow Control
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request OpenCode's current plugin system provides event hooks but lacks comprehensive pipeline access comparable to middleware patterns like Ring (Clojure) or Rack (Ruby) and dozens in JS land. This restricts plugins from: 1. Universal tool interception - MCP tools bypass plugin hooks (#2319) 2. Result manipulation - Plugins can't modify tool outputs before AI sees them 3. Configuration access - No read access to current tool/agent settings 4. Pipeline control - Can't implement sophisticated security or transformation policies Security is my chief concern. If I can’t see and intercept every part of the pipeline — including the pieces that stay tucked away — it’s difficult to build trust. **When the whole system is open to inspection, trust comes much easier, because the platform hands some control back to us.** ## Proposed Solution Extend plugin system to expose the pipeline and permit middleware. As I explained in my request for modal dialogs (#5147), human-in-the-loop interactions are pipeline based, not event based. Better security, too, is pipeline based. You need to influence what's flowing through the system, not just react to it. With an extensible middleware architecture and modals, you have a solid backbone which permits an overwhelming number of feature requests to fall out of core and back to the community. That's been my goal with these recent requests: to shift more and more of the feature burden to the community. **My thought is every penny spent here is a dime in savings.** ## Universal Pipeline Hooks ```js export const PipelinePlugin = async ({ project, client, $, directory, worktree }) => { return { // Universal interception for ALL operations pipeline: { before: async (context) => { // Intercept any operation (tools, sessions, config) // Modify inputs, add auth, implement policies }, after: async (context, result) => { // Transform outputs, filter content, add metadata }, error: async (context, error) => { // Error handling, recovery, logging } } } } ``` The above is purely suggestive of the idea. ## Configuration Access - Expose read-only access to the opencode configuration object after all merges (#4960) - Expose tool/agent configurations ## Benefits to Existing Issues This could help solve: - #2319 (MCP tool coverage) - Universal pipeline includes all tool types - #1727 (Webfetch permissions) - Fine-grained network control - #2945/#3291 (Session management) - Better state preservation - #744 (CORS/network middleware) - Network-level transformations - #3432 (Agent definitions) - Access to AGENTS.md configurations ## Implementation Pattern Similar to established middleware patterns: - Chain of responsibility for plugin composition - Request/response transformation capabilities - Early termination for security policies - Context preservation across pipeline stages ## Use Cases Enabled - Session tainting (#5091) with complete data flow control - Security policies for network access and data exfiltration - Content filtering and sanitization - Advanced logging and audit trails - Custom approval workflows beyond basic permissions This approach transforms OpenCode plugins from event handlers into powerful middleware capable of sophisticated data flow control, enabling an ecosystem of advanced security, monitoring, and transformation tools. My several requests are all in service to writing plugins to service my own needs. My goal is to, as much as possible, do that, but it depends on the core you expose (#753). I'll continue to say it: **this is an amazing product.** It's only because I'm chomping at the bit to jump in and develop my own features I've been so aggressive with requests. I want to build on opencode. I just want to do it by extension.

signal.title: glob tool respects .gitignore
signal.text: ### Summary The `glob` tool runs `rg --files --glob=<pattern>` without `--no-ignore`, so anything in `.gitignore` is silently filtered out — even when the agent passes an exact path it already knows exists. This makes sense for `grep` (gitignored matches would flood context with `node_modules`/`dist` noise). It doesn't make sense for `glob`, which only returns paths. The cost of including a gitignored hit is one line; the cost of hiding it is the agent asserting a file doesn't exist when it does. ### Reproduction Just using this repo as example, on `dev` after `bun install`, ask your agent to run: ``` $ ls packages/opencode/node_modules/effect/package.json # exists glob("packages/opencode/node_modules/effect/package.json") # I → No files found glob("**/node_modules/effect/package.json") → No files found ``` Same for `dist/`, `tmp/`, `logs/`, `.env*`, `*.tsbuildinfo`. Inconsistent with `--hidden`, which the same call passes — hidden files are returned, gitignored files are not. Common cases this breaks: - "Find the built bundle" → `dist/**/*.js` returns nothing - "Where does `effect` define X?" → `**/node_modules/effect/**` returns nothing - "Find generated SDK / codegen output" → invisible ### Code `packages/core/src/ripgrep.ts:157-170`: ```ts glob: (input) => run<string>({ cwd: input.cwd, args: [ "--no-config", "--files", ...(input.hidden ? ["--hidden"] : []), ...(input.follow ? ["--follow"] : []), `--glob=${input.pattern}`, "--glob=!**/.git/**", ".", ], ... }) ``` ### Suggestion Add `--no-ignore-vcs` to the `glob` argv (keep `--glob=!**/.git/**`), leave `grep` as-is. Optionally expose `respectGitignore` on the tool for opt-back-in. Happy to PR.
