signal.title: Desktop: renaming a project folder breaks the project binding (phantom project, rename ignored, sessions silently fall back to global)
signal.text: ### Description On OpenCode Desktop (v1.18.14, macOS arm64), renaming a project **folder in Finder** (outside OpenCode) permanently breaks the project↔directory binding. The app keeps a phantom project whose `worktree`/`project_directory` point to non-existent paths, the project display name cannot be changed, and new sessions silently fall back to the `global` project (or fail to start when clicking the phantom). ### To Reproduce 1. Create a project in OpenCode Desktop (folder `A`). Rename the project in-app to e.g. "DarkRain" → Save. 2. Rename folder `A` → `B` in Finder, then rename the project in-app → **name does not change**. 3. Rename folder `B` → `C` in Finder. Delete the project in-app, then create a new project selecting folder `C` → **the name auto-reverts to the original project name**, and a phantom entry pointing at a dead path still shows in the sidebar. 4. Click that phantom project and start a conversation → **no output, no session is created**. ### Expected behavior - Renaming the project folder in Finder should either re-associate the same project (follow the rename) or the app should detect the stale record and clean it up / relink it. - In-app project rename should always persist. - Recreating a project on a new path must not reuse the stale DB record. ### Environment - OpenCode Desktop 1.18.14 - macOS arm64 - SQLite storage at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` ### Root cause (from bundled code) - `Project.fromDirectory` does an **exact-match** lookup of the directory (via `projectV2.resolve` + `project_directory`). After a Finder rename the new path has no row, so it silently resolves to the `global` project (`worktree = "/"`, per `node-CU9-BMuP.js` `fromDirectory`). - `ProjectCopy.refresh` only deletes stored directory rows whose paths no longer exist; it never adopts a renamed folder as the same project, so the old `project.worktree` / `project_directory.directory` stay stale. - The edit-project dialog (`edit-project.js`) special-cases the `global` project: for it the save path only calls `sync.project.meta(...)` (silent, no DB `project` row), which is why renames appear to do nothing. Observed DB state after the sequence above: ``` project: cfdc78b7… name=DarkRain worktree=/old/A (deleted) project_directory: cfdc78b7… /old/B (deleted) session for folder C: project_id=global ``` The snapshot (`.local/share/opencode/snapshot/<projectID>`) also keeps a git worktree config pointing at the deleted path. ### Related issues - #38478 (project display name changes ignored in NewLayout) - #35851 (deleting and re-adding a project with a different path reuses stale worktree) - #40336 / #39471 (sessions fail / empty response when saved directory no longer exists) - #35240 (stale `project.worktree` after folder rename) --- ## 中文版描述 ### 问题描述 OpenCode Desktop (v1.18.14, macOS arm64) 中，在 Finder 里直接重命名项目文件夹（OpenCode 之外的操作）会永久破坏"项目 ↔ 目录"的绑定：应用里留下一个幽灵项目，其 `worktree`/`project_directory` 指向已不存在的路径；项目显示名无法修改；新会话会静默回退到 `global` 项目（点击幽灵项目发起会话则直接无响应）。 ### 复现步骤 1. 在 OpenCode Desktop 新建项目（文件夹 `A`），在应用内把项目改名为如 "DarkRain" → 保存。 2. 在 Finder 里把文件夹 `A` 改名为 `B`，然后在应用内改名项目 → **名称不变化**。 3. 在 Finder 里把文件夹 `B` 改名为 `C`。在应用内删除该项目，再新建项目并选择文件夹 `C` → **名称自动变回最初的项目名**，侧边栏仍显示一个指向死路径的幽灵条目。 4. 点击该幽灵项目发起对话 → **无任何输出，不创建会话**。 ### 预期行为 - 在 Finder 中重命名项目文件夹后，应用应能重新关联同一项目（跟随改名），或检测到失效记录并清理/重新关联。 - 应用内修改项目名称应始终生效。 - 在新路径重建项目时，不得复用旧的数据库残留记录。 ### 环境 - OpenCode Desktop 1.18.14 - macOS arm64 - 数据存储：`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`（SQLite） ### 根因分析（来自打包代码） - `Project.fromDirectory` 对目录做**精确匹配**（通过 `projectV2.resolve` + `project_directory`）。Finder 改名后新路径无对应记录，便静默降级到 `global` 项目（`worktree = "/"`，见 `node-CU9-BMuP.js` 的 `fromDirectory`）。 - `ProjectCopy.refresh` 只会删除路径已不存在的目录记录，**从不**把改名后的新目录重新关联为同一项目，导致 `project.worktree` / `project_directory.directory` 一直残留旧路径。 - 编辑项目对话框（`edit-project.js`）对 `global` 项目做了特判：保存时只调用 `sync.project.meta(...)`（静默，不写 `project` 表），这就是改名看起来"没生效"的原因。 上述操作序列后观察到的数据库状态： ``` project: cfdc78b7… name=DarkRain worktree=/old/A (已删除) project_directory: cfdc78b7… /old/B (已删除) 文件夹 C 的会话: project_id=global ``` 快照目录（`.local/share/opencode/snapshot/<projectID>`）中的 git worktree 配置同样指向已删除的路径。

signal.title: fix(app): project rename silently fails for non-git projects (id "global")
signal.text: ### Description Renaming a project via the "Edit Project" dialog silently has no effect when the project's resolved ID is `"global"` (i.e., a plain/non-git folder, or a git repo with no remote, no commits, and no cached ID). The dialog closes but the displayed name never changes. Restarting, re-opening the project, or closing/re-adding the workspace does not help. Root cause: for such projects the app's `save` path (`packages/app/src/components/edit-project.ts`) only performs the real update when `props.project.id` is set and not `"global"`: ```ts if (props.project.id && props.project.id !== "global") { ... await sdk.client.project.update({ projectID: props.project.id, ... }) // real, persisted save return } serverCtx().sync.project.meta(props.project.worktree, { name, ... }) // dead store: never read ``` `Project.resolve` (`packages/core/src/project.ts`) returns `ID.global` for any directory that isn't a git repo, or whose repo has no remote / `.git/opencode` cache / root commit: ```ts if (!repo) return { id: ID.global, ... } return { id: id ?? ID.global, ... } ``` The fallback `sync.project.meta(...)` writes to `childStore.projectMeta` (localStorage), but that store is write-only in the codebase — `enrich()` (`global.tsx` / `layout.tsx`) only ever reads the server's `data.project`. So the rename appears to succeed (dialog closes) but is never persisted or displayed. **Plugins** None (OpenCode Desktop, default plugins). **OpenCode version** 1.18.18 (OpenCode Desktop;) **Steps to reproduce** 1. Create a brand-new empty folder (no git), or run `git init` in a folder but do **not** commit / add a remote. 2. In OpenCode Desktop (old layout) click **+** to add that folder, then open it. 3. Open the project's **Edit Project** dialog and change the default name to something new, then click **Save**. 4. The dialog closes, but the name in the sidebar stays unchanged. 5. Repeat after restarting the app, after re-opening the project, and after closing + re-adding the workspace — the rename still has no effect. 6. (Control) Repeating the same steps on a folder that is a git repo **with at least one commit or a remote** works fine. **Screenshot and/or share link** Will attach if needed. **Operating System** Windows 11 **Terminal** N/A — OpenCode Desktop (Electron app), old layout ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: fix(app): scope manual model override to the selected agent
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #38333 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? In the v2 composer the persisted draft model is checked before the agent's configured model: ```ts const key = [prompt.model.current(), input.agent()?.model, configured(), recent(), fallback()].find(...) ``` Nothing clears it on an agent switch, and `openNewTab` seeds a new draft with the previous tab's model — so the stale value is already in place before the agent is ever consulted. Instead of reordering that list, this tags the persisted selection with the agent it was made under and only honours it while that agent is active. `PromptModel` gains an optional `agent` field; `override()` returns the persisted model only when the tag matches. Untagged values (pre-existing drafts, models inherited from another tab) lose to a configured agent model, but are still used for agents that have no model configured — so the `openNewTab` inheritance stays intact where it is unambiguous. `set` and `variant.set` write the tag, and `variant.selected` reads through `override` so a stale variant can't leak across a switch. Result: new sessions and agent switches land on the agent's model, while a deliberate pick sticks for as long as you stay on that agent. The field is optional and the undefined case is handled explicitly, so no migration is needed. Note on the neighbouring PRs: #38372 fixes this from the agent select callback, which a new tab never fires. #39319 is the same code path from the other side, where the agent model overwriting a manual pick is the bug — scoping rather than reordering is what lets both hold at once. Happy to rework this if you would rather land one of those first. ### How did you verify your code works? Applied the equivalent transformation to the shipped 1.18.13 renderer bundle and ran the desktop app against agents with different configured models. Checked: new session, agent switch, manual pick surviving across turns on the same agent, switching away and back, and variant selection. Not yet exercised as a source build. ### Screenshots / recordings No visual change — the model picker shows a different value. Happy to add a recording if useful. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: tui: auto-assigned "medium" variant crashes sessions for models with empty variants (e.g. mimo-v2.5-free)
signal.text: ## Summary opencode2 (V2) auto-assigns the `medium` variant when creating a session with a reasoning model whose catalog entry has `variants: []` (empty). Runtime then fails with `SessionRunnerModel.VariantUnavailableError` and the session silently falls back to another model. ## Environment - opencode version: 0.0.0-next-17444 (next channel) - OS: Linux 7.0.11-76070011-generic (linux x64) - Terminal: xterm-256color / truecolor - Shell: /bin/bash - Install/channel: next (v2 binary `opencode2`) - Active plugins: @warp-dot-dev/opencode-warp ## Reproduction 1. Open the opencode2 TUI (next channel). 2. Select `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free` from the model picker (`/models`); do not touch any variant setting. 3. Send any prompt. ## Expected Behavior The session runs `mimo-v2.5-free` with variant `default` (the catalog entry defines no variants), and the model responds normally. ## Actual Behavior The created session is pinned to `variant: "medium"` even though the model catalog entry has `variants: []`. The model resolver throws: ``` SessionRunnerModel.VariantUnavailableError: Variant unavailable for opencode/mimo-v2.5-free: medium ``` and the session falls back to `opencode/big-pickle`. ## Root Cause The TUI defaults the variant to `medium` for models with `reasoning: true`, but `mimo-v2.5-free`'s catalog entry has an empty variants list (`variants: []`). The resolver does not tolerate a variant that does not exist and hard-fails instead of falling back to the default. Verified via the HTTP API: creating a session with `variant: "default"` (or omitting the variant) resolves correctly and the model works. Log source: `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` (`Failed to drain Session ... SessionRunnerModel.VariantUnavailableError`). ## Workaround After selecting the model with `/models`, choose the default option in `/variants`, or switch via API: ```sh opencode2 api post /api/session/<sessionID>/model --data '{"model":{"id":"mimo-v2.5-free","providerID":"opencode","variant":"default"}}' ``` ## Additional Context - opencode V1 (1.17.18) works fine with the same model: it does not use the variant mechanism. - The models.dev cache entry for `mimo-v2.5-free` has `reasoning: true` and `reasoning_options: []`. - Related: #40524 (V2 catalog reconciliation), #41868 (variants not selectable for Merge Gateway).

signal.title: Auto-updater breaks global npm install: stub binary + missing shims, hung npm processes left behind
signal.text: ## Bug Report: Auto-updater can permanently break the global install (stub binary + missing shims), and hung `npm install` processes keep running **Environment:** Windows 11 (10.0.26200), node v24.15.0, npm 11.12.1, opencode installed via `npm install -g opencode-ai` ### Summary On every startup, opencode spawns a **background** `npm install -g opencode-ai@<latest>` (the parent process of the npm process is the opencode.exe process itself). When the npm registry is unreachable/flaky (e.g. `ECONNRESET`), this install **hangs for 15+ minutes** and, when it finally progresses, it can leave the global installation in a broken state: 1. npm extracts the new tarball, which **overwrites `bin/opencode.exe` (the currently running binary!) with the 479-byte placeholder stub** that says "Error: opencode-ai's postinstall script was not run." 2. npm removes the old bin shims (`opencode`, `opencode.cmd`, `opencode.ps1`) before creating new ones - the failed install leaves only `.opencode-*` temp files behind. 3. The postinstall then fails with `EBUSY: resource busy or locked` because the still-running opencode processes hold the old binary file (Windows locks running executables) - the install rolls back, but the shims are never recreated and the stub stays in place. ### Result - `opencode` is no longer recognized in new terminal sessions (command not found). - Even invoking the exe directly prints the "postinstall was not run" stub error. - Existing opencode sessions keep working (the old binary stays mapped in memory) - so the breakage is invisible until you open a new terminal. ### Observed evidence - `npm install -g opencode-ai@1.18.18` started at 16:49 and 16:56, parented by `cmd.exe /d /s /c` whose parent was the `opencode.exe` process (auto-update), **still alive/hung ~30 min later**. - npm debug log: `ECONNRESET Invalid response body while trying to fetch https://registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai: aborted`. - After the failed install: `bin/opencode.exe` = 479-byte stub (LastWriteTime = the moment of the breakage), shims missing, `.opencode-UwDeVezx` / `.opencode.cmd-*` / `.opencode.ps1-*` temp files left behind. ### Suggested fixes 1. **Don't replace the binary in place while a process is running from it** - install/verify first, then atomically swap; or refuse to update when an opencode process is still running (on Windows this can never work). 2. **Verify postinstall succeeded before removing old bin links**, and restore the previous state on failure. 3. **Run the updater with a network timeout/retry limit** instead of hanging indefinitely in the background. 4. **Provide a supported way to disable auto-update** (e.g. `autoupdate: false`) - today there is no config option to opt out.

signal.title: Attached images degrade to a bare text placeholder when the model lacks vision — agent has no way to read them
signal.text: ## Summary When a user pastes images into a chat and the active model does not support vision (e.g. a text-only model like `deepseek-v4-flash`), the image `file` parts are replaced by a plain text placeholder before being sent to the model. The agent then has **no way to access the actual image content** — the placeholder carries no reference to how the image can be retrieved. ## Current behavior In `packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts` (around line 213): ```ts if (options?.stripMedia && isMedia(part.mime)) { userMessage.parts.push({ type: "text", text: `[Attached ${part.mime}: ${part.filename ?? "file"}]`, }) } ``` So the model sees only `[Attached image/png: image-2.png]`. There is no session/message/part id, no API reference, no data URL — nothing the agent could use to fetch the image itself. The only way to recover the image is to query the local `opencode.db` (the `part` table stores `{type:"file", mime, filename, url}` with `session_id`/`message_id`) or hit the local serve API, which is undocumented for this purpose and requires guessing the current session. ## Why it matters This forces workarounds: to read a pasted image, an agent (or a skill like an "image recognition" skill) has to: 1. guess the current session (no env var exposes `session_id`), 2. query the sqlite DB / serve API to find the most recent image part, 3. forward the `data:` URL to a separate vision model. That's fragile (parallel sessions race) and entirely non-obvious from the placeholder alone. ## Proposal (any of these would help) 1. **Include a retrievable reference in the placeholder**, e.g. `[Attached image/png: image-2.png] (session: …, message: …, part: …)` or a URL like `opencode://session/{sessionID}/message/{messageID}/part/{partID}` the agent can dereference. 2. **Expose the current session id to agents** (e.g. `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` env var when running tool calls) so tools/skills can scope queries precisely. 3. **A config option** to keep sending lightweight media metadata (mime, filename, session/message/part ids) to text-only models instead of dropping it. ## Environment - opencode version: 1.18.18 (OpenChamber distribution, `opencode serve`) - Model: `deepseek-v4-flash` (no vision) - OS: macOS Happy to help with a PR if a direction is agreed.

signal.title: [FEATURE] Pre/post API call hooks in Provider interface for secret redaction and exfiltration prevention
signal.text: ## Problem When using OpenCode, all code, file contents, command outputs, and user prompts are sent to external LLM API servers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, etc.). This includes secrets, project names, company names, and NDA-protected material. Organizations need the ability to **prevent sensitive data from leaving the machine** — whether to the LLM provider or to attackers via prompt injection — and un-redact AI responses before they reach local tools. ### Current plugin limitations The existing plugin system provides `tool.execute.before` which intercepts tool calls. But this operates at the **tool level**, not the **API level**. There is no way to: - Redact file contents read by tools before they're sent in the API request - Redact user prompts before they reach the LLM provider - Un-redact model responses before tool calls execute - Cover all providers uniformly (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, etc.) ## Proposed Solution Add two hook points in the `Provider` interface, firing before/after the actual API call. ### Where in the code The interception point already exists in `internal/llm/provider/provider.go`: ```go func (p *baseProvider[C]) SendMessages(ctx context.Context, messages []message.Message, tools []tools.BaseTool) (*ProviderResponse, error) { messages = p.cleanMessages(messages) // ← NEW: fire PreApiCall hooks here, allow modifying messages return p.client.send(ctx, messages, tools) // ← NEW: fire PostApiCall hooks here, allow modifying response } func (p *baseProvider[C]) StreamResponse(ctx context.Context, messages []message.Message, tools []tools.BaseTool) <-chan ProviderEvent { messages = p.cleanMessages(messages) // ← NEW: fire PreApiCall hooks here, allow modifying messages return p.client.stream(ctx, messages, tools) // ← NEW: fire PostApiCall hooks on each event, allow modifying content } ``` ### Implementation approach: Go decorator ```go type RedactingProvider struct { inner Provider redactor Redactor // interface with Redact(text) and Unredact(text) } func (r *RedactingProvider) SendMessages(ctx context.Context, messages []message.Message, tools []tools.BaseTool) (*ProviderResponse, error) { redactedMessages := r.redactMessages(messages) response, err := r.inner.SendMessages(ctx, redactedMessages, tools) if err != nil { return nil, err } r.unredactResponse(response) return response, nil } ``` This: - Works with **all providers** (wraps the `Provider` interface) - Requires **minimal code changes** (wrap at creation time) - Is **testable** (mock the `Redactor` interface) - Is **opt-in** (only activates when configured) ### Alternative: Plugin hooks If a Go-level change is not preferred, expose as plugin events: ```typescript api.on("api.request.before", (event) => { return { messages: redactMessages(event.messages) }; }); api.on("api.response.after", (event) => { return { response: unredactResponse(event.response) }; }); ``` ## End-to-end flow ``` 1. User: "Check config.py for the AcmeCorp API key" 2. Agent reads file → gets content with real secret 3. Agent builds messages array with tool_result containing the secret 4. ✨ PreApiCall fires → redacts secret → placeholder token 5. Redacted messages sent to LLM provider — secret never leaves machine 6. LLM responds using placeholder token 7. ✨ PostApiCall fires → un-redacts token → real value 8. Agent processes response with real values 9. Tool calls execute with real content ``` ## Defense against prompt injection exfiltration Beyond protecting data sent to the LLM provider, API-level hooks defend against **prompt injection attacks** that trick the model into exfiltrating secrets via tool calls. Real-world attack vectors (see [gricha/dangerous-skills](https://github.com/gricha/dangerous-skills)): | Attack | Pwn Rate | Vector | |--------|----------|--------| | Trojan helper script | 100% | Payload buried in legitimate bash code | | Memory poisoning | 96% | Persistent backdoor in global config, survives skill removal | | Hook exploitation | 89% | Skill-defined hooks fire shell commands — model never knows | | Test file RCE | 60% | `conftest.py` auto-imported by pytest | | Symlink exfiltration | 54% | "Example" file is symlink to `~/.ssh/id_rsa` | | Supply chain | 36% | npm `postinstall` hook | | Image injection | 30% | Hidden instructions in PNG metadata | With PreApiCall, a redaction tool scans the **entire outgoing request** and blocks secrets before they reach any server. With PostApiCall, suspicious tool calls in the response can be stripped before execution. ## Why this matters - **Enterprise adoption**: Organizations cannot send proprietary code to external APIs without redaction - **GDPR/PII compliance**: Employee names, emails, internal data must be scrubbed - **NDA protection**: Project names, client names, business logic - **Provider-agnostic**: One redaction layer covers all LLM providers - **Zero gaps**: Unlike tool-level hooks, API-level hooks cover everything - **Defense-in-depth**: Catches exfiltration that tool-level hooks miss ## Scope Minimal change — add 2 hook points in `provider.go` or expose via plugin API. The actual redaction logic lives in external tools/plugins. OpenCode just needs to provide the interception point.

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Plugins can't intercept outbound requests for AI-SDK models (http.request hook excludes the AI-SDK path)
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request The runtime hook `ctx.session.hook("http.request", (event) => { … event.request … })` lets a plugin mutate the outbound Web `Request` immediately before provider dispatch. Per the docs, though, it **applies to native models only — AI-SDK-routed models don't pass through it**: > From https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins: > "HTTP hooks can modify requests and responses. They apply to native models; AI SDK models do not currently pass through these hooks. Request and response bodies are one-shot streams." The separate `ctx.aisdk.hook("sdk" | "language", …)` capability covers the AI-SDK seam but exposes only the SDK/model objects, not the outbound HTTP request/body. So for **any provider configured with a custom OpenAI-compatible `baseURL`** (self-hosted proxies, gateways like a LiteLLM/router layer, local model servers) — all of which route through the AI SDK — a plugin currently **cannot inspect or rewrite the outbound request at all**. #### Why it matters This is the same motivation as #19425 ("pre/post API call hooks … for secret redaction and exfiltration prevention"), but for the AI-SDK path that the shipped hook skips: 1. **Security / governance (primary).** Redact secrets from outbound bodies, enforce egress policy, and audit/log exactly what leaves the machine — for self-hosted-proxy and gateway deployments, which are common in orgs that route everything through one controlled endpoint. Today none of this is possible for AI-SDK providers. 2. **Payload shaping.** Normalize or strip fields, inject required headers/tenant tags per `baseURL`, etc. 3. **Request-body compression (concrete, broadly useful).** Large, growing JSON contexts are re-uploaded every turn. Compressing the body + setting `Content-Encoding` is a real, standardized optimization that multiple real targets already accept: - **Google Vertex AI** accepts `Content-Encoding: gzip` on `generateContent` request bodies (working `... | gzip | curl -H "Content-Encoding: gzip"` example: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/discussions/3967). - **Cerebras Inference** documents accepting compressed request bodies on `/v1/chat/completions` (`Content-Encoding: gzip`, msgpack+gzip): https://github.com/Cerebras/inference-examples/blob/main/payload-compression/simple_example.py. - **Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible servers** (vLLM/FastAPI/Uvicorn-based, and proxies) can decode `gzip`/`zstd` request bodies — it's a standard server capability (e.g. FastAPI gzip-request middleware pattern). Being explicit so this doesn't overclaim: **OpenAI does not support request-body compression** (confirmed in that same LiteLLM thread), and Anthropic/Azure/Bedrock don't document it either. The point is not "all providers" — it's that a plugin should be able to compress **where the target accepts it** (Vertex, Cerebras, self-hosted proxies), scoped by `baseURL`, and leave the rest untouched. On a constrained uplink a ~600 KB (≈150K-token) body is tens of seconds of pure upload wait per round-trip; JSON compresses ~5–8×. All three use cases require the one missing capability: a plugin-reachable seam that can rewrite the **outbound request (headers + body)** on the **AI-SDK path**, scoped by target. #### Ask Let plugins intercept/rewrite the outbound request for AI-SDK-routed models — either by extending `http.request`/`http.response` dispatch to cover the AI-SDK path, or by adding an outbound-request seam to `ctx.aisdk.hook` (whichever fits the architecture). The event should expose the request (headers + body, replaceable) and enough `model`/provider/`baseURL` context that a plugin can scope changes to a specific endpoint and leave all other providers untouched. If this is intentionally out of scope, documenting the supported alternative would also close the gap. Happy to test a fix end-to-end against a live `Content-Encoding: zstd`/`gzip`-accepting endpoint. #### Related Narrows #19425 and #2661 (generic pre-provider / body-rewrite hook requests) to the now-actionable gap: the hook shipped, but the AI-SDK dispatch path is excluded.
